units.tr: Argument of chapter 18: The disciples dispute about primacy. Christ explains the question put to him, and extends it: it is not for them to ask who will be greatest in the kingdom of heaven, but how they themselves may enter into it. The proposition, therefore, is this: without true humility and the forgiving of a brother's offences, we cannot hope for eternal life. This argument contains four notable passages. The first is about the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. The second is about the scandal that need not be avoided, at verse 5. The third is about fraternal admonition in offence, verse 15. The fourth is about forgiving the same offence, verse 21.

units.la: Ex GALILÆA Christus orsus est iter suum Hierosolymam versus, ut offerret se illic morti, ubi hora aduenerit. Itineris historiaMat-thaeus per summa capita perstringit, ut constet Christum ubique salutis humanae studiosum, ubique benefactorem sese offerre. Hactenus igitur de profectione per Galilaeam.
units.tr: Christ began his journey from Galilee towards Jerusalem, in order to offer himself there to death, where his hour had come. Matthew touches on the journey only in summary, so that it is clear that Christ everywhere showed himself eager for human salvation and everywhere set himself forth as a benefactor. So far, then, concerning the departure through Galilee.

units.la: Nunc egressus Galilaeam iter continu at pe Iudaeam in qua non minus salutis nostrae studio-sus declaratur; nam & sanat morbidos, & docet rudes, & quærentibus responsa dat. Summa, nullas occasiones ut prosit negligit. Nos igitur quasi viæ comites Dominum nostrum prosequamur cum pia turba, & obseruemus quid ubique & dixerit & fecerit in nostram salutem.
units.tr: Now, having left Galilee, he continues his journey into Judaea, where his zeal for our salvation is no less evident. For he both heals the sick, and teaches the ignorant, and gives answers to those who ask. In short, he neglects no occasion to help. Let us, then, as companions of the road, follow our Lord with the pious crowd, and observe what he says and does everywhere for our salvation.

units.la: Capite xix habentur sermones Christi de vita oeconomica: ut pote de coniugio eiusque diuortio: de liberorum educatione: re familiari siue opibus: pietatis atque salutis remoris. Loci præcipui sunt tres. 1. Soluitur quæstio de diuortio. II. Benedicit Christus pueris sibi oblatis. III. v. 13. Quam difficile sit diuiti regnum cœlorum ingredi, declarat. v. 16.
units.tr: In chapter 19 are found Christ's discourses on domestic life: namely on marriage and its divorce, on the upbringing of children, on property or wealth, and on hindrances to piety and salvation. There are three principal passages. 1. The question about divorce is resolved. 2. Christ blesses the children brought to him. 3. At verse 13, he shows how hard it is for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven, verse 16.

units.la: Caput xx. in quinque partes distingui potest. Nam primo proponit Christus similitudinem de operariis a Patre familias conductis in vineam. Secundo prædicit duodecim discipulis passionem & mortem suam, v. 17. Tertio reiicit petitionem matris filiorum Zebedæi, atque ea occasione discipulos ad humilitatem hortatur vel suo proprio exemplo, v. 20. (Ac sic Dominus Christus iam ex Galilæa promouit Ierechuntem usque, festinans Hierosolymam.) Quarto, egredienti Ierechuntem cæci duo iuxta viam adsunt, qui ab eo, ut petierunt, sanantur, ac in comitatu etiam eius manent. v. 29.
units.tr: Chapter 20 can be divided into five parts. For first, Christ proposes the likeness of the workers hired by the householder for his vineyard. Second, he foretells to the twelve disciples his passion and death, verse 17. Third, he rejects the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee, and on that occasion exhorts the disciples to humility, even by his own example, verse 20. (And so the Lord Christ, already advancing from Galilee, reaches Jericho, hastening towards Jerusalem.) Fourth, as he leaves Jericho, two blind men beside the road meet him; they are healed, as they asked, and remain in his company, verse 29.

units.la: Sequitur tertia pars itineris, de his quæ Hierosolymis & circa contigerunt: Et hinc iam incipit Euangelista narrare illa Domini Iesu facta & dicta, quæ occasionem præbuerunt exequendo ipsius muneri sacerdotali: nempe illa quibus irritati primores Iudæorum, ad supplicium ipsum rapuerunt. quæ quidem narratio continuatur per tria capita, usque ad cap. 24.
units.tr: There follows the third part of the journey, concerning what happened at and around Jerusalem. And here the Evangelist now begins to narrate those deeds and words of the Lord Jesus which gave occasion for carrying out his priestly office, namely those by which the leading men of the Jews, provoked, seized him for punishment. This narrative continues through three chapters, down to chapter 24.

units.la: Ac primùm, caput xxi. narrat potissimùm tria: Primò adventum Iesu regium in urbem regiam Hierosolymam. Secundò, miraculum arefactæ ficus. v. 17. Tertiò, sermones postridie, vel (ut nonnullis videtur) tertio post die habitos in templo inter ipsum & primores Iudæorum.v.27.
units.tr: First, chapter 21 relates chiefly three things. First, the royal arrival of Jesus in the royal city of Jerusalem. Second, the miracle of the withered fig tree, verse 17. Third, the discourses held in the temple on the following day, or (as some think) on the third day after, between him and the leading men of the Jews, verse 27.

units.la: Deinde, capite xxii. pergit Euangelista narrare sermones habitos Hierosolymis inter Christum & primores Iudæorum, paulò ante ipsius passionem. Ac primò recitat parabolam quam Christus eis proposuit de vocatis ad nuptias filij Regis. Secundò, responsionem eius ad quæstionem Pharisæorum: An liceat censum dare Cæsari. v.15. Tertiò, responsionem ad quæstionem Sadducæorum de uxore septem fratrum, cuius ex illis futura sit in resurrectione mortuorum. v.23. Quartò, responsionem ad quæstionem Legisperiti cuiusdam: quodnam sit maximum mandatum in lege. v.34. Quintò, & postremò, quæstionem quam ipse proposuit Pharisæis de Christo; Cuius filius sit.
units.tr: Then, in chapter 22, the Evangelist goes on to relate the discourses held at Jerusalem between Christ and the leading men of the Jews, shortly before his passion. First, he recites the parable he proposed to them about those invited to the wedding of the king's son. Second, his answer to the question of the Pharisees: whether it is lawful to give tribute to Caesar, verse 15. Third, his answer to the Sadducees' question about the wife of the seven brothers, whose she will be in the resurrection of the dead, verse 23. Fourth, his answer to a certain lawyer's question: which is the greatest commandment in the law, verse 34. Fifth and last, the question he himself put to the Pharisees about Christ: whose son he is.

units.la: Caput xxiii. potest distingui in duas partes principales pro diuersitate personarum ad quas Dominus sermonem suum distinctè convertit. I Sermo Christi ad turbam & discipulos: in quo illos monet de cauenda hypocrisi Scribarum & Pharisæorum, ne illi imitentur illorum ambitionem. II Sermone ad ipsos Scribas & Pharisæos conuerso, multiplicem ipsorum hypocrisin incusat, ac nominatim auaritiam, intemperantiam & crudelitatem; eoque nomine illis iudicium Dei tum æternum,tum temporale denunciat.à v.13. ad finem usque capitis.
units.tr: Chapter 23 can be divided into two main parts, according to the different persons to whom the Lord clearly addresses his speech. I. Christ's speech to the crowd and the disciples, in which he warns them to beware of the hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees, so that they do not imitate their ambition. II. Turning his speech to the scribes and Pharisees themselves, he accuses them of their manifold hypocrisy, and especially of their greed, intemperance and cruelty; and on that account he announces to them the judgement of God, both eternal and temporal, from verse 13 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Sequentibus duobus capitibus Euangelista recitat sermones Domini quos habuit ad discipulos privatim paulò ante diem Paschatis, quo ad supplicium raptus fuit: ijque partim ante templum v. 2. capitis vigesimi quarti:partim in monte olearum,v.4. eiusdem capitis,& inde usque ad finem capitis vigesimi quinti.
units.tr: In the two following chapters the Evangelist recounts the Lord's discourses which he gave to the disciples privately, shortly before the day of the Passover on which he was seized for punishment. These were partly spoken before the temple, at verse 2 of chapter 24, and partly on the Mount of Olives, at verse 4 of the same chapter, and from there to the end of chapter 25.

units.la: Caput igitur x x i v. partes habet quatuor: 1 Orationem priorem, quam habuit ante templum, in qua est vaticinium de excidio templi: 11 partem posterioris orationis in monte habitæ, in qua est primo prophetia de calamitatibus Iudæorum,excidium templi atque urbis antecessuris, necnon de excidij atrocitate, à v.4. usque ad v.29. 111 Prophetia de fine mundi, & aduentu Domini ad iudicium, usque ad v.42. 1 v Exhortatio ad vigilantiam, à v.42. deinceps.
units.tr: Chapter 24, then, has four parts. 1. The first discourse, which he gave before the temple, containing the prophecy of the temple's destruction. 2. The second part of the discourse given on the mount, in which first there is a prophecy of the calamities that will come upon the Jews, the destruction of the temple and city, and the atrocity of that destruction, from verse 4 to verse 29. 3. A prophecy of the end of the world and the coming of the Lord to judgement, down to verse 42. 4. An exhortation to watchfulness, from verse 42 onward.

units.la: Cap. x x v. Continuatur exhortatio Domini ad vigilantiam superiore capite instituta: & ad illam adhibentur duæ parabolæ. 1 una de decem virginibus nuptialibus. 11. Altera de talentis quæ herus peregrè abiens commisit suis seruis ad negotiandum.v.14. 111. Additur descriptio extremi iudicij, v.31.
units.tr: Chapter 25. The Lord's exhortation to watchfulness, begun in the previous chapter, continues, and two parables are added to it: (1) the one about the ten virgins at the wedding; (2) the other about the talents, which a master, going abroad, entrusted to his servants to trade with, v.14; (3) a description of the final judgement is added, v.31.

units.la: POSTERIORIS HVIVS PARTIS ministerii Christi prophetici capita hunc in modum in G. F. connectuntur.
units.tr: THE CHAPTERS OF THE PROPHETIC MINISTRY OF CHRIST IN THIS LATTER PART are arranged in this way by G. F.

units.la: Gesta Christi in Galilæa: discipulorum quorundam confirmatio per transfigurationem in monte, cap. 17. ambitiosorum correptio. cap.18. Iudæ[?] Confinibus, vbi refutati[?] Pharisæi. cap. 19. Discipuli.cap.20. Ingressus cap.21. Metropoli: e-ius Commoratio, vbi eius Disputatio cū adversariis cap. 22. Doctrina ad populum.cap.23. Prophetia de destructione templi & fine mundi.cap.24. Hortatio ad vigilandum.cap.25.
units.tr: Christ's deeds in Galilee: the confirmation of certain disciples through the transfiguration on the mountain, chapter 17; the rebuke of the ambitious, chapter 18; the borders of Judea, where the Pharisees were refuted, chapter 19; the disciples, chapter 20; the entry into the metropolis, chapter 21; his stay there, where he disputed with his adversaries, chapter 22; his teaching to the people, chapter 23; the prophecy of the destruction of the temple and the end of the world, chapter 24; the exhortation to watchfulness, chapter 25.

units.la: Hactenus narrata sunt ea, quæ pertinent ad ad-ministrationem muneris Prophetici Christi, quaeque præbuerunt occasionem administrationi muneris Sacerdotalis: quatenus nimirum Scribæ & Pharisæi tum doctrinâ tum miraculis Christi, tum maximè reprehensione suæ hypocriseos irritati fuerunt, ad consilium capiendum de illo ad mortem rapien-do. Deinceps sequitur narratio
units.tr: Hitherto have been related those things which pertain to the exercise of Christ's prophetic office, and which gave occasion for the exercise of his priestly office: namely, in that the scribes and Pharisees were provoked, both by his teaching and by his miracles, and above all by his rebuke of their hypocrisy, to take counsel to seize him and put him to death. Next follows the narrative

units.la: DE ADMINISTRATIONE MV-eris SACERDOTALIS, nempe historia pas-sionis & mortis Christi.
units.tr: On the Priestly Office of Christ the Mediator, namely the history of Christ's passion and death.

units.la: IN HISTORIA Passionis & mortis Christi
units.tr: IN THE HISTORY OF THE PASSION AND DEATH OF CHRIST

units.la: Christi narrantur primum ea quæ passionem proximè antecesserunt, & viam illi strauerunt ab initio capitis vigesimi sexti, usque ad versum 36. eiusdem capitis. Deinde passiones ipsæ, multæ, graues ac variæ, à v. 36. capitis x x v i. usque ad v. 51. capitis vigesimi septimi. Tertiò ea quæ passionem proximè consecuta sunt: inde usque ad illius capitis finem.
units.tr: The narrative of Christ is given in three parts. First, the events that immediately preceded the passion and prepared the way for it, from the beginning of chapter 26 to verse 36 of the same chapter. Then the sufferings themselves, many, grievous and varied, from verse 36 of chapter 26 to verse 51 of chapter 27. Thirdly, the events that immediately followed the passion, from there to the end of that chapter.

units.la: Capitis x x v i. partes duæ sunt: Prima habet Antecedentia passionis dominicæ: secunda partem passionum ipsarum.
units.tr: Chapter 26 has two parts. The first contains the antecedents of the Lord's passion; the second contains the sufferings themselves.

units.la: ANTECEDENTIA passions [?] & præparatoria sunt numero sex:
units.tr: The antecedents and preparations of the passion are six in number:

units.la: 1. Prædictio passionis per Iesum. v. 1. & 2.
units.tr: 1. The prediction of the passion by Jesus, vv. 1 and 2.

units.la: 2. Consultatio procerum, de occidendo Iesu. v. 3. 4. 5.
units.tr: 2. The council of the leaders about killing Jesus, vv. 3, 4 and 5.

units.la: 3. Pactio Iudæ Iscariotis cum proceribus de ipso prodendo, à v. 6. usque ad v. 17.
units.tr: 3. The bargain of Judas Iscariot with the leaders to betray him, from v. 6 to v. 17.

units.la: 4. Indicatio proditoris per Iesum apud discipulos in celebratione paschatis. à v. 17. usque ad 26.
units.tr: 4. The indication of the betrayer by Jesus among the disciples at the celebration of the Passover, from v. 17 to v. 26.

units.la: 5. Doctrina Domini de passionis suæ fructu in institutione S. cœnæ, à v. 26. usque ad v. 30.
units.tr: 5. The Lord's teaching on the fruit of his passion in the institution of the Holy Supper, from v. 26 to v. 30.

units.la: 6. Prædictio comprehensionis sui, fugæ discipulorum & abnegationis Petri, à v. 30. usque ad v. 36.
units.tr: 6. The prediction of his arrest, the flight of the disciples and Peter's denial, from v. 30 to v. 36.

units.la: In his Antecedentibus continentur causæ Passionis & mortis Christi. In primis verò insinuatur causa prima, causas secundas gubernâs, videlicet decretum Dei: quod Christo planè cognitum & perspectum fuisse, argumento est ad monitio Christi ad discipulos, qua mortis suæ circumstantias prænunciat, ut patet ex primo & ultimo Antecedente. Sic etiam singulari Dei gubernatione factum esse significatur, ut Christus occideretur in festo, contra consilium procerum. Sic Deum Patrem comprehensionis & occisionis Christi principalem autorem fuisse, significatur ab ipso Christo, verbis illis Prophetæ Zachariæ; Percutiam pastorem, & dispergentur oues gregis. Quòd causas secundas attinet, sunt illæ tum causæ agentes principales, videlicet proceres Iudæorum: tum causa adiuuans & administra, nempe proditor Iudas: Item causa finalis, in fructu passionis Domini: Denique causæ permittentes, nec impedientes, videlicet Discipuli.
units.tr: In these antecedents the causes of the passion and death of Christ are contained. First of all, the primary cause is hinted at, which governs the secondary causes, namely the decree of God. That this was plainly known and clearly seen by Christ is shown by the warning Christ gave to the disciples, in which he foretells the circumstances of his death, as is evident from the first and last antecedents. So too it is indicated that by a singular governance of God it came about that Christ was put to death at the feast, against the plan of the leaders. Likewise, that God the Father was the principal author of the arrest and killing of Christ is indicated by Christ himself, in the words of the prophet Zechariah: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered." As for the secondary causes, there are, on the one hand, the principal efficient causes, namely the leaders of the Jews; on the other, the helping and serving cause, namely the traitor Judas; likewise the final cause, in the fruit of the Lord's passion; and finally the permitting causes, which did not hinder, namely the disciples.

units.la: Atque hæc de iis quæ Passionem antegressa sunt.
units.tr: These things concerning what went before the Passion.

units.la: PASSIONES ipsæ deinceps exponuntur reliqua parte capitis vigesimi sexti, & toto capite vigesimo septimo. Eaeque commodissimè secundum loca in quibus acciderunt, possunt distingui; Pathemata Christi in Horto: cap. 26. v. 36. Iudicio Ecclesiastico Politico. Loco supplicij. cap. 27.
units.tr: The passion itself is then set out in the rest of chapter 26 and the whole of chapter 27. These can most conveniently be distinguished according to the places in which they occurred: the agonies of Christ in the garden (chapter 26, v. 36); the ecclesiastical and civil judgment; the place of execution (chapter 27).

units.la: Secunda igitur parte capitis xxvi. exponuntur Passiones Christi, primum in Horto, deinde in domo Caiaphæ. Passiones in horto narrantur quinque: 1 Lucta ineffabilis cum horrore irae Dei, & metu mortis instantis eamque comitantium, à v. 37. usque ad v. 40. 11 Securitas & ignauia discipulorum, à v. 40. usque ad 46. 111. Proditio. v. 46. usque ad v. 50. 1 v. Captio seu comprehensio per ministros pontificum. v. 50. ubi & eius causa impediens, præposítera Petri pro Christo digladiatio connotatur. v. 51. & seqq : v. Fuga discipulorum. v. 56.
units.tr: The second part of chapter 26, then, sets out the sufferings of Christ, first in the garden and then in the house of Caiaphas. The sufferings in the garden are narrated as five: (1) the unspeakable struggle with the horror of God's wrath and with the fear of impending death and of the things accompanying it, from v. 37 to v. 40; (2) the security and sloth of the disciples, from v. 40 to v. 46; (3) the betrayal, v. 46 to v. 50; (4) the seizing or arrest by the servants of the high priests, v. 50, where also the hindrance to it is noted, namely Peter's absurd fighting for Christ, v. 51 and following; (5) the flight of the disciples, v. 56.

units.la: Passiones in domo Caiaphæ in quam Christus ducebatur, (v. 57.) sequente ipsum Petro (v. 58.) ad tres classes revocari possunt: quarum prima est eorum quæ passus est à falsis testibus, à v. 59. usque ad v. 62. Secunda eorum quæ passus est à Pontifice Caiapha & concilio, nec non à ministris illorum, usque ad v. 69. Postrema eorum quæ passus est à Petro negante ipsum, inde ad finem usque capitis.
units.tr: The sufferings in the house of Caiaphas, to which Christ was led (v. 57), Peter following him (v. 58), can be reduced to three classes. The first is of what he suffered from false witnesses, from v. 59 to v. 62. The second is of what he suffered from the high priest Caiaphas and the council, and also from their servants, up to v. 69. The last is of what he suffered from Peter denying him, from there to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Capite xxvii. post transitionem perse-ctam (v. 1. 2.) & narrationem pœnitentiæ Iudæ desperantis, (usque ad v. 11.) redit ad passiones Christi: & cùm in postrema parte capitis antecedentis commemorauerit quæ Christus in conciliabulo Ecclesiastico perpessus est; nunc describit primò eius pathemata in iudicio politico coram præside Pilato, partim ante prætorium, partim in prætorio, à v. 11. usque ad v. 32. eaque ad quatuor classes reduci possunt: 1. Ac-cusatio, quòd se voluerit facere Regem Iudæorum, usque ad v. 16. 11. Comparatus cum Barabba latrone, eidem postea ponitur, usque ad v. 22. 111. Ad crucem à turba petitus, à Pilato ad eam damnatur. v. 22. usque ad v. 27. 1v. Flagellatus, illusus & verberatus à militibus abducitur e prætorio ad locum supplicii, usque ad v. 32: quo indicatur, quid ipsi in via illa acciderit.
units.tr: In chapter 27, after the transition (vv. 1 and 2) and the account of the despairing repentance of Judas (up to v. 11), he returns to the sufferings of Christ. Having in the last part of the previous chapter recorded what Christ endured in the ecclesiastical assembly, he now describes first his sufferings in the civil judgment before the governor Pilate, partly before the praetorium and partly within it, from v. 11 to v. 32. These can be reduced to four classes: 1. The accusation, that he claimed to be King of the Jews, up to v. 16. 2. His being set against Barabbas the robber, and afterwards placed beside him, up to v. 22. 3. Being demanded for the cross by the crowd, he is condemned to it by Pilate, v. 22 to v. 27. 4. Scourged, mocked and struck by the soldiers, he is led away from the praetorium to the place of execution, up to v. 32; by which is indicated what happened to him on that road.

units.la: Secundò narrantur pathemata Christi in loco supplicij, usque ad v. 51. Eorum summaria proposi-tio est; Christum ignominiosissima crucis morte fuisse affectum, & sine omni aspectatorum commiseratio-ne. Imo ut doloris maior esset acerbitas, miscue-runt sanas, fel, acetum, &c:
units.tr: Secondly, the sufferings of Christ are narrated in the place of execution, up to v. 51. The summary of them is this: that Christ was afflicted with the most ignominious death of the cross, and without any pity from the onlookers. Indeed, so that the bitterness of his pain might be greater, they mixed for him wine with gall, vinegar, etc.

units.la: Sic fuerunt Passiones Christi, quarum terminus fuit Mors, quam proxime
units.tr: Thus were the sufferings of Christ, whose end was death, which followed very closely.

units.la: SECUTA SUNT
units.tr: WHAT FOLLOWED

units.la: Primò miracula, à v. 51. usque ad 55. v. huius capitis: nimirum I. Aulæum templi fissum. II. Terræ motus. III. Petræ fissæ. IV. Monumenta aperta. V. Quorundam sanctorum surrectio. VI. Centurionis & militum testificatio. Deinde, officia quorundam discipulorum erga defunctum, in quibus potissimum Christi sepultura describitur, à Iosepho ex Arimathæa impetrata & procurata, usque ad v. 62. Tertiò, iniuria inimicorum erga eundem defunctum & sepultum, nimirum quod eum ut impostorem calumniati sunt Sacerdotes & Scribæ apud Pilatum; ac proinde ab illo petierunt milites, ad custodiendum sepulchrum. à v. 62. usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: First, the miracles, from verse 51 to verse 55 of this chapter, namely: (I) the veil of the temple torn in two; (II) the earthquake; (III) the rocks split; (IV) the tombs opened; (V) the rising of certain saints; (VI) the testimony of the centurion and the soldiers. Then, the duties performed by certain disciples toward the dead man, in which chiefly Christ's burial is described, obtained and arranged by Joseph of Arimathea, up to verse 62. Third, the injury done by his enemies to the same dead and buried man, namely that the chief priests and scribes slandered him before Pilate as an impostor; and therefore they asked Pilate for soldiers to guard the sepulchre, from verse 62 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: DE ADMINISTRATIONE muneris Regy.
units.tr: On the Administration of the Kingly Office

units.la: HACTENUS expositum est quomodo Christus in statu humiliationis suæ administrarit munus suum Propheticum & Sacerdotale: illud quidem, prædicando Euangelium, arguendo hypocrisin & scoliodoxiam Scribarum Pharisæorum, suamque doctrinam aduersus illorum contradictionem defendendo, nec non præmonendo discipulos de malis euenturis, tum toti populo Iudaico propter ingratitudinem aduersus gratiosam Dei visitationem per Euangelium, tum ipsis propter confessionem nominis ipsius: hoc vero, offerendo seipsum Patri in cruce pro datis sibi ab illo, id est, pro electis. Deinceps narratur quomodo coeperit administrare munus suum Regium: deuincendo nimirum mortem, per potentem & gloriosam suam Resurrectionem, & ablegando Apostolos in totum terrarum orbem ad prædicandum Euangelium Regni, atque ita ad coll gendum electos in regnum ipsius.
units.tr: So far it has been explained how Christ, in the state of his humiliation, administered his prophetic and priestly office. The prophetic office he administered by preaching the gospel, by exposing the hypocrisy and perverse teaching of the Pharisaic scribes, by defending his doctrine against their opposition, and by forewarning the disciples of the evils to come, both for the whole Jewish people, because of their ingratitude toward God's gracious visitation through the gospel, and for the disciples themselves, because of their confession of his name. The priestly office he administered by offering himself to the Father on the cross for those given to him by the Father, that is, for the elect. Next it is narrated how he began to administer his kingly office: namely by overcoming death through his mighty and glorious resurrection, and by sending the apostles out into the whole world to preach the gospel of the kingdom, and so to gather the elect into his kingdom.

units.la: Quæ autem capite x x v i i i. scribuntur de Resurrectione Domini, eo spectant, ut ostendant, quomodo & per quos illa primum mundo innotuerit. Nec solum piis quales tum erant Apostoli, & paucæ mulieres, sed etiam impiis, quales erant hostes Christi capitales, summi Pontifices & Scribæ. His utrinque innotescit Christi resurrectio, & per testes utrinque fide dignos. Mulieribus Angeli testificantur de Resurrectione Saluatoris, quæ mox idem ad Discipulos Christi perferunt. At Pontificibus alij dantur testes, nunquam enim hi discipulis Christi aut mulierculis erant crediturí. Indigni etiam ut Angelos haberent tantæ rei præcones. Quare audire debent isti à prophanis militibus suis, quòd, & quomodo Christus resurrexerit.
units.tr: What is written in chapter 28 about the resurrection of the Lord aims to show how and through whom it first became known to the world. It became known not only to the pious, such as the apostles then were, and a few women, but also to the impious, such as Christ's chief enemies, the chief priests and scribes. In both cases Christ's resurrection became known, and through witnesses worthy of belief on each side. Angels testify to the women about the resurrection of the Saviour, and the women promptly carry the same news to Christ's disciples. But other witnesses are given to the chief priests, for they were never going to believe the disciples of Christ or silly women. Nor were they worthy to have angels as heralds of so great a matter. Therefore they must hear from their own soldiers, who were profane men, that Christ has risen, and how.

units.la: Diuisa sunt illa in locos quatuor. Primum enim describitur aduentus mulierum ad sepulcrum, & quid tum contigerit : quò pertinet Angeli descen-sus, & eiusdem suauis illa oratio ad ipsas, quòd Christus jam resurrexerit, usque ad v. 8. Deinde quid ipsis abeuntibus in via contigerit, dum in ur-bem festinant ad discipulos : habent obuiam ipsum Christum testem suæ resurrectionis, usque ad v. 11. Tertiò, quomodo eadem res ad Pontifices defera-tur,& quomodo ex eo nuncio sint affecti ;quid item contra sint machinati, usque ad v. 16. Postremò plenius & illustrius exhibet se Christus suis discipu-lis in Galilæa,ubi etiam mandatum videntur accipere docendi puram doctrinam, & administrandi Baptismum.
units.tr: These matters are divided into four sections. First, it describes the women's coming to the sepulchre and what happened then; to this belongs the descent of the angel and his sweet address to them, that Christ has already risen, down to v. 8. Then what happened to them on the way as they left and hurried into the city to the disciples: they meet Christ himself, the witness of his resurrection, down to v. 11. Third, how the same matter is reported to the chief priests, how they were affected by that news, and what they devised in opposition, down to v. 16. Last, Christ shows himself more fully and more clearly to his disciples in Galilee, where they also seem to receive the command to teach pure doctrine and to administer baptism.

units.la: ARGUMENTA CAPITUM EVANGELII SECUNDUM MATTHÆUM, ELEGIACO CARMINE, à D. Rudolpho Gualthero expressa. CAPUT I.
units.tr: ARGUMENTS OF THE CHAPTERS OF THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO MATTHEW, expressed in elegiac verse by D. Rudolph Gualther. CHAPTER I.

units.la: Maiores numerat sancti & primordia Christi, Qui fuit è casta virgine natus homo. Multa timet stupida percussus mente maritus, Angelicis verbis cura recedit iners.
units.tr: He recounts the ancestors and beginnings of Christ, who was born a man of a chaste virgin. The husband, struck in his dazed mind, fears greatly; at the angel's words his idle care departs.

units.la: Fœlici veniunt deducti sydere Persæ, Atque ferunt Regi mystica dona nouo. Infantes pereunt, Aegypti regna subiit CHRISTUS, at in patriam mox tamen inde redit.
units.tr: Led by a happy star, the Persians come and bring mystical gifts to the new King. The infants perish; Christ goes down into the realm of Egypt, but soon returns from there to his homeland.

units.la: Edocet abiectâ Vates respiscere mente, Multorumque sacra corpora tingit aqua. Quæ steriles scindat plantas jam facta securis. Tingitur & CHRISTUS, dat sua signa pater.
units.tr: The prophet teaches repentance with a humbled mind and bathes the holy bodies of many in water. The axe, now made ready, cuts down the barren plants. Christ too is washed, and the Father gives his signs.

units.la: Testiferi CHRISTUS tentatur dæmonis astu. Vincit, & hinc sancto prædicat ore fidem, Discipulósque vocat,quos divina imbuat arte, Et multos morbo liberat inde grauî.
units.tr: Christ the witness is tempted by the devil's cunning. He conquers, and from there with holy mouth proclaims the faith; he calls disciples, whom he imbues with divine art, and frees many from grievous disease.

units.la: 5 Quis verè fœlix, quæ sit pia vita ministri, Quo sensu lex sit percipienda, docet. Ira procul cedat, Veneres, iuratáque[?] verba. Sanctus & in fratrem pectore flagret amor.
units.tr: 5 He teaches who is truly happy, what the pious life of a minister is, and in what sense the law is to be understood. Let anger depart far away, and lust, and sworn words; and holy love burn in the breast toward a brother.

units.la: 6 Quænam sit miseros inopes pia cura iuvandi, Et qua nam deceat mente rogare Deum. Quæque Deo placeant tenuis ieiunia ventris, Non amor abripiat vos quoque cæcus opum.
units.tr: 6 He teaches what the pious care of helping the wretched and needy is, and with what mind one ought to ask of God. And what fasts of a slight belly please God; let not blind love of wealth carry you off too.

units.la: 7 Non damnes alios, proprio te crimine purga, Nec lanient rapidi dogmata sancta canes. Funde preces, patulæ placeant non limina portæ. Doctores falsos cura cauere fiet[?].
units.tr: 7 Do not condemn others; purge yourself of your own crime, nor let the rapid dogs tear the holy doctrines. Pour out prayers; let not the open gates of the wide door please you. Take care to guard against false teachers.

units.la: Non satis audire est, si non pia facta sequuntur. Extructam[?] quassat sæua procella domum.
units.tr: It is not enough to hear if pious deeds do not follow. A savage storm shakes the house that has been built.

units.la: 8 Leprosum mundat, fidei sit regula verae Centurio, Petri languida surgit anus. Sunt sua lustra feris, compescit & æquoris undas. Dæmonis impulsu porcus in alta ruit.
units.tr: 8 He cleanses the leper; the centurion learns the rule of true faith; Peter's feverish old woman rises. The wild beasts have their dens, and he restrains the waves of the sea. At the devil's urging the swine rush into the deep.

units.la: 9 Exurgit validus, fuerat qui membra solutus. Matthæus surgens turpia lucra fugit. Peccantes sanat Dominus, ieiunia tractat. Sanguinis à fluxu fœmina sana redit. Suscitat extinctam, reddit sua lumina cæcis. Dæmonis imperio liberat inde virum.
units.tr: 9 He who was loosed in his limbs rises strong. Matthew, rising, flees shameful gain. The Lord heals sinners and deals with fasting. The woman is restored, healed of her flow of blood. He raises the dead girl and restores sight to the blind. Then by the devil's command he frees a man.

units.la: 10 Discipulos mittit, doceant ut dogmata CHRISTI, Eventus quorum hic officiumque docet. Non ego do pacem, sed tristia prælia surgent. Sed, quem non terrent prælia, salvus erit.
units.tr: 10 He sends out the disciples, that they may teach the doctrines of Christ; here he teaches the outcome and duty of their work. "I came not to bring peace": yet grievous battles will rise. But whoever is not terrified by battles will be saved.

units.la: 11 Laudat Ioannis præstantia munera CHRISTUS. Quàm sit Iudææ gens malesana docet. Devovet ingratas urbes, mysteria parui Percipiunt: omnes sub sua signa vocat.
units.tr: 11 Christ praises the excellent gifts of John. He shows how raging the nation of Judea is. He curses the ungrateful cities; the little ones receive the mysteries; he calls all under his standards.

units.la: 12 Sabbata tractantur „sanatur languida dextra. Insidiasque[?] fugis, CHRISTE supreme, graues. Restituit mentem linguæ illi & luminis usum, Quem nimis immani præserat arte Satan. Pneuma sacrum violant: (moneo) sint verba pudica. Signa negat: fratres indicat inde suos.
units.tr: 12 The sabbath is debated; the withered hand is healed. You flee the grievous snares, supreme Christ. He restores the mind of that man, and the use of his tongue and sight, which Satan had bound with monstrous art. They violate the holy Spirit (I warn): let words be chaste. He refuses signs; thence he names his brothers.

units.la: 13 Comparat heic semen, zizania, retia rara, Fermentum, sinapi: sic sua regna docens. Ponitur & verus thesaurus & inclyta gemma. Doctorem spernit patria dura suum.
units.tr: 13 Here he compares seed, tares, rare nets, leaven and mustard: thus teaching his kingdom. A true treasure and a famous gem is set forth. The hard homeland spurns its own teacher.

units.la: 14 Concidit Herodis Baptista furore peremptus. Panibus exiguis millia multa cibat.
units.tr: 14 Herod's Baptist falls, slain by fury. With a few loaves he feeds many thousands.

units.la: Calcat aquas CHRISTUS, Petrus sed mente vacillat. A variis multos liberat inde malis.
units.tr: Walks on the waters Christ, but Peter wavers in mind. Thence he frees many from various ills.

units.la: 15 Humanae culpat rationis dogmata falsa. Et quae sint, hominem quae violare queant.
units.tr: 15 He condemns the false doctrines of human reason, and what they are that can violate man.

units.la: Voti compos abit Chananaeae gentis alumna. Aegrotos sanat: millia multa cibat.
units.tr: The child of the Canaanite race departs with her wish fulfilled. He heals the sick; he feeds many thousands.

units.la: 16 Signa petunt, prohibet fermentum gentis iniquae. Et CHRISTUM sancto praedicat ore Petrus. Dat claves: mortem praedicit: praemia quae sint Sanctorum, & fidei munera digna docet.
units.tr: 16 They seek signs; the leaven of the faithless nation forbids them. And Christ Peter proclaims with holy mouth. He gives the keys; he foretells death; he teaches what the rewards of the saints are, and the worthy gifts of faith.

units.la: 17 Transformat vultum clara sub imagine CHRISTUS Quem nequeunt alii liberat ille virum. Tristia praedicit mox mortis fata futura. Nummum sub patulo gutture piscis habet.
units.tr: 17 He transforms his face in a bright image, Christ ; he frees the man whom others could not free. He foretells the sad fates of death soon to come. Under the open throat of the fish is a coin.

units.la: 18 Quis maior docet heic, prohibetque offendere parvos. Nam CHRISTUS nostra causa salutis adest. Candona fratri quae in te delicta notavit, Hoc gravis accepti summa remissa docet.
units.tr: 18 Who is greater? He teaches here, and forbids offending the little ones. For Christ is present for the cause of our salvation. Forgive your brother, whose offences against you he has noted; the sum of a grave debt remitted teaches this.

units.la: 19 Coniugii quae sit ratio & quae cura pudoris, Et quae sit pueris gratia danda docet. Quae via sit vitae, quam vix adit omnis abundans Divitiis, & quae praemia danda piis.
units.tr: 19 He teaches the principle of marriage and the care of chastity, and what grace is to be given to children. He teaches what the way of life is, which every rich man scarcely enters, and what rewards are to be given to the pious.

units.la: 20 Agricolas plures conducit, tristia fata Narrat, pro natis mater inepta rogat. Quis vere magnus? reliquis qui rite ministrat. Accepto caeci lumine cuncta vident.
units.tr: 20 He hires several labourers and tells of sad fates; the foolish mother begs for her sons. Who is truly great? He who rightly ministers to the rest. Receiving sight, the blind see everything.

units.la: 21 Ingreditur Solymas cunctanti vectus asella: Expurgat templum: paruula turba canit. Fit sterilis ficus, faciat cur talia quaerunt. Iudaicae gentis pectora dura notat. Occidunt servos Domini, fera fata subibunt. Perdere non audent, quem periisse velint.
units.tr: 21 He enters Jerusalem, riding on a young ass. He cleanses the temple; the little crowd sings. The fig becomes barren; they ask why he does such things. He marks the hard breasts of the Jewish nation. They kill the servants of the Lord and undergo cruel fates. They dare not destroy him whom they wish to have perished.

units.la: 22 Eiicitur thalamis impura veste prophanus, Caesaris & quae sunt reddere rite iubet. Denuo consurgent defuncti: maxima quae sit Lex docet, & David mystica verba canit.
units.tr: 22 The profane man, impure in his garment, is cast out of the wedding chamber; and he bids that what is Caesar's be rightly rendered. The dead will rise again; he teaches what the greatest law is, and David sings mystical words.

units.la: Væ tonat horrendum falsis cultoribus, & quæ Illorum meritis pœna futura fiet, Quod falso fallant supremum corde Tonantem, Et sæuo innocuum ense propheta cadat.
units.tr: Woe thunders dreadfully on the false worshippers, and on what punishment will be due for their deserts, because they falsely deceive the Thunderer supreme in heart, and the innocent prophet falls by the savage sword.

units.la: Tristia quæ immineant Solymis nunc fata recenset, Et quam iudicii sit metuenda dies. Omnibus & quæ nam præcedant signa notanda, Quæ non ignava cernere mente iubet.
units.tr: He now recounts the sad fates that threaten Jerusalem, and how the day of judgement is to be feared. He notes also for all what signs must go before, which he bids us discern with an unslothful mind.

units.la: Janua prudentes admittit aperta puellas, Quæ veniant fatuæ, Janua nulla patet. Dividit hinc servis Dominus numerosa talenta, Judicii quæ sit forma tremenda docet.
units.tr: The open door admits the wise virgins; the foolish ones who come find no door open. Thence the Lord divides his numerous talents among the servants, and teaches the dreadful form of judgement.

units.la: Corsilium captant.unguenta fluentia stillant. Doctorem vendis perfide Juda tuum. Instituit cœnam, precibus patremq; fatigat. Cum capitur, forti dimicat ense Petrus. Pontifices damnat, alapis cum cæditur insons, Hunc Petrus attonito territus ore negat.
units.tr: They plot against him; fragrant ointments drip. Treacherous Judas, you sell your teacher. He institutes the supper and wearies the Father with prayers. When he is taken, Peter fights with a brave sword. The priests condemn him, when the innocent one is struck with blows; Peter, terrified, denies him with astonished face.

units.la: Damnatum cernens laqueo se perdit Judas. Et populus claro Barraban ore vocat. Spinea serta gerit: delusus pendet in alto: Dividit & vestes barbara turba sacras. Multa necem diram comitantur signa sepulcrus Confossum corpus qui tueantur habet.
units.tr: Seeing him condemned, Judas destroys himself with a noose. And the people with clear voice call for Barabbas. He bears a crown of thorns; mocked, he hangs on high. The barbarous crowd divides the sacred garments. Many dire signs accompany the death; the sepulchre holds the pierced body, which guards are set to watch.

units.la: Advenient Mariæ, queis angelus omnia narrat. Contrectat CHRISTI dextra pudica pedes. Militibus nummi, ceu falsi præmia, dantur. Discipulis visus regna suprema petit.
units.tr: Mary's women come, to whom the angel tells everything. Christ's chaste right hand touches the feet. Money is given to the soldiers as the reward of a falsehood. He seeks the supreme kingdom, appearing to the disciples.

units.la: VERSUS MEMORIALES EX GEMMA FABRI, ORDINE ALPHABETICO ITA CONTEXTI, UT SINGULIS distichis singulorum capitum argumentum indicetur.
units.tr: MEMORIAL VERSES FROM FABER'S GEM, ARRANGED IN ALPHABETICAL ORDER, SO THAT THE ARGUMENT OF EACH CHAPTER IS INDICATED BY A PAIR OF DISTICHS FOR EACH.

units.la: CAPUT I.
units.tr: CHAPTER I.

units.la: Aprisci oritur CHRISTUS. turbatur Iosph. Angelus hunc retinet. virgo beata parit.
units.tr: Christ rises in Aprisci. Joseph is troubled. The angel restrains him. The blessed virgin bears a child.

units.la: Barbara gens quærit trepidat rex. Memphis aditur: Casi nessentur[?], sponsus adire timet[?]. 3Clamat Iohannes, taxat.se deiicit ipsum: Abluit. aduolitat Pneuma Paterque sonat. 4Dæmone ter vitio. lux magna est orta. vocantur. Bis duo. morborum pellitur omne genus. 5En tibi fœlices. sal. lux. impletio legis. Ne occidas, iures, dilige more patrum. 6Facita. des, ores. ieiunes atque recondas. Sit lux pura. duplex ne sit herus, vide anes[?]. 7Grandis trabs. petito. lata est via. Pseudo prophetas Vita, nescio vos. firma, unensque[?] domus 8Instat lepra. socrus. miles. fouea. tumulator. Somnus. turba maris. porcus in amne perit. 9Lectifer atque Leui. sponsus. diruptio. primas. Profluuium. cæci. mutus. & alba seges 10Missi quid faciunt. fugitatque ferantque, monentur. Viuit confessor, pax perit. vnda iuuat. 11Nuncius ecce duplex. vatis laus, improbat urbes. Parulus hæc nouit. recreo. tolle iugum. 12Obiicitur Dauid spicis. manus arida. regnum. Diuisum. quærunt signa. forisque tui. 13Proiectum semen. zizania. grana sinapis. Fermentum. gaza. gemma. sagena. stupor. 14Quæ mors Baptistæ. pisces duo. per mare Christus It. stupor hinc. multos fimbria tacta iuuat. 15Respondet scribis. ex corde malum. Cananæa. Mox septem panes bis quo mille replent. 16Signa petunt. fermenta vetat. Confessio Petri. Probra crucis. temet spernito. reddet opus. 17Transformat sese? non cedit luna ministris. Ingens vis fidei. drachma soluta duplex. 18Vis fieri magnus? sis infans. scandala tolle. Errat omis. fratrem corripe. mitis herus 19An licet uxorem? Eunuchi. adducuntque puellos. Anne bonus? vendas. multiplicata dabit. 20Bacchi cultores. duplici cum pignore mater. Baptismus. lites. bis Miserere sonat. 21Concisi rami. vendentes, arida ficus. Curat vter patrem? vina locata. lapis. 22De nupta regis, censu, septemque maritis De magno iussu, deque parente Dei.
units.tr: The barbarian people seek him; the king trembles. They go to Memphis: Casi are slain[?]; the bridegroom fears to approach[?]. 3John cries out and rebukes; he casts himself down and washes. The Spirit flies down and the Father sounds forth. Three times the demon is cast out by the vice. A great light has arisen; they are called. Twice two. Every kind of disease is driven out. 5Behold, happy ones for you: salt, light, the fulfilling of the law. Do not kill, do not swear; love as the fathers taught. 6Do, give, pray, fast, and hide away. Let the light be pure; let there not be a double master; see[?]. 7A great beam; seek; the way is broad. Vita, Pseudo-prophets, I know you not; the house stands firm and is one. 8Leprosy threatens; the mother-in-law, the soldier, the pit, the undertaker, sleep, the storm of the sea; the swine perish in the river. 9The bier-bearer and Levi; the bridegroom; the breach; the first; a flux; the blind man; the mute man; and the white harvest. 10The sent ones do what they do; they flee and carry, they are warned. The confessor lives; peace perishes; the wave helps. 11Behold the double messenger; praise of the prophet; he condemns cities. The little one knows these things; I refresh; take up the yoke. 12David is objected to on account of the ears of grain; the withered hand; the kingdom divided; they seek a sign; and your outside.

units.la: 23 En cathedram Mosis. repetitum. væ tibi Scriba. Efficienda alii, quæ fugis, ipse doces.
units.tr: 23 Behold the seat of Moses. Repeated: woe to you, scribe. What you flee, you yourself teach others to do.

units.la: 24 Forma cadit templi, seductio. bella. tenebræ. Ficus. prima ratis. fur. famulusque vigil.
units.tr: 24 The form of the temple falls; seduction; wars; darkness. The fig tree; the first ship; the thief; and the servant who watches.

units.la: 25 Gaudent prudentes. poscuntur lucra talenti. Gloria iudicii, totaque forma patet.
units.tr: 25 The wise rejoice. The gains of the talent are demanded. The glory of judgment, and the whole form is revealed.

units.la: 26 Infusum unguentum. fit pascha. rogat. Cadit auris. Insimulant testes. scommata. Petre negas.
units.tr: 26 The ointment is poured out. The passover is made. He asks. The ear falls. They accuse by witnesses. Scoffings. Peter, you deny.

units.la: 27 Luctus. fur. sors. nox. probra. signa. stuporque Tribunus. Largitum corpus. milite cincta petra.
units.tr: 27 Mourning; the thief; the lot; the night; reproaches; signs; and the amazement. The tribune. The body given away. The rock sealed with a soldier.

units.la: 28 Mira vident Mariæ, quas ut confessit Iesus Milite corrupto. monstrat agenda suis.
units.tr: 28 They see the wonders of Mary, which Jesus confessed as he showed his followers what they must do, the soldier having been bribed.

units.la: VERSUS HEXAMETRI, QUIBUS SINGULIS QUINA CAPITA quàm brevissimè comprehen-duntur.
units.tr: HEXAMETER VERSES, IN WHICH FIVE CHAPTERS EACH ARE COMPRESSED AS BRIEFLY AS POSSIBLE.

units.la: {1}Ortus, {2}Adoratur, {3}Lotus, {4}Tentatque, {5}Docetque, {6}Orantes, {7}post Dogmata, {8}Sus, {9}Vocatio, {10}Lectli, {11}Missi, {12}per Sata, {13}post Ænigma, {14}Caputque, {15}Catelli, {16}Claues, {17}& Iubar, {18}Infans, {19}Vnio, {20}Denariorum, {21}Tum Hosiāna, {22}Numismnaq̃, {23}Pullos, {24}Signaq̃, {25}Lapas, {26}Iudas, {27}& Spinis, {28}mox Rediuiuus adest.
units.tr: {1} Birth, {2} Worship, {3} Washing, {4} Temptation, {5} Teaching, {6} Those praying, {7} After the doctrines, {8} The swine, {9} Calling, {10} The bier, {11} The sent ones, {12} Through the grainfields, {13} After the riddle, {14} And the head, {15} The little dogs, {16} Keys, {17} And the radiance, {18} The child, {19} Union, {20} Of the denarii, {21} Then Hosanna, {22} And the coin too, {23} The chicks, {24} And the sign, {25} The lamp, {26} Judas, {27} And with thorns, {28} soon the Risen One is present.

units.la: Declaratio vocum ex singulis capitibus memoralium.
units.tr: Explanation of the words from the memorial verses for each chapter.

units.la: Ortus Christi ex semine Dauidis & Abrahami. tatur Christus à Magis. v 11. Lotus in S. Baptismate à Iohanne v. 16. Tentatque diabolus Christum v. 1. &c. Docetque Christus in monte. v. 2. Orantes quid deceat. v. 7. post Dogmata varia, Sus ruit in mare. v. 32. Vocatio Matthæi. v. 9. Lecti duodecim discipuli. v. 1. Missi ab Iohanne discipuli ad Iesum. v. 2. per Sata euntes discipuli vellunt spicas, v. 1. post Ænigma varium. Caputque Iohannis Baptistæ in patina v. 10 Catelli colligentes micas sub mensa. v. 27. Claues Petro promittuntur, v. 19 Iubar faciei Christi vt sol. v. 2. Infans à Iesu aduocatus. v. 2. Vnio vxoris & mariti in carnem vnam. v. 5. Denariorum merces pro opere. v. 2. 9. Tum Hosianna acclamant Christo. v. 9. Numismaque cum imagine Cæsaris. v. 19. Pulli congregati sub ala Gallinæ. v. 37. Sinaque extremi iudicij Lampas virginum prudentum. v. 1. Iudas proditor osculatur Christum. v. 49. & Spinis coronatur Christus. v. 29. mox Redivivus adest Christus é sepulchro. v. 6.
units.tr: The birth of Christ from the seed of David and Abraham. Christ is worshipped by the Magi, v. 11. Washed in holy baptism by John, v. 16. The devil tempts Christ, v. 1, etc. Christ teaches on the mountain, v. 2. The prayers: what is becoming, v. 7. After various doctrines, the swine rush into the sea, v. 32. The calling of Matthew, v. 9. The bier: the twelve disciples, v. 1. The disciples sent by John to Jesus, v. 2. The disciples going through the grainfields pluck ears, v. 1. After the varied riddle. The head of John the Baptist on a dish, v. 10. The little dogs gathering crumbs under the table, v. 27. The keys are promised to Peter, v. 19. The radiance of Christ's face as the sun, v. 2. The child called to Jesus, v. 2. The union of wife and husband into one flesh, v. 5. The wage of the denarii for the work, v. 2, 9. Then they cry Hosanna to Christ, v. 9. The coin with the image of Caesar, v. 19. The chicks gathered under the hen's wing, v. 37. The sign of the Last Judgment; the lamp of the wise virgins, v. 1. Judas the betrayer kisses Christ, v. 49. And Christ is crowned with thorns, v. 29. Soon the Risen Christ is present, out of the sepulchre, v. 6.

units.la: ANALYSIS SVMMARIA EVANGELII DOMINI NOSTRI IESU CHRISTI SECUNDUM MARCUM.
units.tr: ANALYSIS SUMMARY OF THE GOSPEL OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST ACCORDING TO MARK.

units.la: INPRÆSENTIS Euangelistæ ingressu primò occurrit nobis Epigraphe i. inscriptio seu titulus, magna ex parte in Matthæi prolegomenis iam explicatus: Secundò ipsa succedit Tradatio, hoc est, Historia Euangelica, à beatissimo Euangelista Marco, singulari Spiritus diuini instinctu, hisce literis, ceu publicis tabulis mandata, ad euidentem vniuersæ posteritatis electæ vtilitatem.
units.tr: At the start of this Gospel we first meet the Epigraphe, that is, the inscription or title, which was largely explained already in the prolegomena to Matthew. Second comes the narrative itself, that is, the Gospel history, which the most blessed evangelist Mark, moved by a singular instinct of the divine Spirit, committed to writing in these letters, as to public records, for the clear benefit of the whole elect posterity.

units.la: DE INSCRIPTIONE.
units.tr: ON THE INSCRIPTION.

units.la: Inscriptio complectitur i. Materiam, seu ὕλην, ὑποκείμενον. [illegible, ~12 letters] quae est Euangelium, seu historia Euangelica. 2. Scriptorem seu personam scribentis, quae fuit Marcus de quo vide B. Aretium in prolegomenis in Euangelium Marci.
units.tr: The inscription contains: 1. the matter, or hyle, the subject, [illegible, ~12 letters], which is the Gospel, or the Gospel history; 2. the writer, or the person of the one writing, who was Mark, on whom see B. Aretius in his prolegomena to the Gospel of Mark.

units.la: Historiam Euangelicam describendi occasio priuata seu peculiaris Marco oblata fuit à fratribus Italicis & his quae Romae erant, quorum rogatu hunc libellum conscripsit. Rationes vero scribendi plures alias eum habuisse certum est: vt nimirum posteritas, fidei Christianae certam haberet historiam ex doctrina ipsius Christi. Et quia non Apostolus, sed sectator tantum Apostolorum fuit Marcus, sicuti & Lucas, obseruatione dignum est, nihil interesse ad percipiendum & praedicandum Euangelium, vtrum illi annuncient, qui eundem Dominum hic in carne apparentem, discipulatu famulante secuti sunt, an ij qui ex illis fideliter comperta tradiderunt.
units.tr: The private or particular occasion for describing the Gospel history was given to Mark by the Italian brothers and those who were at Rome, at whose request he wrote this little book. It is certain, however, that he had several other reasons for writing: namely, that posterity might have a sure history of the Christian faith drawn from the teaching of Christ himself. And since Mark was not an apostle but only a follower of the apostles, as Luke also was, it is worth observing that it makes no difference to the perceiving and preaching of the Gospel whether those announce it who followed the same Lord, present here in the flesh, as servants in discipleship, or those who faithfully handed down what had been learned from them.

units.la: Propositio & scopus est: Messiae vitam in his terris actam describere, mortem, resurrectionem & ascensum in coelos, vbi pro redemptis suis fidelibus manet intercessor vsque ad diem iudicij.
units.tr: The proposition and aim is: to describe the life of the Messiah lived on this earth, his death, resurrection and ascension into heaven, where he remains as intercessor for his redeemed faithful until the day of judgment.

units.la: Potest hoc propositum isto syllogismo comprehendi:
units.tr: This proposition can be summed up in the following syllogism:

units.la: Is in quo euenerunt ea quae in Christo euentura praedixerunt prophetae, est Christus.
units.tr: That in which the things foretold by the prophets about Christ have come to pass is Christ.

units.la: Atqui Iesus hic Nazarenus, est is in quo illa euenerunt.
units.tr: But this Jesus of Nazareth is the one in whom those things have come to pass.

units.la: Ergo hic est Iesus Christus.
units.tr: Therefore this is Jesus Christ.

units.la: Huius syllogismi propositio confirmatur testimoniis prophetarum, quae passim in hac historia allegantur. Assumtio vero confirmatur testimonio huius narrationis: quæ fidem mere-tur apud omnes bonos: cum Marco,(vt hiftori-ci Ecclesiastici tradunt) dictata fit ab Apostolo Petro, qui horum fere omnium oculatus testis fuit,& quæ ipse non vidit, ab ipso Domino co-gnouit. Hinc Euangelių hoc Petri multi esse iu-dicant. Marci tame est vt scriptoris & doctoris, qui indiuiduus & fidelis comes Apostoli Petri fuit. Quod ex his verbis Petri colligi potest: Salutat vos Ecclesia, quæ est in Babilone collecta & Marcus Filius Meus, Pet. 5.v.13. Vocauit autem Marcum, filium suum: sicut Paulus Timotheum vocat filium, quem in Sacris literis Apostolus diligentissime instituerat.
units.tr: The major premise of this syllogism is confirmed by the testimonies of the prophets, which are cited throughout this history. The minor premise is confirmed by the testimony of this narrative, which deserves belief among all good people: since, as the ecclesiastical historians hand down, it was dictated to Mark by the apostle Peter, who was an eyewitness of almost all these things, and what he did not see he learned from the Lord himself. Hence many judge this Gospel to be Peter's. Yet it is Mark's, as writer and teacher, who was the constant and faithful companion of the apostle Peter. This can be gathered from these words of Peter: "The Church that is in Babylon, chosen together with you, salutes you, and so does Mark my son" (1 Pet. 5.13). He called Mark his son, just as Paul calls Timothy a son, whom the apostle had most diligently instructed in the Sacred Letters.

units.la: Marci proprium studium erat, vt historiam ita breui compendio contraheret, vt tamen aliorum dicta magno orationis lumine, admirabili ratione illustraret, neq; epitomen fecit Euangelij à Matthæo scripti, sicut Hieronymus putauit: quia abinitio tractandi ratione est dissimilis: in progressu alium ordinem sequitur, partim res verius tractando, partim nouas inferendo. Guilh: Perkinsus.
units.tr: Mark's own method was to condense the history into so brief a summary, yet to illuminate the sayings of others with great brilliance of expression and admirable skill. He did not make an epitome of the Gospel written by Matthew, as Jerome thought, because from the beginning his manner of treatment is different; in its progress he follows another order, partly by treating the matters more fully, partly by introducing new material. Guilielmus Perkinsus.

units.la: PARTES principales
units.tr: THE principal PARTS

units.la: Huius historiæ sunt tres.
units.tr: This history has three parts.

units.la: Prima est de administratione muneris Pro-phetici, quod amnistrauit prædicando Euange-lium, explicaado legem Dei, arguendo peccata & falsa dogmata Iudæorum: prophetando de cladibus populo Iudaico euenturis, nec non de suo aduentu ad iudicium: cui tamen narrationi admixta sunt opera regia, videlicet vocatio dif-cipucipulorum & legatio eorundem in Iudæam ad prædicandum Euangelium, demonstratio mi-raculorum, ingressus regius in urbem, & deni-que repurgatio templi. Quæ pars continetur tredecim primis capitibus.
units.tr: The first concerns the exercise of the prophetic office, which he carried out by preaching the Gospel, expounding the law of God, refuting the sins and false teachings of the Jews, prophesying the calamities that would befall the Jewish people, and also his coming to judgment. Mixed into this narrative are royal acts, namely the calling of the disciples and their mission into Judea to preach the Gospel, the demonstration of miracles, the royal entry into the city, and finally the cleansing of the temple. This part is contained in the first thirteen chapters.

units.la: Secunda pars est de ad ministratione Sacer-dotij, quod administravit patiendo pro nostris peccatis ac moriendo: quæ historia capite decimo quarto & decimo quinto continetur.
units.tr: The second part concerns the exercise of the priestly office, which he carried out by suffering for our sins and dying. This history is contained in chapters fourteen and fifteen.

units.la: Tertia pars est de inchoatione regni gloriosi per resurrectionem à mortuis, legationem Apostolorum in vniuersum orbem terrarum ad prædicandum Euangelium & Baptizandum Euangelio credentes & denique per ascen-sionem incœlum & sessionem ad dextram Dei : capite vltimo[?].
units.tr: The third part concerns the beginning of the glorious kingdom through the resurrection from the dead; the sending of the apostles into the whole world to preach the Gospel and to baptize those who believe the Gospel; and finally the ascension into heaven and the sitting at the right hand of God, in the last chapter.

units.la: PRIMÆ PARTIS DE ADMINI-stratione muneris prophetici synopsis generalis.
units.tr: THE GENERAL SYNOPSIS OF THE FIRST PART, ON THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PROPHETIC OFFICE.

units.la: Commemoratur hic præparatio Christi ad munus propheticum per Iohannis Baptistæ ministerium cap. 1. usque ad vers: 9. Christi Baptismum & in augurationem. v. 9.10.11. Tentationem in deserto. vers: 12.13. Administratio muneris prophetici cuius partes duæ 1. Ante postremam Christi profectionem Hierosolymam sine mortis mentione: ministerio prædicandi functus est Christus Solus: cap. 1. v. 14. & cap. 2. & cap. 3. usque ad vers: 13. Adscitis collegis discipulis. cap. 3. v. 13. usque ad capitis octavi vers: 13.
units.tr: Here we are reminded of Christ's preparation for the prophetic office through the ministry of John the Baptist, chapter 1 to verse 9; of Christ's baptism and inauguration, verses 9–11; and of his temptation in the wilderness, verses 12–13. The administration of the prophetic office has two parts. (1) Before Christ's final journey to Jerusalem, with no mention of death, Christ alone discharged the ministry of preaching: chapter 1 verse 14, chapter 2, and chapter 3 to verse 13. (2) After he had taken the disciples as colleagues, chapter 3 verse 13 to chapter 8 verse 13.

units.la: 2. In postremam illa profectione Hierosolymam ad mortem oppetendam: Quid dixerit & fecerit Christus Ante ingressum eius in urbem Hierosolymam mortis Christi Vaticinium primum. cap. 8. v. 13. Remedium oppositum offendiculo, in Transfiguratione: & secunda mortis prædictio. cap. 9. Tertium vaticinium cum antegressis & consecutis. c. 10. Sub ipsum ingressum: quæ eo die & sequentibus duobus diebus gestaque cap. 11. Post ingressum Sermones Christi contra adversarios cap. 12. ad discipulos cap. 13.
units.tr: (2) On that final journey to Jerusalem, to meet death, we have what Christ said and did. Before his entry into the city of Jerusalem, there is the first prophecy of Christ's death, chapter 8 verse 13; the remedy against the stumbling block, in the Transfiguration, and the second prediction of death, chapter 9; the third prophecy with what came before and after it, chapter 10. At the very entry, what was done that day and the following two days, chapter 11. After the entry, Christ's sermons against his adversaries, chapter 12, and to the disciples, chapter 13.

units.la: Capite igitur primò, post narrationem praeparationis Christi, exponit ea quae Christus publicè docuerit & fecerit, vbi primo occurrit prima Christi concio, & vocatio quatuor discipulorum. v. 14.11 (Concio Christi Capernaumi in synagoga habita, & eiectione daemonij confirmata. v. 21. 111. Miraculum sanatae socrus Petri, & multorum aliorum simul sanatorum. v.29. 1v. Praedicatio Christi in contiguis oppidulis, & miraculū purgati leprosi. v.35.
units.tr: Chapter 1, therefore, after narrating Christ's preparation, sets out what Christ taught and did publicly. Here first occurs Christ's first sermon and the calling of four disciples, v. 14–20. (Christ's sermon in the synagogue at Capernaum, confirmed by the casting out of a demon, v. 21–28. The miracle of Peter's mother-in-law healed, and of many others healed at the same time, v. 29–34. The preaching of Christ in the neighbouring towns, and the miracle of the cleansed leper, v. 35–45.)

units.la: Capite secundo describit Marcus quando Christus reuersus sit in Capernaum, & quae illic ediderit miracula. Propositio est, Christum & corporum & animorum verum esse medicum, contra opinionem Scribarum & Pharisaeorum. Partes capitis sunt quatuor. 1. de sanatione cuiusdam paralytici in urbe Capernaum. 11. de vocatione Leuis qui alias Matthaeus. v 13. 111. de defensione sui & discipulorum contra criminationem discipulorum Iohannis propter omissionem ieiunij. v.18. 1v. de defensione discipulorum contra criminationem Pharisaeorum, propter euulsas in sabbatho spicas. v. 23.
units.tr: Chapter 2 describes when Christ returned to Capernaum and what miracles he performed there. The proposition is that Christ is the true physician of both bodies and souls, against the opinion of the scribes and Pharisees. The parts of the chapter are four: (1) the healing of a paralytic in the city of Capernaum; (2) the calling of Levi, otherwise Matthew, v. 13; (3) his defence of himself and his disciples against the accusation of John's disciples over the omission of fasting, v. 18; (4) his defence of the disciples against the accusation of the Pharisees over the ears of corn plucked on the sabbath, v. 23.

units.la: Capite tertio narratur primò miraculum de arida manu restituta in synagoga Capernaumi, & quis huius miraculi fuerit fructus. Secundò, quos & quot designauerit Iesus Apostolos. (Nam Christus hactenus solus docuerat: nunc collegas sibi adinnxit: Vide Matth: 10. v. 13.) Tertiò, quae fuerint suorum, ac Scribarum de se iudicia, vbi & defensio Christi contra criminationem Scribarum, dicentium eum eiicere daemonia per Beelzebub. v.21. Quartò veri Christi amici qui sint. v. 31.
units.tr: Chapter 3 relates, first, the miracle of the withered hand restored in the synagogue at Capernaum, and what fruit this miracle bore. Second, whom and how many Jesus appointed as apostles (for Christ had hitherto taught alone; now he joined colleagues to himself; see Matth. 10. v. 13). Third, what the judgments of his own people and of the scribes were concerning him, and the defence of Christ against the accusation of the scribes, who said that he cast out demons by Beelzebub, v. 21. Fourth, who are the true friends of Christ, v. 31.

units.la: CHRISTVS hactenus negotium salutis
units.tr: Christ has hitherto set forth the matter of salvation

units.la: aperto genere orationis proposuit. Nunc do- cet quidem, sed vt discipulis fit neceffum priua- tim illum conuenire,& doctrinæ ipsius sensum interrogare. Eiusmodi parabolicos sermones aliquot describit Marcus capite quarto, cuius partes sunt quinque 1. Proponit Dominus turba parabolam de femine inter seminandum quadrifa- riam cadente,eamque discipulis priuatim explicat, iisque ampliorem Euangelij in mundo patefactio- nem promittit. 11 Monet discipulos vt sibi caueant tum ab ignauia inuidiaue in cælesti doctrina aliis communicanda, tum ab ignauia incuriaue in ea- dem meditanda atque custodienda. v. 24. & 25. Tertiò, proponit parabolam de occulto feminis la- tèli incremento: & de incremento inopinato grani sinapis, v. 26. & feqq: Quartò sedat tempestatem maris. v. 35.
units.tr: in an open manner of speaking. Now he teaches indeed, but in such a way that it is necessary for the disciples to meet him privately and ask the sense of his teaching. Mark describes several such parabolic sermons in chapter 4, whose parts are: (1) The Lord proposes to the crowd the parable of the seed falling in four ways as it is sown, and explains it privately to the disciples, promising them a fuller revelation of the gospel in the world. (2) He warns the disciples to be on their guard, both against sloth and envy in communicating the heavenly teaching to others, and against sloth and carelessness in meditating on and keeping the same, v. 24–25. (3) He proposes the parable of the hidden growth of the seed, and of the unexpected growth of the grain of mustard, v. 26ff. (4) He calms the storm at sea, v. 35.

units.la: Capite quinto trium insignium miraculo- rum historia habetur. Primùm est ejectio le- gionis dæmoniorum,quæ impetrata venia porcos bis mille præcipitant in mare. Secundùm Excitatio filiæ Iairi v. 21. & feqq: 3. 111 Sanatio mulieris la- borantis fluxione sanguinis , quæ narratio inferta est historiæ excitationis puellæ: incipiens v. 25. de- finens v. 34.
units.tr: Chapter 5 contains the history of three notable miracles. First, the casting out of the legion of demons, who, having obtained leave, rush into the sea, two thousand swine. Second, the raising of Jairus's daughter, v. 21ff. Third, the healing of a woman suffering from a flow of blood, a narrative inserted into the history of the raising of the girl, beginning at v. 25 and ending at v. 34.

units.la: Capitis sexti membra sunt sex 1. Christus do- cet Nazarethæ. 11 Mittit Apostolos binos & bi- nos in terram Israël ad prædicandum Euangelium. v. 7. 111 Iudicium Herodis de Christo, & decolla- tio Iohannis Baptifte,v. 14. 1 v Christus cum Apo- stolis quærit quietem in deferto: sed præoccupatus à populo,docet eos & cibat miraculosè.v. 30. v. Pre- catus in monte ambulat super mare: & discipulis diffidifficulter nauigantibus opem fert. v. 45. VI Sanat ægrotos variis ex locis allatos. v. 54.
units.tr: The chapter 6 has six parts: (1) Christ teaches at Nazareth. (2) He sends out the apostles two by two into the land of Israel to preach the gospel, v. 7. (3) Herod's judgment about Christ, and the beheading of John the Baptist, v. 14. (4) Christ, with the apostles, seeks rest in the wilderness, but is anticipated by the people; he teaches them and feeds them miraculously, v. 30. (5) Having prayed, he walks on the sea over the water, and brings help to the disciples who are struggling at the oars, v. 45. (6) He heals the sick brought from various places, v. 54.

units.la: Capitis septimi partes sunt tres, prout tria narrantur de Christo. I Disputat cum Pharisæis & Scribis de cultu Dei, contra traditiones. II Eiicit dæmonium ex filia mulieris Chananæa[?], v. 24. III Sanat surdum quendam impeditæ linguæ. v. 31.
units.tr: The parts of chapter 7 are three, as three things are related of Christ: (1) He disputes with the Pharisees and scribes about the worship of God, against the traditions. (2) He casts a demon out of the daughter of a Canaanite woman, v. 24. (3) He heals a certain deaf man with an impediment of speech, v. 31.

units.la: Cap. octaui partes sunt quinque. I. Christus miraculose cibat turbam. II Recusat signum dare Pharisæis. v. 10. III Monet discipulos, de cauendo fermento Pharisæorum & Herodis. v. 14. IV Sanat quendam cæcum. v. 22. V. Testatur se esse Christum: item passurum & resurrecturum: inde hortatur discipulos ad patientia persecutionis propter confessionem Euangelij. v. 27. & seq.
units.tr: Chapter 8 has five parts: (1) Christ miraculously feeds the crowd. (2) He refuses to give a sign to the Pharisees, v. 10. (3) He warns the disciples to beware the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod, v. 14. (4) He heals a certain blind man, v. 22. (5) He testifies that he is Christ; likewise that he will suffer and rise again; and thence he exhorts the disciples to patience in persecution on account of their confession of the gospel, v. 27ff.

units.la: Hic igitur est secunda Administrationis officij prophetici pars: nimirum quid fecerit & dixerit Christus in postrema illa profectione Hierosolymam instituta ad oppetendam mortem, quam ter discipulis prædicit, & eos contra offendiculum crucis munit: Vide sup: synopsin & cohærentiam capitum sequentium generalem, pag: 68.
units.tr: Here, then, is the second part of the administration of the prophetic office: namely, what Christ did and said on that final journey to Jerusalem, undertaken to meet death, which he foretold to the disciples three times, and by which he fortified them against the stumbling block of the cross. See above, the general synopsis and the coherence of the following chapters, p. 68.

units.la: Caput nonum videtur unius diei historiam complecti; quid Christus & fecerit & docuerit, à monte Thabor usque ad ingressum Capernai, ubi pronocauit. Partes sunt quatuor. I Iesus transformatus erudit discipulos de aduentu Eliæ. II Eiicit spiritum mutum & surdum quem discipuli propter incredulitatem expellere non potuerant. v. 14. III Iterum prædicit discipulis passionem suam & resurrectionem. v. 30. IV Quid in hospitio Capernaumi sit actum v. 33. Huc pertinet
units.tr: Chapter 9 seems to embrace the history of one day: what Christ both did and taught, from Mount Tabor to his entry into Capernaum, where he spent the night. Its parts are four. (1) Jesus, transfigured, instructs the disciples about the coming of Elijah. (2) He casts out a dumb and deaf spirit, which the disciples had been unable to expel because of their unbelief, v. 14. (3) Again he foretells to the disciples his passion and resurrection, v. 30. (4) What was done in the lodging at Capernaum, v. 33. To this belongs

units.la: E[?]. iij. quæstio de primatu, item de homine edente miracula in nomine Christi, & tamen non sequente ipsum, & admonitio de offendiculis studiose cauendis.
units.tr: E. iij. the question about primacy; likewise about the man who performed miracles in the name of Christ and yet did not follow him; and the admonition to take studious care to avoid stumbling blocks.

units.la: Persequitur Euangelista historiam itineris Christi Hierosolymam versus, illic passuri: ac narrat quid egerit & docuerit, cùm priuatim, tum publicè. Ac Capite decimo nominatim quid à traiectu Iordanis per Iudæam vsque in Bethphage suos docuerit: quid contra Pharisaicos errores egerit, & quæ miracula ediderit. Diuisa hæc sunt in locos hos septem. Primùm de repudio agit contra Pharisæos. ii Infantibus aditum ad se concedit, eisque benedicit. v. 13. iii Respondet interroganti de modo acquirendi vitam æternam, & monet discipulos de periculis diuitiarum. v. 17. iv Confessoribus promittit eos nihil frustra Christi nomine deserere, quia abundè illis compensatur. v. 28. v In via tertiò discipulis reuocat in memoriam prædictionem passionis & resurrectionis, quos singulariter munire voluit contra scandalum crucis. v. 32. vi Quæstio de primatu iterum mouetur per filios Zebedæi, quorum petitionem repellit, & discipulos ad humilitatem hortatur. v. 35. vii Visum restituit Bartimæo. v. 46.
units.tr: The evangelist follows the history of Christ's journey towards Jerusalem, where he was to suffer, and narrates what he did and taught, both privately and publicly. In chapter 10 in particular, he sets out what he taught his followers from the crossing of the Jordan through Judea to Bethphage, what he did against Pharisaic errors, and what miracles he performed. These are divided into the following seven sections. (1) First, he deals with divorce, against the Pharisees. (2) He admits infants to himself and blesses them, v. 13. (3) He answers the one who asks about the way to obtain eternal life, and warns the disciples about the dangers of riches, v. 17. (4) He promises to those who confess him that they will lose nothing in vain for Christ's name, since it is abundantly repaid to them, v. 28. (5) On the way, a third time, he recalls to the disciples the prediction of his passion and resurrection, which he wished to fortify them against the scandal of the cross, v. 32. (6) The question of primacy is raised again by the sons of Zebedee, whose petition he rejects, and he exhorts the disciples to humility, v. 35. (7) He restores sight to Bartimaeus, v. 46.

units.la: Capite xi. historia palmarum describitur; hoc est qua pompa Christus sese Iudæis obtulerit, vt verum Messiam & Regem patribus promissum; & quid in vrbe gestum, non solum die palmarū, sed & duobus diebus sequentibus. Partes sunt tres secundùm dierum numerum: nam primùm speciosus ingressus in die palmarum describ-bitur. ii. Postero die ex Bethania reuertens in itinere ficus maledixit, ac in templum reuersus illud repurgarepurgauit, magna etiam hostium admiratione. v. 12.
units.tr: Chapter 11 describes the history of the palms; that is, with what pomp Christ presented himself to the Jews as the true Messiah and King promised to the fathers, and what was done in the city, not only on the day of palms but also on the two days following. There are three parts, according to the number of days: first, the splendid entry on the day of palms is described. Second, on the following day, returning from Bethany, he cursed a fig tree on the way, and on returning to the temple he cleansed it, to the great astonishment of his enemies, v. 12.

units.la: III. Iterum ex Bethania redeuntes, in via disserit de fidei efficacia, sumta occasione a ficu arida, cui pridie maledixerat: ac reuersus in templum contra aduersarios disserit de sua & Iohannis Baptistae autoritate. v. 20.
units.tr: III. Returning again from Bethany, on the way he discourses on the efficacy of faith, taking occasion from the dried fig tree he had cursed the day before. Then, returning to the temple, he speaks against his opponents about his own authority and that of John the Baptist. v. 20.

units.la: Pergit Marcus cap. XII. describere doctrinam Christi in templo contra diuersos propositam. Ac ad historiam tertii diei, ut apparet, non male referri possunt. Insunt autem hi loci sex primarij: Primus de vinea optime instructa, & locata ingratis colonis, quam parabolam manifeste contra Pharisaeos dirigit. II (Contra Herodianos de censu dando (Caesari agit. v. 13. III. De resurrectione mortuorum contra Sadducaeos. v. 18. IV Interrogatur a Scriba quodam de maximo mandato. v. 28. V. Refutat doctrinam Scribarum de Christo, & eorum mores cauendos esse monet. v. 35. VI. Praedicat oblationem viduae pauperculae. v. 41.
units.tr: Mark, in chapter 12, goes on to describe the doctrine Christ set forth in the temple against various opponents. As it appears, these matters may fitly be referred to the history of the third day. There are six main passages: First, the parable of the vineyard excellently planted and let out to ungrateful tenants, which he plainly aims against the Pharisees. (2) Against the Herodians, on paying the tax to Caesar. v. 13. (3) On the resurrection of the dead, against the Sadducees. v. 18. (4) He is questioned by a certain scribe about the greatest commandment. v. 28. (5) He refutes the doctrine of the scribes concerning Christ, and warns that their manners are to be avoided. v. 35. (6) He commends the offering of the poor widow. v. 41.

units.la: Capite XIII. describitur sermo Domini habitus ad discipulos post vltimum egressum e templo: qui sermo duobus constat principali-bus membris, prophetia, vsque ad v. 33. & ex hortatione, inde vsque ad finem capitis. Prophetia est gemina: una, pronunciata in vrbe, ad discipulos vniuersos, de excidio templi, duobus primis versibus: altera pronunciata extra vrbem, in monte olearum, ad quatuor discipulos solos, de calamitati-bus Iudaeorum excidium templi antecedentibus, a v. 2. vsq; ad 14. Item de ipsius excidii atrocitate, a v. 14. vsque ad 24. Denique de suo aduentu ad iudicium vniuersale, a v. 24. vsq; ad v. 33. II Exhortatio est ad vigilantiam, seu vigilantem sui expectationem.
units.tr: Chapter 13 describes the Lord's discourse delivered to the disciples after his last departure from the temple. This discourse has two principal parts: a prophecy, up to v. 33, and an exhortation, from there to the end of the chapter. The prophecy is twofold: one, delivered within the city to all the disciples, concerning the destruction of the temple, in the first two verses; the other, delivered outside the city, on the Mount of Olives, to the four disciples alone, concerning the calamities of the Jews that will precede the destruction of the temple, from v. 2 to 14. Likewise concerning the very atrocity of that destruction, from v. 14 to 24. Finally concerning his coming to the universal judgment, from v. 24 to v. 33. (2) The exhortation is to watchfulness, or to waiting for him while watching.

units.la: DE ADMINISTRATIONE muneris Sacerdotalis.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE priestly office.

units.la: Hactenus narratum, quomodo admini-strarit Christus munus suum propheticum: se-quitur nunc quomodo Sacerdotale munus in hisce terris peregerit, patiendo scilicet pro ele-ctis sibi à Patre datis.
units.tr: So far it has been narrated how Christ administered his prophetic office. Now follows how he carried out his priestly office on this earth, namely by suffering, that is, for the elect whom the Father had given him.

units.la: Passionis historia habet Antegressa, Media, & consequuta.
units.tr: The history of the Passion has things preceding, things in the middle, and things following.

units.la: Antecedentia in capite xiv commemo-rantur sex. i Consultatio procerum de Iesu ad supplicium rapiendo. v.1.2. ii Unctio Domini ad sepulturam seu funerationem, à v. 3. usque ad 10. iii Pactio Iudae cum sacerdotibus de Iesu prodendo, v.10. & 11.[?] iv Indicatio proditoris apud discipulos in celebratione paschatis, à v.12. usque ad 22. v Doctrina de passionis fructu in cena S. institutione v.22. usque ad 26. vi. Praedictio Christi de sua comprehensione, fuga discipulorum, & abnegatione Petri, à v.26. usque ad v.32.
units.tr: The preceding events are recounted in chapter 14, six in number. (i) The council of the leaders about seizing Jesus for execution. vv. 1, 2. (ii) The anointing of the Lord for burial, or embalming, from v. 3 to 10. (iii) Judas's bargain with the priests to betray Jesus. vv. 10, 11. (iv) The indication of the betrayer to the disciples at the celebration of the Passover, from v. 12 to 22. (v) The teaching on the fruit of the passion at the institution of the holy supper, v. 22 to 26.
