(vi) Christ's prediction of his arrest, the flight of the disciples, and Peter's denial, from v. 26 to v. 32.

units.la: Media, hoc est, Passiones ipsae describuntur in reliqua parte capitis decimi quarti: primum quidem passio spiritualis in horto, & captivitas Christi, à v. 32. usque ad 53. Deinde quid in concilia-bulo Sacerdotum fit passus: ubi eius damnatio, à v. 53. usque ad v.66. & abnegatio Christi per Petrum, à v.66. usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: The middle, that is, the sufferings themselves, are described in the rest of chapter fourteen. First, the spiritual passion in the garden and the capture of Christ, from v. 32 to 53. Then what he suffered in the assembly of the priests: his condemnation there, from v. 53 to v. 66, and Peter's denial of Christ, from v. 66 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Capite xv. pertexuntur Passiones Christi, & primò narrantur ea quae passus est apud Pila-tum iudicem politicum ac praesidem Iudaeae, usque ad v.21. Deinde quid in via cum duceretur ad supplicium, v. 21. Tertiò quae & quanta in ipso supplicij loco perpessus sit, usque ad v.42. consequuta sunt quae ad Sepultu-ram Christi pertinent, quae describitur à tempore, ab efficiente, ab actionibus illius efficientis, & ab adiunctis testibus:v.42.usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: Chapter 15 sets out the sufferings of Christ. First are narrated those things he suffered before Pilate, the civil judge and governor of Judea, up to v. 21. Then what happened on the way when he was led to execution, v. 21. Thirdly, what and how great were the things he endured at the very place of execution, up to v. 42. Following these are the things that pertain to the burial of Christ, which are described by the time, by the agent, by the actions of that agent, and by the witnesses present: v. 42 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: DE ADMINISTRATIONE MU-neris Regy Christi.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE kingly office OF CHRIST.

units.la: Capite xvi & ultimo narratur de Domini resurrectione, legatione Apostolorum, ascensione in coelum, & sessione ad dextram Dei: quae actiones omnes ad administrationem mu-neris regy pertinent. Nam resurrectione sua de-monstravit se victorem ac dominum mortis & peccati & diaboli, hostium scilicet nostrorum spiritualium: legatione Apostolorum ostendit, se potestatem regiam in universum mundum à Patre accepisse: ascensione triumphum de illis hostibus egit: sessione ad dextram Dei exercere coepit regiam suam potestatem in mundo secundum humanam quoque naturam guber-nando.
units.tr: Chapter 16, the last, narrates the Lord's resurrection, the mission of the apostles, his ascension into heaven, and his sitting at the right hand of God. All these actions pertain to the administration of the kingly office. For by his resurrection he showed himself the victor and lord over death, sin and the devil, that is, our spiritual enemies. By the mission of the apostles he showed that he had received royal power over the whole world from the Father. By his ascension he celebrated a triumph over those enemies. By sitting at the right hand of God he began to exercise his royal power in the world, governing also according to his human nature.

units.la: Distingui autem potest hoc caput in tres par-tes: in quarum prima narrantur aliquot testi-monia resurrectionis Domini, usque ad v. 15. In secunda narratur legatio Apostolorum, usq; ad v. 19. In tertia narratur ascensio & sessio ad dextram Dei, duobus versibus ultimis.
units.tr: This chapter may be divided into three parts. In the first, several testimonies to the Lord's resurrection are narrated, up to v. 15. In the second, the mission of the apostles is narrated, up to v. 19. In the third, the ascension and the sitting at the right hand of God are narrated in the last two verses.

units.la: ARGUMENTA CAPITUM EX versibus R. G. expressa. In Cap. I.
units.tr: ARGUMENTS OF THE CHAPTERS, expressed in verse by R. G. In Chapter I.

units.la: Clamat Ioannes, sacrata tingitur unda, Christus, tentatus qui sua iussa docet. Discipulosq; vocat, redimitq; à Daemonis astu, Surgis & à pigra febre redempta socrus.
units.tr: John cries out; the sacred water washes him. Christ, tempted, teaches his own commands. He calls the disciples and rescues them from the demon's cunning; you rise, and the mother-in-law is freed from her sluggish fever.

units.la: Discedens orat, rursum miracula fiunt. / Turpis & à turpi corpore lepra fugit.
units.tr: Departing, he prays; again miracles happen. The foul leprosy flees from the foul body.

units.la: Consurgit, fuerat qui languida membra solutus. / Matthæus quæstum deserit atque dolos.
units.tr: He rises up, the man whose limbs had been weakened and loosed. Matthew abandons his gain and his deceits.

units.la: Peccantes revocat, tractat ieiunia quæ sint: / Sabbata qua deceat religione coli.
units.tr: He calls back sinners and teaches what fasts are, and with what reverence the Sabbaths should be kept.

units.la: Arida dextra valet, elapsus dogmata pandit / Sancta, simul sanans: discipulosque legit.
units.tr: The withered hand is restored. The one who had slipped sets forth holy doctrines, healing at the same time, and gathers the disciples.

units.la: Impuro sanctus violatur spiritus ore. / Et Christus fratres indicat inde suos.
units.tr: The holy spirit is violated by an impure mouth. And then Christ points out his own brothers.

units.la: Seminat hic verbum, quod ne spargatur inane, / Sola Dei virtus sancta iuvare potest.
units.tr: Here he sows the word; lest it be scattered in vain, only the holy power of God can help it.

units.la: Ut sinapi granum, sic crescunt semina verbi. / Commotumque domant fortia verba mare.
units.tr: As a mustard seed, so the seeds of the word grow. And strong words tame the sea when it is stirred.

units.la: Deseruit Satanæ mortalia membra potestas. / Correptos porcos cærula in alta ruens.
units.tr: The power of Satan released mortal limbs. The swine, seized, rush down into the deep blue sea.

units.la: Sanguinis immodici compescit fœmina fluxum. / Mortua quæ fuerat vita puella, valet.
units.tr: A woman checks the flow of immoderate blood. The girl who had been dead comes back to life.

units.la: Patria contemnit: doctores mittit in orbem. / Baptistæ sæuo concidit ense caput.
units.tr: He is despised in his homeland; he sends teachers out into the world. The head of the Baptist falls to the cruel sword.

units.la: Militia multa cibat: fluidis superambulat undis. / Ægrotos plures fimbria tacta iuvat.
units.tr: He feeds a great multitude; he walks over the fluid waves. Many sick are helped by a touched fringe.

units.la: Corripit humanæ rationis dogmata falsa, / Et quæ sint homini non bene munda docet.
units.tr: He rebukes the false doctrines of human reason, and teaches what is not clean for man.

units.la: Liberat hinc syrophœnissæ de dæmone natam. / Auditum surdus, verbaque mutus habet.
units.tr: Hence he frees the Syrophoenician's daughter from the demon. The deaf man has hearing, and the dumb man has speech.

units.la: Bis duo millia alit: poscit gens perfida signum, / Fermentum caveant: cæcus & ante, videt.
units.tr: He feeds two thousand twice over; the faithless nation demands a sign. Let them beware the leaven; the blind man also sees beforehand.

units.la: Discipulis illum fa[?]is sua fata prædicit: / Hortaturque crucis pondera ferre suæ.
units.tr: He foretells his fate to the disciples and exhorts them to bear the weight of his cross.

units.la: Transformat faciem: Satanæ quoque liberat æ[?]tus / Quem pia discipuli vincere dextra nequit.
units.tr: He transforms his face, and also frees from the rage of Satan one whom the pious right hand of the disciples could not overcome.

units.la: Reprimit elatos: aliis ut dæmona pellant / Permittit: rigide scandala dira vetat.
units.tr: He restrains the proud; he permits others to drive out demons, and sternly forbids dire offences.

units.la: Coniugium instituit, tangit sacra dextra puellos: / Divitibus durum est regna subire Dei.
units.tr: He institutes marriage and touches the children with his holy hand. It is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom of God.

units.la: Præmia sanctorum: zebedidas corde superbos / Reprimit: accepto lumine cæce vides.
units.tr: The rewards of the saints: he restrains the sons of Zebedee, proud in heart. The blind man, having received light, sees.

units.la: Vox Hosanna sonat, subito perit arida ficus: / Subvertit sanctæ turpia lucra domus. Quantaque sit virtus fidei : quo numine missu Haec faciat, Dominum gens odiosa rogat. 12 Agricolae ingrati pelluntur : reddite censum. Et caro de putri nostra resurget humo. Maxima lex quae sit : CHRISTVS Dauide creatus, Factus inest Scribis : aera minuta probat. 13 Clara cadent tandem Solymorum moenia : pravos Affligent : Sanctos multa pericla manent. Hinc docet extremae quae nam sit forma diei Quae cunctis vigili corde notanda venit. 14 Vnguentis redolent crines : hunc vendit Iudas. Instituit mortis symbola sacra suae. Vota patri fundit, capitur telisque dolisque. Diffugiunt : forti percutit ense Petrus. Pontifices captum condemnant : caeditur insons : Doctoremque negas territe Petre tuum. 15 Traditur Ausonio Praetori : Barraban alta Voce petunt, CHRISTVM damnat iniqua manus. Fertque crucem propriam : clavis configitur insons. Distribuunt vestes : impia probra sonant. Tristia sed mortem comitantur signa nefandam Et tumulant sanctae mortua membra manus. 16 Angelus attonitis Mariis facta omnia narrat. Appares variis, CHRISTE supreme, modis. Infirmos culpat, totumque ablegat in orbem. Relliquis terris summa sub astra volat.
units.tr: The voice "Hosanna" sounds; suddenly the dry fig tree perishes; he overturns the shameful gains of the holy house. How great is the power of faith, and by what divine power he does these things, the hateful nation asks of the Lord. The ungrateful husbandmen are driven out; pay the tax. Our flesh also rises from the rotten earth. What is the greatest law: Christ, born of David, is present among the scribes, made so; he tests the small coin. The bright walls of Jerusalem fall at last; the wicked will be afflicted, and many dangers await the saints. Hence he teaches what form the last day will take, which must be noted by every watchful heart. (Chapter 14) His hair smells of ointments; Judas sells him. He institutes the holy symbols of his death. He pours out vows to the Father; he is seized with weapons and tricks. They scatter; Peter strikes with a bold sword. The priests condemn the captive; the innocent one is beaten; and you deny your teacher, terrified Peter. (Chapter 15) He is handed over to the Ausonian praetor. They ask for Barabbas with loud voice; the wicked hand condemns Christ. He bears his own cross; the innocent one is fixed with nails. They divide the garments; impious insults resound. Yet sad signs accompany the unspeakable death, and holy hands entomb the dead limbs. (Chapter 16) An angel tells the astonished Marys all that has been done. Supreme Christ, you appear in various ways. He blames the faithless and sends the whole [message] into the world. Above the other lands he flies beneath the lofty stars.

units.la: ARGVMENTA CAPITVM ex G. F. CAPVT I.
units.tr: Arguments of the chapters from G. F., chapter 1.

units.la: AEluitur Dominus tentatur, quattuor addit. Daemonium pellit cum febre, cumque lepra.
units.tr: The Lord is tempted; he adds four things. He drives out a demon, and cures fever and leprosy.

units.la: 2 Blasphemum reputant. sequitur Matthaeus. utrisque Rumpuntur. pellis spica vexulsa famem.
units.tr: 2 They count him a blasphemer. Matthew follows. Both are broken off. The ears of grain are plucked; hunger.

units.la: 3 Cura manus. fuga spirituum. cognomina bis sex. Regnum divisum non stat, adesque parens.
units.tr: 3 The healing of the hand. The flight of the spirits. The twelve names. A divided kingdom does not stand, and the house falls.

units.la: 4 Dat semen fructum. patefient omnia. crescit Sponte seges. minimum semen. & unda fremens.
units.tr: 4 It gives seed and fruit. All things will be made manifest. The crop grows of its own accord. The smallest seed. And the roaring sea.

units.la: 5 Egreditur legio. natitat grex, rheuma cruoris Cessat. primatia filia viua sedet.
units.tr: 5 The legion goes out. The herd swims. The flow of blood ceases. The ruler's daughter sits up alive.

units.la: 6 Fabrigena hæc? paria emittit. Baptista necatur. Pascit. calcat aquas. languida membra valent.
units.tr: 6 The carpenter's son? He sends out pairs. John the Baptist is put to death. He feeds them. He treads on the waters. The weak limbs grow strong.

units.la: 7 Gignit mens impura malum. non sordida palma. Mica placet catulis. recta loquela redit.
units.tr: 7 An impure mind begets evil. Not with unwashed hands. A crumb pleases the puppies. Right speech returns.

units.la: 8 Implet. taxat. abit. sensim dat lumina cæco Quemque vocent rogitat. quaque ferenda monet.
units.tr: 8 He fills, he rebukes, he departs. Gradually he gives light to the blind man. He asks whom they call him, and advises what is to be borne.

units.la: 9 Lux formæ. quæ vis ieiuni quis prior. edit Signa malus. trunces membra. parato salem.
units.tr: 9 The light of the form. What power of fasting; which comes first. The evil one gives signs; he maims the limbs; prepare the salt.

units.la: 10 Moses dissoluit. dimes dolet. omnia linquunt. Stulta petis genitrix. tu quoque cæce vides.
units.tr: 10 Moses is dissolved. The tithe-payer grieves. They leave everything. Foolish mother, you seek; you too, blind one, see.

units.la: 11 Nunc asinum quærunt. ficus perit. emptor abactus. En quæ vis fidei. qui facis ista rogans.
units.tr: 11 Now they seek the donkey. The fig tree withers. The buyer is driven off. Behold the power of faith, you who ask and do these things.

units.la: 12 Occisus natus. census. connubia septem. Ius primum. Christi quis pater. æs vidua.
units.tr: 12 The dead son. The tax. Seven marriages. The first right. Whose father is Christ? The widow's coin.

units.la: 13 Plurima iudicium præcedunt signa. diesque Soli nota patri, nos vigilare monet.
units.tr: 13 Many signs precede the judgment, and the day known only to the Father. He warns us to watch.

units.la: 14 Quæstus Iudæ. pascha. preces. auris. fuga nudi. Testes. sputa, alapæ. cum lachrymante Petro.
units.tr: 14 The bargain of Judas. The Passover. Prayers. The ear. The flight of the naked man. Witnesses. Spittle and blows, with Peter weeping.

units.la: 15 Reiectus. lapsus suspensus. signa salesque. Eli. Centurio, membra petita. lapis.
units.tr: 15 Rejected. Fallen, hanged. Signs and mockery. Eli. The centurion. The limbs sought. The stone.

units.la: 16 Surgit. conspicitur. dubitantibus exprobrat. iisdem Ite inquit. fidei signa dat. alta petit.
units.tr: 16 He rises. He is seen. He rebukes those who doubt. To the same he says, "Go." He gives signs of faith. He ascends on high.

units.la: TERTII GENERIS
units.tr: Of the third kind

units.la: versus μνημονευτικος[?] 1 2 3 4 5 Baptistæ, Curat, Tactu, de Semine, Dæmon, 6 9 7 8 9 10 Patria, non Lotis, velut Arbor, Fullo, Camelus, 11 12 13 14 15 Sternunt: Æra duo, Vigil, Azyma, Passio, in 16 Altum.
units.tr: Mnemonic verse [μνημονευτικός] 1 2 3 4 5: Of the Baptist, heals, by touch, of the seed, demon; 6 9 7 8 9 10: native place, not washed, like a tree, fuller, camel; 11 12 13 14 15: they strew, two coins, watch, unleavened bread, passion; 16: on high.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Baptistæ Iohannis ministerium. Curat Christus paralyticum. v. 4. Tactu sanatur contractus. v. 10. de Semine, in diversa loca sparso. v. 3. Dæmon obsidens hominem. v. 2. Patria Christi ingrata. v. 4. non Lotis manibus cibum capiunt. v. 2. velut Arbor homo apparet cæco sanato. v. 24. Fullo vestes irrigans. v. 3. Camelus transiens per foramen acus. v. 25. Sternunt frondes & vestimenta in via. v. 8. Æra duo immituntur gazophylacio. v. 24. Vigilandum discipulis Christi. v. 33. Azyma liba. v. 1. Passio Christi. in Altum evehitur Christus à nube. v. 19.
units.tr: Of the Baptist: the ministry of John. Heals: Christ heals the paralytic. v. 4. By touch: the contracted woman is healed by touch. v. 10. Of the seed: scattered in various places. v. 3. Demon: besieging a man. v. 2. Native place: Christ's ungrateful homeland. v. 4. Not washed: they take food with unwashed hands. v. 2. Like a tree: a man appears like a tree to the blind man who was healed. v. 24. Fuller: washing garments. v. 3. Camel: passing through the eye of a needle. v. 25. They strew: leaves and garments on the way. v. 8. Two coins: put into the treasury. v. 24. To be watched: by the disciples of Christ. v. 33. Unleavened bread: the cakes. v. 1. Passion: of Christ. On high: Christ is carried up on high from the cloud. v. 19.

units.la: ANALYSIS EVANGELII SE-CUNDUM LUCAM.
units.tr: ANALYSIS OF THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE.

units.la: EX OCCASIONE TITVLI & Præfationis huius Euangelistæ, quatuor potissimum generalis προθεωρίας causâ perstringemus: Quis scribat, Quid, Quomodo, & Quibus.
units.tr: Taking the occasion from the title and preface of this Evangelist, we shall especially touch on four matters by way of general introduction: who writes, what, how, and to whom.

units.la: Quis scribat. S. Lucas Euangelista, cui Patria fuit Antiochia Syriæ. Hinc Syrus à S. Hieronymo dicitur in Prologo in Lucam. Idem ibidem eum Medicum fuisse ait: quod etiam illi tribuit Nicephorus. Unum addit lib. 6. cap.16. insignem eum fuisse pictorem. Vita igitur ge-nus ante conversionem philosophicum fuisse videtur, cùm medicus professione fuerit, ac eam professionem etiam in Christianismo retinuerit: nam Paulus in Epistola ad Col. cap. 4. Salutat vos (inquit) Lucas medicus.
units.tr: Who writes. St Luke the evangelist, whose native city was Antioch in Syria. For this reason Jerome, in his Prologue on Luke, calls him a Syrian. In the same place he says that Luke was a physician, and Nicephorus also ascribes this to him. In book 6, chapter 16, Nicephorus adds that he was an outstanding painter. As to his life, then, it seems that before his conversion he was of a philosophical kind, since he practised medicine as his profession, and he kept that profession even as a Christian. For Paul, in his Epistle to the Colossians, chapter 4, says: "Luke, the beloved physician, greets you."

units.la: Quos pietatis habuerit Præceptores ipse non obscurè significat in præfatione ad Theophi[?] lum ; hos nimirum qui ab initio suis oculis viderunt & pars aliqua fuerunt eorum quæ scribit. Ex quo certum est, Lucam ab Apostolis fuisse instructum de vera Salutis ratione, & historia Christi agentis inter homines.
units.tr: The teachers he had in piety he indicates quite plainly in the preface to Theophilus: namely, those who from the beginning saw things with their own eyes and were some part of the things he writes about. From this it is certain that Luke was instructed by the apostles in the true way of salvation and in the history of Christ's dealings among men.

units.la: Quid scripserit. Scripta S. Lucæ duo insignia extant, historia hæc Euangelica, & Acta Apostolorum. Euangelium quid sit, & quomodo accipiatur in S. literis, superius est expositum. Huc autem pertinent specialia, qualis est occasio, argumentum, propositio. Occasio illi oblata fuit, & quidem necessitate imposita. Siue enim à Petro hoc munus illi iniunctum, vt vult Dorotheus, in sua Synopsi, siue à Paulo, vt Nicephorus, qui lib.2. cap.45. iussum à Paulo scribit, vt Marcus à Petro, & lib.5. cap.16. sane tantorum virorum authoritas, necessario illi fuit sequenda. Cæterum ipsemet veram occasionem exprimit mox in præfatione, quia scilicet videbat scribi multa à multis, quæ non erant satis comperta : ideoque voluit sua opera posteritati consulere, vt compertam & solidam haberet Ecclesia historiam Euangelicam. Et de ipsius constantia & synceritate in doctrina Euangelij, & officiis quibus Apostolum Paulum iuuit, testatur Paulus, cum inquit : Demas me dereliquit, amplexus præsens seculum, & abijt Thessalonicam : Lvcas mecum est solus. 2. Tim. 4. Etsi igitur Lucas non fuit ex numero duodecim Apostolorum : tamen historiam Euangelicam, & conciones Christi ex ore Apostolorum (qui oculati testes fuerunt) diligentissime & fidelissime excepit atque literis consignauit.
units.tr: What he wrote. Two notable writings of St Luke survive: this Gospel history and the Acts of the Apostles. What the gospel is, and how the term is understood in the Holy Scriptures, has been explained above. What belongs here are the particular matters: the occasion, the subject, and the proposition. The occasion was presented to him, and indeed was laid upon him by necessity. For whether this task was enjoined on him by Peter, as Dorotheus holds in his Synopsis, or by Paul, as Nicephorus writes in book 2, chapter 45, that he was bidden by Paul just as Mark was by Peter (and in book 5, chapter 16), certainly the authority of such great men had to be followed by him. Moreover, he himself states the true occasion shortly afterwards in the preface, namely that he saw that many things were being written by many people which were not sufficiently established; therefore he wished to serve posterity by his work, so that the Church might have a established and sound Gospel history. And Paul bears witness to Luke's constancy and sincerity in the doctrine of the gospel, and to the services by which he helped the apostle Paul, when he says: "Demas has forsaken me, having embraced the present world, and has gone to Thessalonica; Luke alone is with me." 2 Tim. 4. Although Luke was therefore not one of the twelve apostles, nevertheless he received most diligently and most faithfully, from the mouths of the apostles (who were eyewitnesses), the Gospel history and the sermons of Christ, and set them down in writing.

units.la: Et hoc
units.tr: And this

units.la: Right page, margin notes at the left edge of the scan (cut off): Et hoc Euangelium secundum Lucam Ecclesia recepit & approbauit: cum ea, quae sub nomine Nicodemi, Thomae ac Barnabae circumferebantur iustis de causis reprobauerit. Potuit enim primitiua Ecclesia, quae ipsos Apostolos audiebat, recte de genuinis & suppositiitis scriptis iudicare. Et Ecclesiae officium est, suppositicia a veris discernere: non autem propterea potestatem habet, vel suppositicia scripta approbandi, vel vera & genuina reiiciendi. Aliud est enim agnoscere sigillum & chirographum sui Principis: aliud est, sibi ius sumere Principis sui statuta & decreta immutandi, abolendi, aut falsa sub nomine Principis obtrudendi. Horum nihil facit Ecclesia Christi: conatur autem id facere Ecclesia Antichristi.
units.tr: Margin notes on the right-hand page, cut off at the left edge of the scan: The Church received and approved this Gospel according to Luke, while for good reasons it rejected those writings which were circulated under the names of Nicodemus, Thomas and Barnabas. For the primitive Church, which heard the apostles themselves, could rightly judge between genuine and spurious writings. It is the office of the Church to distinguish spurious writings from true ones; but it does not therefore have the power either to approve spurious writings or to reject true and genuine ones. For it is one thing to recognise the seal and handwriting of one's prince; it is another to take upon oneself the right to change, abolish, or foist false decrees and statutes under the prince's name. The Church of Christ does none of these things; but the Church of Antichrist tries to do them.

units.la: Argumentum. Exorditur autem historiam Euangelicam altius quam Matthæus & Marcus, qui cum Luca humanitatis Christi historiam inprimis persequuntur. Nam non contentus a Baptismo Ioannis & Genealogia Christi rem ordiri, resumit etiam illa, quae ad conceptionem tam Christi, quam Ioannis Baptistæ pertinent: item utriusque natiuitatem, & quae circa illa tempora contigere. Hinc demum ad Christi doctrinam & facta progreditur. In miraculis diligens & copiosus est: indicat enim occasiones, fructus, variasque circumstantias. Vitam Christi exornat affectibus humanis, & ad gratificandum pronis.ita ut absit peccatum: comites ubique tribuit Christo, discipulos, summe simplices, aut turbas ad discendum auidas: adversarios extreme pertinaces, Judæos, & ex his,
units.tr: Subject. Now Luke begins his Gospel history more deeply than Matthew and Mark, who above all follow Christ's history in its human aspect with Luke. For, not content to start the matter with John's baptism and Christ's genealogy, he also takes up those things which concern the conception of both Christ and John the Baptist, likewise the birth of each, and what happened around those times. Only then does he proceed to Christ's teaching and deeds. He is careful and full in the miracles, for he indicates the occasions, the fruits, and the varied circumstances. He adorns the life of Christ with human feelings, and with inclinations toward kindness, yet so that sin is absent. He assigns companions to Christ everywhere: disciples who are extremely simple, or crowds eager to learn; and adversaries who are extremely obstinate: the Jews, and among them

units.la: Pharisæos, Pontifices, Scribas, Seniores, penes quos cura debuit esse Religionis. Reliqui auditores, faciles ad intelligendum animos, ut plurimùm afferunt. Tandem historiam passionis ingressus, studiosè indicat veras illius causas externas, Christum ubique præscium & paratum ad mortem: quid ante mortem, in morte & post mortem contigerit. Denique historiam concludit glorioso ad cœlos reditu, unde illum adhuc expectamus iudicem viuorum & mor-tuorum, donec ad salutem nostram appareat.
units.tr: the Pharisees, the high priests, the scribes and the elders, to whom the care of religion ought to have belonged. The remaining hearers are, for the most part, minds easy to instruct. At last, entering upon the history of the passion, he carefully sets out its true external causes, Christ everywhere foreknowing and ready for death; and what happened before death, in death and after death. Finally he concludes the history with the glorious return to heaven, whence we still await him as judge of the living and the dead, until he appears for our salvation.

units.la: Propositio & scopus est, Christum esse verum illum Messiam Patribus promissum, Redem-torem humani generis, licet pauci illud agno-verint, cuius veram historiam voluit describe-re. Ipse Lucas Act.1. Propositione instituti sui, sic fere statuit: De doctrina & miraculis Christi, omnisque vitæ historia vsque ad reditum ad cœlos, & institutum ministerium docendi Euan-gelium Apostolis relictum in Ecclesia.
units.tr: The proposition and aim is to describe the true history of him whom he wished to describe: that Christ is that true Messiah promised to the fathers, the Redeemer of the human race, although few have recognised it. Luke himself, in Acts 1, sets out the proposition of his undertaking roughly thus: concerning the teaching and miracles of Christ, and the whole history of his life up to his return to heaven, and the ministry of teaching the Gospel, instituted and left to the apostles in the Church.

units.la: Quomodo scripserit. Genus orationis apud Lu-cam, florens est, & historico more dilucidum. Ac quod verba quidem attinet, sermonis forma humilis videtur: demittit enim sese ad popula-rem puræ loquendi consuetudinem, non tamen uti Matthæus & Marcus: politor aliquanto Lucæ stylus est, non tamen assurgit ad Demosthe-nicam pompam, & Ethnicum splendorem verborum: ideoque εὐχήμων [?] est, qualis habitus veritatis historiam decet. Sin vero rem ipsam inspicias, grauis est & sublimis idea. tractat enim res impendio graues: de Filio Dei æterno Mediatore humani generis, de fide, de vita æterna, de ratione salutis, de poenis impiorum,de præ-miis fidelium,de morte,resurrectione, & ascen-sione Christi,de ministerio verbi instituto, &c.
units.tr: How he wrote. The style of Luke is flourishing and, in historical manner, clear. As to words, the form of his speech seems humble: for he lowers himself to the common usage of pure speech, yet not as Matthew and Mark do. Luke's style is somewhat more polished, but it does not rise to Demosthenic grandeur or to the showy brilliance of the pagan writers; and so it is becoming [εὐσχήμων], as the dress of historical truth ought to be. But if you look at the matter itself, the idea is weighty and lofty. For he treats matters of very great weight: the eternal Son of God as Mediator of the human race, faith, eternal life, the way of salvation, the punishments of the wicked, the rewards of the faithful, the death, resurrection and ascension of Christ, the ministry of the Word as instituted, and so on.

units.la: Lucæ proprium studium erat vt historiam exactam & plenam ex rerum ordine & serie contexeret .Luc. 1. v. 2.3.4. Hinc omnia à primordiis in ipso altè re petita.
units.tr: Luke's own aim was to weave together an exact and full history, following the order and sequence of events (Luke 1:2–4). Hence he takes up everything from the very beginnings, traced far back.

units.la: DE PRÆFATIONE.
units.tr: ON THE PREFACE.

units.la: S. Lucas inter cætera & hoc à reliquis Euangelistis peculiare habet,quod reliqui sine Proœ-mio,Lucas autem προοιμιάζων[?] historiam auspicatur. Docemur hinc, non positum in istis pietatis cardinem,sed liberum esse præfari, aut non præfari, modo in capitibus ipsius causæ consensus reperiatur.Scopus & propositio præfationis est:Theophilo (sunt autem omnes verè Christiani theophili)de veritate huius historiæ nullatenus esse dubitandum :1. quia scribat narrationem earum rerum quarum plena fides nobis facta est: 2. idque ab iis qui fuerunt oculati testes & ministri : 3. quia Lucas scribit postquam omnia à principio accuratè persecutus est: quæ omnia ad Theophili diriguntur ædificationem : nam quæ hactenus viva voce didicit,iam scripto quoque leget magis expolita & explicata.
units.tr: Among other things, Luke has this peculiarity compared with the other Evangelists: the rest begin without a preface, but Luke begins his history with a proem [προοιμιάζων]. We are taught from this that a preface is not a fixed element of piety, and that one may or may not write a preface, provided that agreement is found in the main points of the matter itself. The aim and proposition of the preface is that there should be no doubt at all to Theophilus (and indeed all true Christians are Theophili) about the truth of this history: (1) because he writes a narrative of those things of which full certainty has been given to us; (2) and this from those who were eyewitnesses and ministers; (3) because Luke writes after he has carefully traced everything from the beginning. All these things are directed to the edification of Theophilus, for what he has so far learned by word of mouth he will now also read in writing, more polished and explained.

units.la: DISTRIBUTIO EVANGELII secundum Lucam.
units.tr: DISTRIBUTION OF THE GOSPEL according to Luke.

units.la: Describitur Christi Redemptoris Persona & vita priuata: eius. Incarnatio cuius not: Antegressa sunt Iohannis Baptistæ, qui Christi fuit prodromus, natales: quibus etiam inseritur vaticinium, siue annunciatio conceptionis & natiuitatis Christi, ab Angelo ad Mariam misso. cap. 1. Media seu coniuncta cum consecutis: ipsa natiuitas: circumcisio, oblatio, educatio, & specimen diuinitatis. cap. 2. praeparatio ad officium per Vocationem & inauguratio-nem Christi ad præconium Euangelij, in publica Iohannis Baptistæ proclamatione, & solenni S. Trinitatis declarationem: vbi additur Genealogia Christi. cap. 3. Tentationem, in qua se victo-rem Diaboli memorabili illa monomachia demonstrauit. cap. 4. usque ad v. 14. officio & vita eius publica, in statu tum Humiliationis: officii Propheticum, a v. 14. Capitis quarti usque ad finem capitis 21. Vide horum subdiuisionem infra suo loco. Sacerdotale, in passione & morte Christi, c.22.28[?] Exaltationis: munus Regium cap. 24.
units.tr: The person and private life of Christ the Redeemer are described. His incarnation, of which the notes are: preceding it are the birth of John the Baptist, who was the forerunner of Christ; inserted among these is the prophecy, or announcement of the conception and birth of Christ, sent by the angel to Mary (ch. 1). The middle, or what is joined with what follows: the birth itself, the circumcision, the presentation, the upbringing, and a display of divinity (ch. 2). Preparation for the office through the calling and inauguration of Christ, with the proclamation of the gospel in the public proclamation of John the Baptist, and the solemn declaration of the Holy Trinity, where the genealogy of Christ is added (ch. 3). The temptation, in which he showed himself the victor over the Devil in that memorable single combat (ch. 4 to v. 14). His public office and life, in the state of humiliation: the prophetic office, from ch. 4 v. 14 to the end of ch. 21; see its subdivision below in its place. The priestly office, in the passion and death of Christ, ch. 22–28. The exaltation: the kingly office, ch. 24.

units.la: Capitis primi post praefationem partes sunt quinq; : I. Narratio de conceptione Johannis Baptistæ, præcursoris ac primi ex hominibus testis publici Domini incarnati: à v. 5. usque ad v. 26. II. Narratio de conceptione Christi, usque ad v. 39. III. Recitatio prophetationis Elisabethæ & Mariæ de ipso usque ad v. 57. IV. Narratio de natiuitate & circumcisione Johannis Baptistæ, usque ad v. 67. V. Recitatio prophetationis Zachariæ tum de Christo, tum de Johanne.
units.tr: The parts of the first chapter after the preface are five: I. The narrative of the conception of John the Baptist, the forerunner and first public witness among men of the incarnate Lord: from v. 5 to v. 26. II. The narrative of the conception of Christ, to v. 39. III. The recital of the prophesying of Elizabeth and Mary about him, to v. 57. IV. The narrative of the birth and circumcision of John the Baptist, to v. 67. V. The recital of the prophesying of Zechariah, both about Christ and about John.

units.la: In capite secundo quatuor de Christo narrantur: primùm Natiuitas eius, usque ad v. 21. deinde (circumcisio. v. 21. tetiò præsentatio illius in templo, ubi & Simeonis & Annæ prophetissæ de Christo confessio, usque ad v. 41. Postremò specimen & quasi tyrocinium muneris prophetici, nec non specimen muneris regij, usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: In the second chapter four things about Christ are narrated: first, his birth, to v. 21. Then (his circumcision, v. 21. Third, his presentation in the temple, where also the confession about Christ by Simeon and the prophetess Anna is given, to v. 41. Last, a specimen and, as it were, an apprenticeship of the prophetic office, and also a specimen of the kingly office, to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Hactenus de iis quæ pertinent ad Christi natiuitatem & pueritiam atque adolescentiam: de-inceps sequuntur ea quæ pertinent ad ætatem eius virilem: ubi primo præmittuntur ea quibus ad munus propheticum administrandum fuit præ-paratus: quæ sunt numero tria: 1. Ministerium Johânis Baptistæ quo præparati sunt auditores. 2. Baptismus Christi in quo voce Dei præsentatus fuit & donis Spiritus sancti repletus; 3. ten-tatio ipsius à Diabolo.
units.tr: So far concerning what pertains to the birth, childhood and youth of Christ; next follow those things which pertain to his adult age. Here first are set forth those things by which he was prepared to discharge the prophetic office, which are three in number: (1) the ministry of John the Baptist, by which the hearers were prepared; (2) the baptism of Christ, in which he was presented by the voice of God and filled with the gifts of the Holy Spirit; (3) his temptation by the Devil.

units.la: Capite tertio narratur primò ministerium Johannis Baptistæ, usque ad v. 21. Deinde Baptisatio Christi, v. 21. & 22. Postremò genealogia seu recensio maiorū Christi, inde usque ad finem capitis
units.tr: In chapter three there is narrated first the ministry of John the Baptist, to v. 21. Then the baptism of Christ, vv. 21 and 22. Last, the genealogy, or listing of the ancestors of Christ, from there to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Capite quarto, à v. 1. usque ad v. 14. est tertia præparatio Christi ad munus ipsius propheticum fungendum, videlicet tentatio à diabolo.
units.tr: In chapter four, from v. 1 to v. 14, is the third preparation of Christ for performing his prophetic office, namely the temptation by the Devil.

units.la: Hactenus igitur de persona Christi, vita eius primaria, & praeparatione ad officium : sequitur
units.tr: So far, then, concerning the person of Christ, his early life, and his preparation for the office; what follows is

units.la: DE EXECUTIONE MUNERIS prophetici, à v. 14. capitis quarti, usque ad cap. 22.
units.tr: ON THE EXECUTION OF THE PROPHETIC OFFICE, from ch. 4 v. 14 to ch. 22.

units.la: CURSUM executionis muneris prophetici bipartito (ut & in prioribus Evangelistis) distinguemus. Prima pars continet historiam eorum quae dixit fecitque Christus toto illo tempore, quod ab ipsius Baptismo & tentatione, usque ad ultimam eius Hierosolymam profectionem moriendi gratia institutam, intercessit, à v. 14. capitis quarti, usque ad capitis noni versum 51. Secunda pars habet dicta gestaque Christi illius profectionis usque ad historiam passionis & mortis, à v. 51. capitis noni, usque ad initium 22. capitis.
units.tr: We shall distinguish the course of the execution of the prophetic office in two parts (as also in the other Evangelists). The first part contains the history of what Christ said and did during the whole time that passed from his baptism and temptation until his last journey to Jerusalem undertaken for the sake of dying, from ch. 4 v. 14 to ch. 9 v. 51. The second part has the sayings and doings of Christ on that journey, up to the history of the passion and death, from ch. 9 v. 51 to the beginning of ch. 22.

units.la: DE PRIMA PARTE, CUIUS hæc est synopsis & subdivisio.
units.tr: ON THE FIRST PART, WHOSE SYNOPSIS AND SUBDIVISION IS AS FOLLOWS.

units.la: Christus officio prophetico functus Solus[?] Reliqua parte capitis quarti, docendo & operando. Capite quinto toto: Christi miracula & dicta. Parte capitis sexti: vbi dicta & facta eius à v. 1. usque ad 12. versum. Sociis adscitis Apostolorum electio & consolatio, à v. 12. capitis 6. usque ad eius finem. Reliqua Christi dicta gestaque cap. 7. 8. & parte noni Hic not:
units.tr: Christ, having performed the prophetic office, teaching and working. The whole of chapter five: the miracles and sayings of Christ. Part of chapter six: where his sayings and deeds are given from v. 1 to v. 12. With companions taken on, the election and comfort of the Apostles, from v. 12 of chapter 6 to its end. The remaining sayings and deeds of Christ in chapters 7, 8 and part of 9. Note here:

units.la: Capitis igitur quarti parte secunda narratur initiù prædicationis Christi in synagogis Galilææ (v. 14.15.) & nominatim sermo habitus Nazareth ex propheta Iesaia, usque ad v. 13. Tertia narratur ejectio dæmonij muti in Synagoga Capernaum, usque ad v. 38. Quarta sanatio socrus Petri, v. 38.39. & multorum ægrotorum & dæmoniacorum, v. 40. & 41. Postrema continuatio prædicationis in Galilæa.
units.tr: The second part of chapter four narrates the beginning of Christ's preaching in the synagogues of Galilee (vv. 14, 15), and by name the sermon delivered at Nazareth from the prophet Isaiah, to v. 13. The third narrates the casting out of a dumb demon in the synagogue at Capernaum, to v. 38. The fourth, the healing of Peter's mother-in-law, vv. 38, 39, and of many sick and demon-possessed, vv. 40, 41. The last, the continuation of preaching in Galilee.

units.la: Capitis quinti partes sunt principales tres: Prima narrantur aliquot miracula Christi : ut est 1. captura piscium. 11 mundatio leprosi. v. 12. 111 Sanatio paralytici, v. 17. Secunda narratur vocatio Leuis, id est, Matthæi, v. 27. 28. Tertia narratur defensio contra Scribarum & Pharisæorum reprehensionem primam, propter conuersationem Christi cum publicanis, usque ad v. 33. & secundam propter indulgentiam eius erga discipulos.
units.tr: The chief parts of chapter five are three. The first: several miracles of Christ are narrated, namely (1) the catch of fish; (2) the cleansing of a leper, v. 12; (3) the healing of a paralytic, v. 17. The second: the calling of Levi, that is, Matthew, vv. 27, 28 is narrated. The third: the defence against the first rebuke of the Scribes and Pharisees, because of Christ's association with tax collectors, to v. 33, and the second, on account of his indulgence towards his disciples, is narrated.

units.la: Capitis sexti membra tria sunt. 1 Christus defendit discipulos contra criminationem Pharisæorum de violato, propter euulsas spicas, Sabbatho, usque ad v. 6. 11. Sanat manum cuiusdam aridam, seque contra tacitam Pharisæorum criminationem de Sabbatho violato inde natam defendit: usque ad v. 12. 111. Eligit duodecim Apostolos: & sermonem prolixum habet, tum ad discipulos recens electos contra persecutiones consolandos, tum ad turbam reliquam a v. 24. usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: The chapter six has three members. (1) Christ defends his disciples against the Pharisees' accusation of breaking the Sabbath by plucking ears of corn, to v. 6. (2) He heals the withered hand of a certain man, and defends himself against the silent accusation of the Pharisees of violating the Sabbath arising from this, to v. 12. (3) He chooses twelve Apostles, and gives a lengthy discourse, both to comfort the newly chosen disciples against persecutions, and to the rest of the crowd, from v. 24 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Cap. septimo narrantur Christi primo quidem gesta, nimirum miraculum sanati servi centurionis, usque ad v. 11. & excitati a morte filij viduæ Naitanæ, usque ad v. 18. Deinde dicta, videlicet Responsum datum nuncijs missis à Iohanne Baptista , & testimonium ipsi apud turbam perhibitum, usque ad v. 31. tum conquæritur de peruersita- te Scribarum & Pharisæorum, usque ad v. 36. Denique remittit in domo Pharisæi cuiusdam pec- cata mulieri peccatrici.
units.tr: In chapter seven there are narrated Christ's deeds first, namely the miracle of the healing of the centurion's servant, to v. 11, and the raising of the son of the widow of Nain from the dead, to v. 18. Then his sayings, namely the answer given to the messengers sent by John the Baptist, and the testimony borne to him before the crowd, to v. 31; then he complains of the perversity of the Scribes and Pharisees, to v. 36. Finally, he forgives the sins of a sinful woman in the house of a certain Pharisee.

units.la: Pergit Dominus in administratione mune- ris Prophetici docendo & operando: docendo quidem: nam proponit & explicat parabolam de satore, usque ad v. 19. & respondet de matre & fratribus, usque ad v. 22. Operando autem: nam sedat tempestatem maris, usque ad v. 26. & eiicit dæmonia complura ex homine uno, usque ad v. 40. & sanat mulierem laborantem fluxione sanguinis, excitatqueà morte filiam Iaïri.
units.tr: The Lord goes on in the administration of the prophetic office, teaching and working: teaching, indeed, for he sets forth and explains the parable of the sower, to v. 19, and answers about his mother and brothers, to v. 22. Working, however: for he calms the storm at sea, to v. 26, and casts out many demons from one man, to v. 40, and heals a woman suffering from a flow of blood, and raises from the dead the daughter of Jairus.

units.la: Capitis noni partes principales sunt duæ: Quædam enim adhuc pertinent ad primam officij prophetici partem principalem, nimirum omnia illa quæ de Christo & discipulis narrantur usque ad v. 51. Quædam ad secundam Ministerij Christi partem referuntur: inde usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: The chief parts of chapter nine are two. Some things still pertain to the first chief part of the prophetic office, namely all those things that are narrated about Christ and the disciples up to v. 51. Some pertain to the second part of the ministry of Christ, from there to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Priore parte narrantur ista. 1 Emissio Apostolorum 12. ad prædicandum. 11 Iudicium Herodis de Christo, & studium videndi ipsum, v.7.8.9. 111 Reditus discipulorum, & Christi cum ipsis seceßus, in quo insigne illud miraculum pastionis 5000. hominum per 5. panes & duos pisces edidit: usque ad v. 18. 1 v Christi sciscitatio de iudiciis hominum de se, ut constaret de Apostolorum confessione, quam Petrus omnium nomine edidit: & prædi- ctio[?] passionis suæ, indeque deducta ad constantiam & tolerantiam exhortatio, usque ad v. 28. v Miraculum Christi, primo transfigurationis in monte, usque ad v. 37. deinde ejecti daemony [?] é puero quodam, usque ad v. 44. v I Dicta Christi, discipulos de passione iterum praemonentis, eosdemque ab ambitione dehortantis, usque ad v. 51.
units.tr: The first part narrates these things: 1 The sending out of the Apostles, chapter 12, to preach. II Herod's judgement about Christ, and his wish to see him, vv. 7, 8, 9. III The return of the disciples, and Christ's withdrawal with them, in which he performed that remarkable miracle of feeding 5000 men with five loaves and two fish, up to v. 18. IV Christ's questioning about what people judged him to be, so that the confession Peter made on behalf of all of them might be established; and his prediction of his passion, and from this the exhortation to steadfastness and endurance, up to v. 28. V The miracle of Christ, first the transfiguration on the mountain, up to v. 37; then the casting out of a demon from a certain boy, up to v. 44. VI The sayings of Christ, again forewarning the disciples about the passion and dissuading them from ambition, up to v. 51.

units.la: Hactenus fuit prima pars administrationis muneris Prophetici Christi: sequitur Altera,
units.tr: So far was the first part of the administration of Christ's prophetic office; the second follows.

units.la: DE POSTREMA CHRISTI HIE-rosolymam SUSCEPTA PROFECTIONE.
units.tr: Concerning Christ's final journey undertaken to Jerusalem

units.la: HANC profectionem copiose describit Lu-cas, commemorans quid ubique hinc inde in via docuerit, & quibus miraculis doctrinam confirmarit: ubi, & apud quos diverterit: quomodo a singulis sit exceptus: quo fructu docuerit: quis fuerit comitatus: qui praecipui ho-stes, &c.
units.tr: Luke describes this journey at length, recounting what Christ taught here and there along the way, and with what miracles he confirmed his teaching; where and with whom he lodged; how he was received by each person; what fruit his teaching bore; who accompanied him; who were the chief enemies, and so on.

units.la: SYNOPSIS ET SERIES HVIVS partis generalis.
units.tr: SYNOPSIS AND ORDER OF THIS GENERAL PART.

units.la: A quo: Discessus Christi é Galilaea in Samariam. Narratur hic Samaritanorum inhospitalitas, praeposterus discipulorum Zelus, & delectus comitum quorundam, &c: a v. 51. capitis noni usque ad eius finem. Per quae: per Iu-dæa: Cō-fide ra hic Discipulorum Christi Secundariorum ablegationem, nimirum 70. in Iudaeam: quo successu docuerint, & quomodo à Christo excepti sint, &c: cap. 10. Christi dicta, facta & eventa in illo itinere reliqua: in quibus eius sermones maximè memorabiles sunt. Disseruit autem Christus de cultu Dei Interno, de invocatione, fide, & poenitentia, cap.11. 12.13. 14. 15, Externo, de cavendo abusu divitiarum & scandalo, & studio orationis, cap. 16. 17.18. Documenta ista suis miraculis à Christo confirmantur. Ad quem, ad urbem Hierosolymorum: c.19.20.21.
units.tr: From where: Christ's departure from Galilee into Samaria. Here is related the inhospitality of the Samaritans, the misguided zeal of the disciples, and the choosing of certain companions, etc., from v. 51 of chapter 9 to its end. Through which places: through Judea. Consider here the sending out of the Seventy Disciples, namely the seventy into Judea: with what success they taught, and how they were received by Christ, etc. (chapter 10). The rest of Christ's sayings, deeds and events on that journey: in these his discourses are most memorable. Christ spoke about internal worship of God, namely invocation, faith and repentance (chapters 11, 12, 13, 14, 15), and about external worship: avoiding the abuse of riches and offence, and devotion to prayer (chapters 16, 17, 18). These teachings are confirmed by Christ with his miracles. To which place: to the city of Jerusalem (chapters 19, 20, 21).

units.la: Summa capitis decimi. Agitur de Ablegatione 70. discipulorum in Iudaeam: quibus cum gaudio reversis, Christus quoque spiritu exultans, tans, uans, Deo Patri cælesti gratias agit, quòd dignos & idoneos prædicationis Euangelicæ auditores elegerit, non huius mundi Sapientes (introductos postea ab ipso Euangelistâ, snb persona Legisperiti, de Lege disputantis) sed paruulos & infantes. (quorum typus est Maria Marthæ soror, verbum Dei ex Christi ore auidè & attente audiens). Partes sunt quatuor. 1. Eliguntur 70 discipuli, qui Christi faciem præcedunt, & docent. 11 Oratio Christi ad Patrem, qua gratias agit pro arcano electionis consilio, v. 21. 22. & ad discipulos, quorum felicitatem ostendit, ut constet quid nos in Christo habeamus, v. 23. 24. 111 Respondet Legisperito de vita æterna & de proximo, usque ad v. 38. 1v Apud Martham & Mariam diuertit, illam reprehendit, & hanc laudat.
units.tr: Summary of chapter ten. The subject is the sending out of the seventy disciples into Judea. When they return with joy, Christ too, exulting in the Spirit, gives thanks to God the heavenly Father that he has chosen as hearers fit and suitable for the Gospel preaching not the wise of this world (the evangelist himself later introduces them, in the person of a lawyer disputing about the Law), but babes and infants. (Mary, sister of Martha, who eagerly and attentively hears the word of God from Christ's mouth, is a type of them.) There are four parts. (1) The seventy disciples are chosen, who go before Christ's face and teach. (2) Christ's prayer to the Father, in which he gives thanks for the hidden counsel of the choosing (vv. 21, 22), and his words to the disciples, whose happiness he shows so that we may see what we have in Christ (vv. 23, 24). (3) He answers the lawyer about eternal life and about the neighbour, as far as v. 38. (4) He lodges with Martha and Mary, rebukes the one and praises the other.

units.la: Argumentum capitis x I. Christus Dominus ut cum suis mitissimus est: ita cum aduersariis, & hypocritis, acrem se declarat antagonistam: quod ut hactenus sæpe, ita & euidenter hoc præsenti capite apparet. Suos enim orare docet, & ut id confidenter faciant, hortatur. Hypocritas vero, dum criminantur opera suæ diuinitatis, animosè aggressus conuincit: signa pe-tentibus[?] negat, non veritus prauam generationem appellare. Grauius autem in hypocrisin inuehitur apud Pharisæum conuiuatus: quem ordinem non solum hypocritarum titulo ornat, sed reum quoque facit sanguinis innocenter ef-fusi. Partes quatuor. 1. De formula orationis, & orandi necessitate. 11 de curato dæmoniaco muto, & facti defensione: eaque occasione monet cauen-dam securitatem; nec non pronunciat qui sint beati,
units.tr: Argument of the chapter. 11. Christ the Lord, as he is most gentle with his own, so he shows himself a fierce opponent of adversaries and hypocrites; as often before, so clearly in this chapter this appears. For he teaches his followers to pray and urges them to do so with confidence. But the hypocrites, whom he accuses for the works of his divinity, he boldly assails and convicts; when they seek a sign, he refuses it, not shrinking from calling them an evil generation. Yet he inveighs more severely against hypocrisy when he is entertained by a Pharisee, a man whom he not only adorns with the title of hypocrite but also makes guilty of the blood of the innocent shed. There are four parts. (1) On the form of prayer and the necessity of praying. (2) On the dumb demoniac who was healed, and the defence of the deed; on this occasion he warns against security, and also pronounces who are blessed,

units.la: v.14. vsque ad v.29. III Sermo ad turbam, signum negans, praeter signum Ionae, Nineuitarum, Reginae Austri, vsque ad v.33. & de luce cognitionis Dei benignè cum aliis communicanda, vsque ad v.37. IV In prandio apud Pharisaeum reprehendit Pharisaeos & Scribas, & Legis interpretes propter vitiosos ipsorum mores.
units.tr: from v. 14 to v. 29. (3) His address to the crowd, refusing a sign except the sign of Jonah, of the Ninevites, of the Queen of the South, down to v. 33; and on the light of the knowledge of God, to be kindly shared with others, down to v. 37. (4) At a meal with a Pharisee he rebukes the Pharisees and the scribes and interpreters of the Law for their faulty morals.

units.la: CHRISTVS à Pharisæis digressus, captat nouam docendi occasionem, quam opportunè illi suppeditat turba ad audiendum auida. Tractat autem in capitis xii. initio idem argumentum, quod supra in prandio apud pharisæum: sed aliis auditoribus accommodatum. Nam discipulos hic praemonet, vt hypocrisin illam Pharisaicam vitent: cuius rei plura proponit argumenta vsque ad v.13. Deinde sollicitudinem huius vitæ carpit, in auaritiam inuectus, vsque ad v.31. Commendat autem curam quaerendi cælestia: de suo aduentu etiam praemonet, & quanta cum vigilantia eum nos oporteat expectare docet, à v.31. vsque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: Christ, having departed from the Pharisees, seizes a new occasion to teach, which the eager crowd offers him opportunely to hear. At the beginning of chapter 12 he treats the same subject as above at the Pharisee's meal, but adapted to other hearers. For here he first warns his disciples to avoid that Pharisaic hypocrisy, and sets out several arguments on this matter down to v. 13. Then he attacks anxiety about this life, inveighing against covetousness, down to v. 31. He commends the care of seeking heavenly things; he also forewarns of his own coming, and teaches with what vigilance we ought to wait for him, from v. 31 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Capitis xiii partes sunt quinque. 1. Ad poenitentiam hortatur Dominus auditores suos & studium pietatis. II Sanat mulierem incuruam, v.10. III Proponit duas parabolas: vnam de grano sinapis, alteram de fermento, v.18. IV. Iterum hortatur ad resipiscentiam & studium pietatis. v.23. V Exprobrat Hierosolymitanis incredulitatem, & poenas denunciat, v.31.
units.tr: Chapter 13 has five parts. (1) The Lord urges his hearers to repentance and to zeal for godliness. (2) He heals a bent woman, v. 10. (3) He proposes two parables: one of the grain of mustard seed, the other of the leaven, v. 18. (4) Again he urges repentance and zeal for godliness, v. 23. (5) He upbraids the Jerusalemites for their unbelief and announces punishments, v. 31.

units.la: Caput xiv duos locos habet. Prior complectitur historiam rerum gestarum in domo cuiusdam Pharisaei, vsque ad v.25. posterior itineris continuationem, in qua est illustris Chri-sti orasti oratio, de nostri abnegatione, & sequela Christi. Prior locus habet i Miraculum sana-ti hydropici. ii monet de modestia in accumbendo, v. 7. iii docet qui sint vocandi ad conuiuia.v. 12. denique utili anagoge hac omnia ad vitam æter-nam transfert: indicans inprimis operam esse dan-dam ne nostro vitio ab illo caelesti conuiuio excluda-mur. v. 15.
units.tr: Chapter 14 has two sections. The first contains the account of what was done in the house of a certain Pharisee, down to v. 25; the second is a continuation of the journey, in which is the famous discourse of Christ concerning our self-denial and the following of Christ. The first section contains (i) a miracle: the healing of a man with dropsy. (ii) He advises modesty in taking places at table, v. 7. (iii) He teaches who are to be invited to feasts, v. 12. Finally, by a useful application he transfers all these things to eternal life, showing above all that care must be taken lest through our fault we are shut out from that heavenly banquet, v. 15.

units.la: Cap. xv. Publicanis & peccatoribus ad Christum confluentibus, murmurant hypocri-tæ, rem Christo indignam iudicantes, damnant-que in ipso Christo patientiam. Hinc Christo opus est apologia: ut ostendat iustè se admit-tere peccatores. Quod factum tuetur triplici pa-rabola, prima est de oue perdita, usque ad v. 8. Secunda de drachma perdita & inuenta, usque ad v. 11. tertia de filio perdito.
units.tr: Chapter 15. Since tax collectors and sinners flock to Christ, the hypocrites murmur, judging the thing unworthy of Christ, and in Christ himself they condemn his patience. Hence Christ needs a defence, to show that he rightly receives sinners. This deed he upholds by a threefold parable: the first is of the lost sheep, down to v. 8; the second of the lost and found coin, down to v. 11; the third of the lost son.

units.la: Quinque ista capita. 11. 12. 13. 14. 15. hunc in mo-dum à Mose Pflachero connectuntur:
units.tr: These five chapters, 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15, are connected in this way by Moses Pflacher:

units.la: Internus Dei cultus de Innovatione, seu orationis dominicae formu-la, &c. cap. 11. Fidei adiunctis syncera & constanti confessio-ne veritatis, & repugnantibus sive impedimentis, ut est cura huius vitae nimia & avaritia & securitas in pietatis studio cap.12. Pænitentia: de pœnitentiæ agendæ causis Impellentibus: ut sint exempla tragica: similia patris familias excin-dentis arborem sterilem, & excludetis ma-lae fidei famulos: vaticinia de reiectione Iudæorum & vocatione Gentium, &c: cap.13. Impedietibus: cuiusmodi est vitiosus amor rerum & personarum. Rerum, ut honorum, & divitiarum amor. Personarum, tum aliorum potissimum sanguine coniunctorum, & sui ipsius in refugendo crucem & afflictiones, ad quas tamen nos tempestive compositos esse decebat: cap.14. Effectis: Quod resipiscentes non tantum a Deo in gratiam recipiantur, sed insuper etiam amplioribus donis ornati, summæ felicitatis participes reddantur, demonstrant suavissimæ Christi parabolæ. cap.15.
units.tr: Internal worship of God, concerning renewal, or the form of the Lord's Prayer, etc., chapter 11. Accompaniments of faith: sincere and constant confession of the truth, and the things that oppose or hinder it, such as excessive care for this life, avarice, and complacency in the pursuit of piety, chapter 12. Repentance: concerning the causes that impel to repentance, so that there are tragic examples, like the householder cutting down the barren tree and the servants of bad faith who are shut out; prophecies of the rejection of the Jews and the calling of the Gentiles, etc., chapter 13. Hindrances: such as a vicious love of things and of persons. Of things, such as love of honours and riches. Of persons, above all of blood relations, and of oneself in shunning the cross and afflictions, for which we ought to have been prepared in good time, chapter 14. Effects: that those who repent are not only received into God's grace but are also adorned with greater gifts and made partakers of the highest happiness, as Christ's most sweet parables demonstrate, chapter 15.

units.la: Sic fuit cultus internus potiss: sequitur ex-ternus.
units.tr: Thus the internal worship has been treated chiefly; there follows the external.

units.la: Cultus Dei ex-ternus est tum Fugiendorum: de cavendo Abusu divitiarum, sub per-sona iniqui dispensatoris, divitis epulonis, & Lazari men-dici. cap. 16. Scandalo, per virtutem fidei, historia de decem leprosis adumbratae, propter aduen-tum Christi novissimum. c. 17. Faciendorum: Exercitium orandi commen-datur ab effectis, adiun-ctis & causis. Huic ad scopum refertur parabola de iniquo iudice, Pharisaeo & Publicano: oblatio infan-tium, disputatio cum divite adolescente, &c. cap. 18.
units.tr: The external worship of God is both of things to be avoided, Avoiding: concerning guarding against the abuse of riches, under the figure of the unjust steward, the rich feaster and the beggar Lazarus, chapter 16. Scandal: through the power of faith, the story of the ten lepers, foreshadowing the Lord's final coming, chapter 17. And of things to be done, Practice: the exercise of prayer is commended from its effects, accompaniments and causes. To this end are referred the parable of the unjust judge, the Pharisee and the Publican, the offering of infants, the dispute with the rich young man, etc., chapter 18.

units.la: Cap. xvi. Dominus i proponit parabolam de dispensatore iniusto, usque ad v. 16. ii Monet de efficacia Evangelij & de autoritate Legis. v. 16. 17. 8. iii Proponit historiam de divite epulone & mendico Lazaro.
units.tr: Chapter 16. The Lord (i) proposes the parable of the unjust steward, to v. 16; (ii) warns of the efficacy of the Gospel and the authority of the Law, v. 16, 17, 8; (iii) proposes the history of the rich feaster and the beggar Lazarus.

units.la: Capitis xvii partes sunt quinque. Do-minus i discipulos monet de cavendis scandalis, & quomodo gerere se debeant erga afficientem iniuria, & deprecantem culpam, usque ad v. 5. ii ostendit quanta sit vis fidei. v. 5. 6. iii Declarat Deum gratiam suam nemini tanquam ex ipsius merito debere: usque ad v. 11. iii Sanat decem leprosos usque ad v. 20. v Docet de adventu regni Dei.
units.tr: Chapter 17 has five parts. The Lord (i) warns the disciples to beware of scandals, and how they ought to behave towards one who wrongs them and asks forgiveness, to v. 5; (ii) shows how great the power of faith is, v. 5, 6; (iii) declares that God owes his grace to no one as if it were due to his merit, to v. 11; (iii) heals the ten lepers, to v. 20; (v) teaches about the coming of the kingdom of God.

units.la: Propositio capitis xviii est: Omnes qui-cunque tandem constanti fide Dominum invocaverint per Christum exaudiendos; nec obsta-[?] rehic paupertatem,infantiam,diuitias, aliaque. Atque meritum Christi morte perfici: miraculis autem ipsius hanc doctrinam confirmari, &c. Partes sunt quinque. 1 Fidei & verae innuocationis naturam nos edocet, quae dum constans & indefessa est, tandem impetrat a Domino postulata, usque ad vers. 15. 11 Iubet sibi adduci puerulos. v. 15.16.17. 111 Diuitibus monstrat viam ad salutem, quam dum negligit dives ille, Christo occasionem praebet differendi de difficultate salvandi divites, & confessoribus suis promittendi remunerationem, usque ad v. 31. 1 v Iterum praedicit Apostolis passionem & resurrectionem suam, usque ad v. 35. v Caecum quendam iuxta Ierechuntem sanat.
units.tr: The proposition of chapter 18 is: all who at last invoke the Lord with constant faith will be heard through Christ; nor does poverty, infancy, riches or anything else stand in the way here. And the merit of Christ is made complete by his death, but this doctrine is confirmed by his miracles, etc. There are five parts. 1. It teaches us the nature of faith and true invocation, which, while it is constant and tireless, at last obtains from the Lord what it asks, to v. 15. 11. He orders little children to be brought to him, v. 15, 16, 17. 111. He shows the rich the way to salvation, which that rich man neglects; Christ thereby gives occasion to discuss the difficulty of the rich being saved, and to promise reward to those who confess him, to v. 31. 1V. Again he foretells to the Apostles his passion and resurrection, to v. 35. V. He heals a certain blind man near Jericho.

units.la: Sic fuit terminus per quem: sequitur de profectionis Christi termino ad quem, nimirum ad urbem Hierosolymorum. Hic notetur Christi In urbem Hierof: ingressus: Christus Ierechunti a Zachæo primum exceptus hospitio, urbem deinde ingressus, honorifica acclamatione excipitur a populo. c.19. Commoratio in urbe: oratio Christi Contra adversarios, variis de rebus habitus. cap.20. Ad discipulos, propheticus, de excidio urbis & consummatione seculi. cap.21.
units.tr: Thus the point by which has been treated; concerning the point to which Christ's journey was directed, namely the city of Jerusalem. Here note Christ's entry into the city of Jerusalem: Christ, first received with hospitality by Zacchaeus at Jericho, then entering the city, is welcomed by the people with an honourable acclamation, chapter 19. His stay in the city: Christ's speech against his adversaries, on various matters, chapter 20. To the disciples, prophetic, concerning the destruction of the city and the end of the age, chapter 21.

units.la: Capitis xix propositio est: Christus verus Rex regnum suum auspicaturus est, non ex discipulorum aut turbae sententia: sed eo modo, quo prophetae praedixere, & qui officio Christi competens est. Partes quatuor sunt.
units.tr: The proposition of chapter 19 is: Christ, the true King, is about to inaugurate his kingdom not according to the opinion of the disciples or of the crowd, but in the manner the prophets foretold and which befits the office of Christ. There are four parts.

units.la: 1 In Ierechunte vocatur Zacheus. 11 In via disserit per parabolam de officio fidelium, quibus tanquam seruis Regis, commissa sunt mina ad vsuram spiritualem: a v. 11. vsque ad 28. 111 Ingreditur vt Rex Hierosolymam, & flet super ea vrbe. vsque ad v. 14. 1 V Eicit e templo vendentes & ementes.
units.tr: 1. In Jericho Zacchaeus is called. 11. On the way he discourses, by parable, on the duty of the faithful, to whom, as servants of the King, the minas are committed for spiritual usury, from v. 11 to 28. 111. He enters Jerusalem as King and weeps over that city, to v. 14. 1V. He casts out of the temple those who sell and buy.

units.la: Caput x x. totum ἀγωνιστικόν [?] est: habet enim varias quæstiones; quibus aduersarij conati sunt Christum irretire. Et quanquam omnes omnia moueant: tamen Christus feliciter omnium conatus euadit: imo vi veritatis ipsos aduersarios sic concludit, vt victi omnes discedant. Membra sunt sex. 1 Quæstio de iure factorum Christi, & de baptismo Iohannis. vsque ad v.9. 11 Per Parabolam de vinea Domini, conqueritur de primorum impietate: vsque ad v. 20. 111 Respondet ad quæstionem de censu, vsque ad v. 27. 1V Asserit resurrectionem carnis contra Sadducæos, vsque ad v. 41. v Dominus monet quæstionem de Christo, quomodo sit Filius Davidis: vsque ad v. 45. V1 Monet discipulos ne imitentur Scribarum hypocrisin.
units.tr: Chapter 20 is entirely agonistic [ἀγωνιστικόν]: for it contains various questions by which the adversaries tried to ensnare Christ. And although they all move every stone, Christ escapes all their attempts successfully; indeed, by the power of truth he so refutes the adversaries that all depart defeated. There are six sections. 1. A question about the authority for Christ's deeds, and about the baptism of John, to v. 9. 11. By the parable of the Lord's vineyard, he complains of the impiety of the first tenants, to v. 20. 111. He answers the question about the tribute, to v. 27. 1V. He asserts the resurrection of the flesh against the Sadducees, to v. 41. V. The Lord proposes a question about Christ, how he is the Son of David, to v. 45. V1. He warns the disciples not to imitate the hypocrisy of the scribes.

units.la: Capitis x x i. partes sunt tres. 1 Dominus laudat oblationem viduæ. 11 Prædicit interitum templi & urbis, nec non signa præcessura extremum iudicium, a v. 5. vsq; ad 36. 111 Narratiuncula generalis de factis Domini per illos dies quibus Hierosolymæ commoratus est sub tempus suæ passionis.
units.tr: Chapter 21 has three parts. 1. The Lord praises the widow's offering. 11. He foretells the destruction of the temple and the city, and also the signs that will precede the final judgment, from v. 5 to 36. 111. A brief general narrative of the Lord's deeds during those days in which he stayed in Jerusalem near the time of his passion.

units.la: Hactenus de Prophetico Christi munere, sequitur
units.tr: Thus far on the prophetic office of Christ; there follows

units.la: DE ADMINISTRATIONE muneris Sacerdotalis.
units.tr: On the Administration of the Priestly Office.

units.la: Filius Dei officium suum propheticum studiosè[?] est executus hactenus: docuit enim nos quæ sit voluntas Dei patris: idque præstitit statim post tentationes in deserto exorsus: præstat idem adhuc & præstabit ad finem vsque mundi per pia organa, vt olim per Apostolos. Orauit etiam & intercessit pro mortalium genere, vt sup.cap. 6. & 9. vidimus. Idem etiam constanter apud Deum Patrem adhuc suis præstat,vt est Rom. 8. 33. Qui est ad dextram Dei, & qui intercedit pro nobis.
units.tr: The Son of God has hitherto diligently carried out his prophetic office. For he taught us what the will of God the Father is, and he began this immediately after the temptations in the desert. He still does the same and will do so until the end of the world, through faithful instruments, as he did formerly through the Apostles. He also prayed and interceded for the human race, as we saw above in chapters 6 and 9. He also still does this constantly before God the Father for his own, as in Rom. 8.33: "who is at the right hand of God, and who also intercedes for us."

units.la: Verum superest longè maximum Christi officium: puram scilicet offerre hostiam Deo Patri pro electis,vt est Eph: 5. 25. & Heb. 9.28. Ad hoc omnia reliqua referuntur. Ob id natus est,docuit, edidit miracula. Ob id ipsum ascendit Ierosolymam subiturus mortem: inde acturus triumphū contra Satanam & mortem.
units.tr: But by far the greatest office of Christ remains: namely, to offer a pure sacrifice to God the Father for the elect, as in Eph. 5.25 and Heb. 9.28. All the rest is referred to this. For this he was born, taught, and performed miracles. For this very reason he went up to Jerusalem, about to undergo death, and from there was to celebrate a triumph over Satan and death.

units.la: Sequentibus igitur duobus capitibus, nimirum vigesimo secundo & vigesimo tertio narratur historia passionis Domini: cuius principes partes sunt tres: PRIMA est præparatio seu effecta destinata quæ passionem Domini proximè antecesserunt, & ad illam quoquo modo destinata fuerunt: vsque ad versum 39. capitis vigesimi secundi. SECUNDA est narratio ipsarum perpessionum, vsque ad versum 50. capitis sequentis. TERTIA est narratio euentorum proximè sequutorum, à v.50. capitis 23. ad eius vsque finem.
units.tr: In the following two chapters, namely the twenty-second and the twenty-third, the history of the Lord's passion is related. Its principal parts are three. The FIRST is the preparation, that is, the events destined for the passion, which immediately preceded the Lord's passion and were in some way ordained for it, up to verse 39 of chapter twenty-two. The SECOND is the narration of the sufferings themselves, up to verse 50 of the following chapter. The THIRD is the narration of the events immediately following, from verse 50 of chapter 23 to its end.

units.la: Præparatio prima est Sacerdotum & Scribarum ad supplicium Domino afferendum, vsque ad v. 3.capitis 23. Secunda est præparatio Iudæ ad Dominum prodendum, vsque ad v. 7.
units.tr: The first preparation is that of the priests and scribes for delivering the Lord up to punishment, up to verse 3 of chapter 23. The second is the preparation of Judas for betraying the Lord, up to verse 7.

units.la: Tertia est varia & multiplex discipulorum præparatio 1 ad supplicium Domini patienter atque cum gaudio ferendum, usque ad v. 21. 11 præparatio eorundem, ne nimis offendantur proditione Iudæ, usque ad v. 24. 111 præparatio discipulorum per dehortationem ab ambitione, usque ad v. 22. 1V per promissionem gaudiorum & gloriæ in regno Christi, usque ad v. 31. V per promissionem perseverantiæ in fide, usque ad v. 33. VI Singularis præparatio Petri per prædictionem negationis, usque ad v. 35: VII iterum generalis præparatio Apostolorum, per prædictionem imminentis persecutionis, usque ad v. 39.
units.tr: The third is the varied and manifold preparation of the disciples: (1) for bearing the Lord's punishment patiently and with joy, up to verse 21; (2) their preparation, so that they would not be too offended by the betrayal of Judas, up to verse 24; (3) their preparation by dissuasion from ambition, up to verse 22; (4) by the promise of joys and glory in the kingdom of Christ, up to verse 31; (5) by the promise of perseverance in faith, up to verse 33; (6) the singular preparation of Peter through the prediction of his denial, up to verse 35; (7) again a general preparation of the Apostles, through the prediction of impending persecution, up to verse 39.

units.la: ipsas sustinuit PASSIONES Christus tum in Horto: tum in Iudicio ecclesiastico & politico: & denique in Loco supplicij:
units.tr: Christ endured the SUFFERINGS themselves: partly in the garden, partly in the ecclesiastical and civil judgment, and finally at the place of execution.

units.la: Secunda igitur capitis vigesimi secundi parte narrantur ea quæ passus est Dominus in horto seu monte olearum, à v. 39. usque ad 54. Sunt-que duo potissimum: Primum quidem perpessio interna, ingens nimirum anxietas ex horrore pleni sensus iræ Dei paulò post in cruce experiundi, usque ad v. 47. Deinde externa Iudæ proditio, & quæ eam excepit captio à ministris magistratuum Hierosolymitanorum; usque ad v. 54.
units.tr: Therefore in the second part of chapter twenty-two are narrated the things the Lord suffered in the garden, or on the Mount of Olives, from verse 39 to 54. There are two chief ones. The first is the inner suffering, namely the great anguish arising from the horror of a full sense of God's wrath, which he was to experience shortly afterwards on the cross, up to verse 47. Then the outer suffering: the betrayal by Judas, and the arrest that followed by the servants of the magistrates of Jerusalem, up to verse 54.

units.la: Tertia huius capitis parte narrantur ea quæ passus est Dominus in domo pontificis maximi, quorum tria sunt. Primum, quòd negatus fuit à Petro, usque ad v. 63: alterum, quòd illusus fuit à famulis pontificum, usque ad v. 66. tertium, quòd à concilio sacerdotum falso crimine blasphemiæ damnatus fuit ad supplicium crucis, usque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: In the third part of this chapter are narrated the things the Lord suffered in the house of the high priest, of which there are three. First, that he was denied by Peter, up to verse 63; second, that he was mocked by the servants of the high priests, up to verse 66; third, that he was condemned by the council of priests on a false charge of blasphemy to the punishment of the cross, up to the end of the chapter.

units.la: Posteaquam Christus à senioribus populi sui (quemadmodum supra cap. 9. & 17. prædixit) reprobatus est, nunc quoque à Gentibus reprobatur, cuius rei in capite vigesimo tertio texitur historia: in quo sunt primo quidem ea quæ coram politicis iudicibus perpessus est Christus, Pilato nimirum, apud quem à primoribus Iudæorum accusatur falso crimine seditionis: ( usque ad v. 6.) & Herode, usque ad v. 13. Inde continatur narratio eorum quæ passus est Dominus coram Pilato; quod nimirum primò comparatus fuit cum latrone Barabba, usque ad v. 21. secundò, quod magnis ac furiosis clamoribus postulatus fuit ad crucem: v 21. 22. 23. ad quam à Pilato damnatur, v. 24. & latroni Barabbæ, tanquam minus innocens post ponitur, v. 25.
units.tr: After Christ had been rejected by the elders of his people (as he foretold above in chapters 9 and 17), he is now also rejected by the Gentiles, and the history of this is woven in chapter twenty-three. In it there is, first, what Christ suffered before the civil judges, namely Pilate, before whom he is accused by the leading men of the Jews of the false charge of sedition (up to verse 6), and Herod, up to verse 13. Then follows the narration of what the Lord suffered before Pilate: first, that he was set alongside the robber Barabbas, up to verse 21; second, that with loud and furious shouts he was demanded for the cross, verses 21, 22 and 23, for which he is condemned by Pilate, verse 24, while Barabbas, as less innocent, is placed after him, verse 25.

units.la: De hinc ea, quæ Domino ad supplicium capitis damnato contigerunt in itinere ad locum supplicij commemorantur usque ad v. 33. in quo itinere sequitur Christum Simon quidam Cyrenæus ferens crucem Christi coactus, v. 26. sponte sequuntur mulieres lamentantes, quæ corriguntur à Iesu: usque ad v. 32. accedunt duo malefici ad idem supplicij genus protracti, v. 32.
units.tr: Next are recorded the things that befell the Lord, condemned to capital punishment, on the way to the place of execution, up to verse 33. On this way Simon of Cyrene, compelled, follows Christ carrying the cross, verse 26; women follow him of their own accord, lamenting, and are corrected by Jesus, up to verse 32; two malefactors are led to the same kind of punishment, verse 32.

units.la: Passiones in loco supplicij sunt, quod crucifixus inter duos latrones coactus est videre direptionem vestium suarum, & sannis exceptus fuit & conuitiis proscissus à variis personis; usque ad v. 44. tandem post miraculum tenebrarum & veli templi diffissi, Christi mors describitur, v. 46. & poenitentia (centurionis ac turbæ. v. 47. 48. quarum rerum testes fuerunt quidam fideles stantes é longinquo v. 49.
units.tr: The sufferings at the place of execution are these: crucified between two robbers, he was forced to see the division of his garments, and he was received with jeers and insults from various persons, up to verse 44. Finally, after the miracle of the darkness and the tearing of the temple veil, Christ's death is described, verse 46, and the repentance of the centurion and the crowd, verses 47 and 48. Witnesses of these things were certain faithful ones standing at a distance, verse 49.

units.la: Sequuta passionem est Sepultura Domini, procurata à Iosepho Arimathaensi, à v. 50. vsque ad finem capitis.
units.tr: Following the passion is the burial of the Lord, procured by Joseph of Arimathea, from verse 50 to the end of the chapter.

units.la: De Munere Regio.
units.tr: On the Kingly Office.

units.la: QUÆ in prima huius libri parte narrata sunt de Domini conceptione & natiuitate, nec non de vita eius priuata; hoc est, de persona Christi & eius ad officium præparatione; sunt tanquam commune fundamentum, cui cætera quæ ad of-ficium spectant, innituntur. Ut enim omni suo officio fungi rectè Dominus posset: taliter ipsum concipi atque nasci oportuit, ut in principio huius historiæ describitur. Cætera verò quæ deinceps huc usque narrata fuerunt, aut ad officium ipsius propheticum, aut ad Sacerdota-le spectant.
units.tr: The things narrated in the first part of this book concerning the conception and birth of the Lord, and also concerning his private life—that is, concerning the person of Christ and his preparation for the office—are like a common foundation on which the rest of what pertains to the office rests. For in order that the Lord might rightly perform every part of his office, it was necessary that he be conceived and born in the way described at the beginning of this history. The things narrated after that, up to this point, pertain either to his prophetic office or to his priestly office.

units.la: Nunc autem hoc cap. xxiv & ultimo, ea describuntur, quæ inchoationem seu primordia muneris Regij concernunt. Partes capitis principales duæ sunt: Prima de Resurrectione: secunda de Ascensione. Ad resurrectionem Christi quod attinet: demonstratur illa primo testimonio duorum Angelorum, mulieribus cupientibus honestius perficere cœptam sepulturam. Ideoque ostendit quam ar-denter & sollicitè ad sepulchrum confluxerint: quæ isthic rerum statum repererint: quo item animo, illi relata admiserint: usque ad v. 13. Secundò demon-stratur resurrectio ab apparitione ipsius Domini, facta duobus discipulis Emaunta petentibus, usque ad v. 36.
