units.tr: as far as verse 16. (2) The disciples' night voyage, which was dangerous, and their deliverance by Christ, who miraculously walked on the sea: as far as verse 22. (3) The Jews, moved by a desire for bodily goods, which they sought from Christ on the occasion of the preceding miracle, hasten with him to Capernaum, both by boat and on foot. The Lord rebukes their perverse eagerness and urges them to seek rather the spiritual food of the soul. There is described a discussion about eating the mystical flesh of Christ by faith, and the outcome of the discussion follows, namely the defection of the Jews, with only the true disciples persevering.

units.la: TERTIVM MEMBRVM IN HISTORIA tertij itineris Christi Hierosolymam ad festum Scenopegiæ, seu tabernaculorum.
units.tr: THE THIRD PART OF THE HISTORY: the third journey of Christ to Jerusalem, for the feast of Tabernacles, or Booths.

units.la: Aduentus ad hoc festum: & quid sub eius initium, medium & finem à Christo dictum-gestumque sit: cap. 7. Hic notetur Christi. Commoratio: quid durante illo festo Hierosolymis, Dixerit, oratio [?]ἀγώνισμα (cui historia adulteræ præmissa est) de vera luce: de priuato in propria causa testimonio, de libertate spirituali, &c: cap. 8. Fecerit: Curatio cæci nati, & quæ eam consecuta est, Actio, inter Christum, cæcum natum & Aduersarios: cap. 9. Dixerit oratio de Christi officio pastorali, & persona, quod sit Messias, Dei Filius, & mundi saluator. cap. 10. Discessus ex urbe in agrum, & vicinam regionem traniordaninam, vbi Lazarum à mortuis excitauit. cap. 11.
units.tr: The arrival at this feast, and what Christ said and did at its beginning, middle and end: chapter 7. Here note: Christ's stay. What he said during that feast at Jerusalem: Dixerit, a discourse [?ἀγώνισμα] (preceded by the story of the adulteress) about the true light, about a testimony given privately in one's own cause, about spiritual liberty, etc.: chapter 8. What he did: Fecerit, the healing of the man born blind, and what followed from it, an action between Christ, the blind man born, and his adversaries: chapter 9. What he said: Dixerit, a discourse on Christ's pastoral office and person, that he is the Messiah, the Son of God and the Saviour of the world: chapter 10. His departure from the city into the countryside and the neighbouring region beyond the Jordan, where he raised Lazarus from the dead: chapter 11.

units.la: Cap. v 11. Iesus Galilaeâ Hierosolymam reuertitur ad festi Tabernaculorum solennitatem celebrandam, ibique aliquandiu vitandi periculi causa clam agens, postmodum in templum media festiuitate progressus, coram frequentissima hominum multitudine docet, publicè de doctrinae suae autoritate testificans, & Iudaeorum sanguinolenta consilia reprehendens. Vbi disputatio de Sabbatho capite quinto mota hîc renouatur, si nulque [?] toto capite varia hominum de se iudicia refutat Dominus, & consilia cruenta Iudaeorum diuinae prouidentiae beneficio ita euadit, vt cum proceres populi Iudaici ministros suos ad capiendum Christum ablegarent, illi ex hostibus amici facti re infecta redeant, & conciliabulum illud dissoluatur. Partes capitis sunt quatuor. I Sermo cognatorum cum Christo habitus ante festum, vsque ad v. II. II Sermo populi de eo in festo, antequam se conspiciendum praeberet. v. 11. 12. 13. III Sermo Christi in templo habitus cum Iudaeis festo iam medio, a v. 14 vsque ad 37. IV Sermo ipsius habitus ad populum die festi vltimo, vna cum euentu, a v. 37. vsque ad finem.
units.tr: Chapter 11 (sic: 7 to 10). Jesus returns from Galilee to Jerusalem to celebrate the solemnity of the feast of Tabernacles. There, for some time, he acts secretly for the sake of avoiding danger, but afterwards, when the festival is half over, he goes up into the temple and teaches a very large crowd of people, bearing public witness to the authority of his teaching and rebuking the bloody plans of the Jews. Here the dispute about the Sabbath, raised in chapter 5, is renewed; and throughout the whole chapter the Lord refutes the various opinions of people about himself, and by the favour of divine providence he escapes the bloody plans of the Jews in such a way that, when the leaders of the Jewish people sent their servants to seize Christ, those men, from enemies made friends, return with nothing done, and that council is dissolved. The parts of the chapter are four. I. A conversation of his relatives with Christ, held before the feast, as far as verse 11. II. A conversation of the people about him at the feast, before he showed himself to be seen: verses 11, 12, 13. III. A discourse of Christ held in the temple with the Jews, the feast now half over: from verse 14 to 37. IV. His discourse addressed to the people on the last day of the feast, together with the outcome: from verse 37 to the end.

units.la: Capite octauo primò Actionem quandam inter Christum & Pharisaeos ex occasione mulieris in adulterio deprehensa natam describit Euangelista, quomodo Pharisaei de condemnanda vel absoluenda ea Christum interrogent, & quid Christus respondeat: vsque ad v. 12. Deinde prolixum describitur colloquium Iesu cum Iudaeis, in quo de officio Christi, de vera libertate filiorum Abrahae, & quinam sint veri filij Abrahae, de diuinitate uem Christi [?] vehementissima contentione ita disceptatur, ut Iu-dæi à verbis ad manifestam crudelitatem descen-dant, in ipso sacratissimo templo Christum lapidibus obruturi, nisi eorum sæuitiam declinasset.
units.tr: In chapter 8 the Evangelist first describes an action between Christ and the Pharisees, arising from the occasion of a woman caught in adultery: how the Pharisees ask Christ whether she should be condemned or acquitted, and what Christ answers, as far as verse 12. Then a long conversation between Jesus and the Jews is described, in which, about the office of Christ, about the true liberty of the sons of Abraham, and who are the true sons of Abraham, and about the divinity of Christ, the matter is debated with the most violent contention, so that the Jews descend from words to open cruelty, about to stone Christ in the most sacred temple itself, unless he had escaped their savagery.

units.la: Nono capite continetur historia de sanato cæ-co à natiuitate. Ac primùm exponuntur miraculi huius occasio & circumstantiæ, usque ad v. 8. Deinde quomodo hæc res innotuerit Pharisæis, usque ad v. 14. Tertiò, quomodo Pharisæi inqui-sierint de rei gestæ veritate, & quomodo cum sanato illo altercati sint super Christo, usque ad v. 35. Quartò, quomodo Christus illi sanato se plenius patefecerit, usque ad v. 39. Postremò, quomodo Christus Pharisæis cæcitatem voluntariam exprobrarit.
units.tr: The ninth chapter contains the story of the man born blind who was healed. First the occasion and circumstances of this miracle are set out, as far as verse 8. Then how this matter became known to the Pharisees, as far as verse 14. Thirdly, how the Pharisees inquired into the truth of the deed, and how they quarrelled with the man who had been healed about Christ, as far as verse 35. Fourthly, how Christ revealed himself more fully to the man who had been healed, as far as verse 39. Lastly, how Christ rebuked the Pharisees for their wilful blindness.

units.la: Capite x. parte priore, de officio & beneficio suis sub figura Pastoris concionatur Christus, quod ipse sit ostium ad ovile Domini, Pastor ovium fidelis, qui summa fide eas curet, pascat, regat, protegat, & vitam æternam largiatur: quæque sint illi, quas pro suis ovibus agnoscat. Quam concionem non pari modo Iudæi excipiunt, quibusdam calumniantibus, aliis vero defendentibus eam: usque ad v. 22. Secundò, controversia in festo Encæniorum inter Iudæos & Christum agitata describitur, quæ fuit de Persona, ac potissimum Divinitate eius, num videlicet Dei Filius, & unum cum Patre sit, an secus. Affirmat hoc Christus, negant Iudæi & execrantur, ut blasphemiam lapidatione vindicandam. Christus tandem suam argumentis tuetur. Ob quam rem in periculum vitæ venisset, nisi trans Iordanem (quo deinde multi ad eum confluxerunt) secessisset.
units.tr: In the first part of chapter 10, Christ preaches, under the figure of a Shepherd, about his office and benefits: that he is the door to the sheepfold of the Lord, the faithful Shepherd of the sheep, who with the greatest faithfulness cares for them, feeds, rules and protects them, and bestows eternal life; and about those whom he acknowledges as his own sheep. This sermon is not received in the same way by the Jews: some slander it, while others defend it: as far as verse 22. Secondly, a controversy at the feast of Dedication between the Jews and Christ is described, which concerned his person, and especially his divinity: namely whether he is the Son of God and one with the Father, or not. Christ affirms this; the Jews deny it and curse him, to be punished by stoning as blasphemy. Christ at last defends his claim with arguments. Because of this he would have come into danger of his life, had he not withdrawn beyond the Jordan (where many afterwards came together to him).

units.la: Capite xi. continetur historia Lazari à Christo excitati è morte: quod miraculum à Iohanne descriptum est vltimum & speciosissimum.
units.tr: Chapter 11 contains the story of Lazarus, raised by Christ from death: a miracle described by John as the last and most splendid.

units.la: Partes principales duae sunt; in quarum priore Iohannes historiam morbi, mortis, & resuscitationis Lazari texit, vsque ad v.45. In posteriore, Concilium Pharisaeorum, eorundemque sanguinolentam aduersus Christum consultationem, & decretum scelera-tum describit. Summa prioris membri haec est: Cum Lazarus Bethaniensis morbo lethali decum-beret; sorores legatione ad Iesum missa, ipsius & adventum & auxilium expetunt. Iesus, data opera, adventum & auxilium vltra mortem vsque Lazari differt: quo iam in agone existente, Christus re cum discipulis communicata in Iudaeam redit. Cuius adventum Martha primo, dehinc Maria, percipientes, adeunt ipsum, & fratris mortem non sine lachrymis exponunt. Vtramque solatur Dominus, eisque spem futurae resuscitationis faciens, ad monu-mentum vadit: vbi praemissa ad Patrem caelestem precatione Lazarum quatriduanum, spectante magna multitudine Iudaeorum, voce sua e sepulcro evocat: qui solutis vinculis mortis e monumento rediuiuus prodit. Posterioris partis sententia est: Illius miraculi virtute multos ad fidem in Christum excitatos: quosdam vero splendore eius magis obcaecatos, re ad Pharisaeos delata, in ipsorum congre-gatione, post multam consultationem, tandem in Caiaphae Pontificis sententiam itum esse pleno assensu, vt ad mortem rapiatur Christus, ex eoque die occasionem ab ipsis captatam, hoc suum decretum exequendi. Right page: [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: There are two principal parts. In the first, John weaves together the history of Lazarus' sickness, death and resurrection, as far as verse 45. In the second, he describes the council of the Pharisees, their bloody deliberation against Christ, and the wicked decree. The summary of the first part is this: when Lazarus of Bethany lay sick with a deadly disease, his sisters, having sent a message to Jesus, ask for both his coming and his help. Jesus, purposely, delays his coming and help until Lazarus is dead; then, when Lazarus is already in his last struggle, Christ, having shared the matter with his disciples, returns to Judea. Martha first, and then Mary, learning of his coming, go to him and explain their brother's death not without tears. The Lord comforts both of them and, giving them hope of a future resurrection, goes to the tomb; there, after a prayer to the heavenly Father, he calls Lazarus, four days dead, out of the sepulchre with his voice, while a great crowd of Jews looks on; and he comes out alive from the tomb, his grave-clothes loosed. The sense of the second part is this: by the power of that miracle many were roused to faith in Christ, but some, being more blinded by its brilliance, reported the matter to the Pharisees; and in their assembly, after much deliberation, at last, with full assent, they agreed to the sentence of Caiaphas the High Priest, that Christ should be put to death; and from that day they sought an opportunity to carry out this their decree. Right page: [illegible, ~20 letters]

units.la: QUARTUM MEMBRUM, DE quarto & postremo Christi ingressu in Hierosolymam, & quid in urbe & circa eam gesserit, & perpessus sit.
units.tr: THE FOURTH PART, concerning Christ's fourth and last entry into Jerusalem, and what he did and suffered in the city and around it.

units.la: Propheticum praecipuè, ut sunt Christi Facta: nempe Ingressus in urbem regius: cap.12. Lorio[?] pedum humilis atque demissa. cap.13. Dicta inter Cœnandum: Oratio Christi consolatoria, cap.14. Egrediundum in hortum, oratio eius ad Discipulos Adhortatoria, ad constantem in fide & officio perseverantiam.c.15. Consolatoria, contra persecutiones imminentes.c.16. Deum patrem precatoria pro se ipso, discipulos & totā Ecclesiā. cap.17. Sacerdotale: Passiones in Horto & atrio Pontificis: quibus etiam accedunt acta quaedam in Praetorio Pilati. cap.18. Praetorio Præsidis & loco supplicij atque sepulturæ. cap.19. Regium: Resurrectio Christi revelata discipulis Versantibus in Iudæa, & adhuc Hierosolymis agentibus. cap.20. Revertis in Galilæam, & ad mare Tyberiadis piscantibus.
units.tr: Chiefly prophetic, as the deeds of Christ are: namely, the royal entry into the city: ch. 12. The humble washing of the feet: ch. 13. The sayings at supper, Christ's words of comfort: ch. 14. Going out into the garden, his exhortation to the disciples to remain steadfast in faith and duty: ch. 15. Words of comfort against the persecutions at hand: ch. 16. Prayer to God the Father for himself, for the disciples and for the whole Church: ch. 17. The priestly: the passion in the garden and in the high priest's court, to which are added certain acts in Pilate's praetorium: ch. 18. The governor's praetorium, the place of execution and the burial: ch. 19. The royal: the resurrection of Christ revealed to the disciples who were staying in Judea and still at Jerusalem: ch. 20. Returning to Galilee and fishing by the Sea of Tiberias: ch. 20.

units.la: Cap. x I I. Primùm narratur quomodo Domi-nus coena exceptus sit Bethaniæ, & quomodo in illa coena à Maria sorore Lazari unctus sit: quidque inde euenerit: vsque ad v. 12. Deinde, quomodo Hierosolymam vectus asello, latis populi acclamationibus & congratulationibus exceptus sit: & quid inde euenerit, vsque ad v. 20. Tertiò narratur sermo eius quem ad discipulos habuit de sua morte, item de sui abnegatione & confessione, item de luce verbisui, vsque ad v. 37. Quartò exponitur causa,cur plerique in eum non crediderint, & cur quidam ex primoribus non ausi sint eum confiteri, vsque ad v. 44. Postremò narratur sermo Domini de fide & incredulitate: nempe cur merito in ipsum credendum sit, & vnde fides illa oriatur: & cur increduli merito condemnentur.
units.tr: Chapter 12. First it is narrated how the Lord was received at a dinner in Bethany, and how at that meal he was anointed by Mary, the sister of Lazarus, and what followed from this, up to v. 12. Then, how he was brought to Jerusalem riding on an ass and received with the people's loud acclamations and congratulations, and what followed from this, up to v. 20. Thirdly, his discourse to the disciples is narrated: about his death, about self-denial and confession, and about the light of his words, up to v. 37. Fourthly, the reason is set out why many did not believe in him, and why some of the leaders did not dare to confess him, up to v. 44. Lastly, the Lord's discourse about faith and unbelief is narrated: namely why he is rightly to be believed, whence that faith arises, and why unbelievers are rightly condemned.

units.la: Capitis x i i i partes sunt tres: 1 (Christus à cœna nouam actionem exorsus, pedes discipulis lauat, quidque hac lotione intendere velit, prolixè declarat, eum ad humilitatè & mutuò miserendi promptitudinem suo exemplo eas hortatur: vsque ad v. 18. 11 Proditionem Iudæ prædicit, & certo iudicio, quis sit ille Proditor, designat, nempe Iudas Iscarioth: qui à cœna surgens ad concilium Pharisæorum instituti sui expediendi causa pergit: vsque ad v. 31. 111 Postea reliquos discipulos ad mutuam charitatem hortari incipit, simulque non obscurè de passione sua iam instante loquitur: cumque iactaret Petrus suam apud Dominum perseuerandi voluntatem intrepidam; (Christus ei futuram abnegationis lapsum prædicit.
units.tr: Chapter 13 has three parts. (1) Christ, beginning a new action after supper, washes the disciples' feet, and explains at length what he intends by this washing, exhorting them by his example to humility and to a ready mutual compassion, up to v. 18. (2) He foretells Judas's betrayal and, with certain judgment, points out who that traitor is, namely Judas Iscariot, who rises from supper and goes to the council of the Pharisees to carry out his own plan, up to v. 31. (3) Afterwards he begins to exhort the remaining disciples to mutual love, and at the same time speaks not obscurely of his passion, now at hand; and when Peter boasted of his fearless resolve to persevere with the Lord, Christ foretells Peter's future fall into denial.

units.la: Deinceps per tria capita, videlicet decimum quartum, decimum quintum & decimum sextum, Euangelista insignem concionem in coena vltima, & partim post cœnam ad discipulos habitam, quæ velut cygnea cantio fuit Christi iam morituri. In quo sermone Dominus discipulos consolatur contra scandalum suæ mortis, & contra suum ab eis discessum: item hortatur eos ad constantiam in fide erga ipsum, & dilectione mutua: denique consolatur eos contra odium & persecutionem mundi.
units.tr: Over the following three chapters, namely the fourteenth, fifteenth and sixteenth, the evangelist records a remarkable discourse, given at the last supper and partly after it, to the disciples. It was like the swan song of Christ, now about to die. In this discourse the Lord comforts the disciples against the scandal of his death and against his departure from them; he likewise exhorts them to constancy in faith toward himself and to mutual love; and finally he comforts them against the hatred and persecution of the world.

units.la: Partes capitis x i v sunt tres: Prima, (Consolatio est, quam Christus perturbationi discipulorum opponit: usque ad v.5. Secunda, (colloquium Christi continet & discipulorum ipsius de vera Dei Patris notitia: usque ad v. 12. Tertiâ, ad consolationem redit, promittens exauditionem precum, & missionem Spiritus sancti, sed inferiùr exhortatio ad seruanda præcepta ab ipso prius proposita.
units.tr: Chapter 14 has three parts. The first is the consolation with which Christ meets the disciples' distress, up to v. 5. The second contains the conversation between Christ and his disciples about the true knowledge of God the Father, up to v. 12. In the third he returns to consolation, promising the granting of prayers and the sending of the Holy Spirit; but then follows an exhortation to keep the commandments he had earlier set forth.

units.la: Cap. x v. Sermonem eiusdem cum priore argumenti orditur; Primùm hortatur discipulos ad constantiam in fide; docens, eos per fidem sibi tanquam palmites viti, esse insitos: usque ad v. 8. Deinde hortatur eos ad studium pietatis, ac inprimis ad mutuam dilectionem: usque ad v. 18. Tertiò, consolatur eos contra odium ac persecutionem mundi, & promissionem præclaram de missione Spiritus sancti renouat; inde à v. 18. usque ad finem.
units.tr: Chapter 15. He begins a discourse on the same subject as the previous one. First he exhorts the disciples to constancy in faith, teaching that through faith they are grafted into him as branches into the vine, up to v. 8. Then he exhorts them to zeal for godliness, and above all to mutual love, up to v. 18. Thirdly, he comforts them against the hatred and persecution of the world, and renews the glorious promise of the sending of the Holy Spirit, from v. 18 to the end.

units.la: Cap. x v i. Continuat sermonem duobus superioribus capitibus institutum, & tria potissimum agit. Primùm prædicit eis mala, ipsis euentura à Iudæis, usque ad v. 5. Deinde consolatur eos rursum contra tristitiam quam conceperant ex futuro ipsius discessu, usque ad v. 29. Postremò prædicit eis futuram ipsorum fugam, sequeque contra illam consolatur, & totius huius prolixæ concio-nis epilogum subiungit.
units.tr: Chapter 16. He continues the discourse begun in the two preceding chapters and deals with three main matters. First he foretells the evils that will befall them from the Jews, up to v. 5. Then he again comforts them against the sorrow they had conceived at his coming departure, up to v. 29. Lastly he foretells their future flight, comforts them against it, and adds the summary of this whole long discourse.

units.la: Capite decimo septimo continetur precatio Domini nostri Iesu Christi, quam habuit tanquam populi Dei summus sacerdos, cùm suum ipsius corpus paulò post in ara crucis oblaturus esset: qua & seipsum, & populum suum Patri commendat. Habet autem precatio hæc tres partes. Primùm enim orat pro seipso, vsque ad v. 6. Deinde pro discipulis, id est, undecim Apostolis, à v. 6. vsque ad 20. Postremò pro reliquis electis, qui per doctrinam Apostolorum credituri erant vsque ad finem mundi.
units.tr: Chapter 17 contains the prayer of our Lord Jesus Christ, which he offered as the high priest of God's people, shortly before he was to offer his own body on the altar of the cross; in it he commends both himself and his people to the Father. This prayer has three parts. First he prays for himself, up to v. 6. Then he prays for the disciples, that is, the eleven apostles, from v. 6 to v. 20. Lastly he prays for the rest of the elect, who were to believe through the teaching of the apostles until the end of the world.

units.la: PASSIONIS DOMINICÆ historia.
units.tr: The history of the Lord's Passion.

units.la: Hactenus de officii Prophetici, sequitur de Sacerdotalis administratione.
units.tr: Thus far concerning the prophetic office; there follows the administration of the priestly office.

units.la: Cap. xiix & xix: describit Euangelista historiam Passionis Domini. Quamuis enim vniuersa vita Christi continua passio fuerit: tamen Passionis vocabulo καθ' ἐξοχὴν intelligitur historia eorum, quæ post completum ministerium suum, (quod prædicationem Euangelij attinet) postmodum sub Pontificibus, præside item Romano passus est: quandoquidem tum demum crucifixus & mortuus, per proprium sanguinem inSanctumSanctorum est ingressus, & consummauit in æternum eos qui sanctificantur. Vltimus hic Actus Christi in terris opus omne coronauit, quando Sacerdotis sanctissimi & plane admirandi partes obiēs, seipsum sponte obtulit ad mortem & cruentum sacrificium pro nobis, vt quod sanguine taurorum & aliorum brutorum in V. T. adumbratum fuerat, reipsa ab eo præstaretur, nimirum expiatio peccatorum nostrorum.
units.tr: Chapters 18 and 19: the Evangelist describes the history of the Lord's Passion. Although the whole life of Christ was a continuous passion, yet by the word Passion is understood, by eminence [καθ' ἐξοχὴν], the history of what he suffered after he had completed his ministry (as far as the preaching of the Gospel is concerned), namely under the Chief Priests and then under the Roman governor. For it was then, at last, that he was crucified and died, and entered the Holy of Holies through his own blood, and "perfected for ever those who are sanctified" (Heb. 9; 10). This last act crowned all the work Christ performed on earth. Discharging the part of a most holy and truly admirable priest, he offered himself willingly to death as a bloody sacrifice for us, so that what had been foreshadowed in the Old Testament by the blood of bulls and other animals might be accomplished by him in reality, namely the atonement for our sins.

units.la: Cap. xiix [?] tres potissimum partes siue actus Passionis Christi continentur. Prior continet eorum descriptionem, quae in horto sunt gesta, vt quod Christus hostibus obuiam procedit, & semetipsum nulla coactione, sed voluntate libera capiendum sistit: cui parti simul includitur narratio dimicationis Petri, vsque ad v. 13. Secunda parte narrantur gesta coram concilio Ecclesiastico Pharisaeorum & Sacerdotum, vbi interseritur narratio lapsus Petri, vsque ad v. 28. Tertia pars ea memorat, quae coram Pontio Pilato præside acta sunt.
units.tr: Chapter 18 [?] contains three principal parts or acts of Christ's Passion. (1) The first contains the description of what was done in the garden: how Christ goes out to meet his enemies and, not under any compulsion but of his own free will, gives himself up to be seized. To this part is also joined the account of Peter's fight, up to v. 13. (2) The second part relates what was done before the ecclesiastical council of the Pharisees and the Chief Priests, where the account of Peter's fall is inserted, up to v. 28. (3) The third part recounts what was done before Pontius Pilate, the governor.

units.la: Cap. xix. (continuatur forensis actio coram Pilato præside in causa Christi;vsque ad v- 17. Secunda pars huius capitis ea continet quae gesta sunt in loco supplicij, qui nominabatur Caluaria, Hebraice Golgotha, a v. 17. vsque ad v. 31. Tertia pars ea continet, quae mortem Christi secuta sunt, vna cum historia sepultura ipsius.
units.tr: Chapter 19. (The judicial proceedings before Pilate the governor in Christ's case continue, up to v. 17. The second part of this chapter contains what was done in the place of execution, which was called Calvary, in Hebrew Golgotha, from v. 17 up to v. 31. The third part contains what followed the death of Christ, together with the history of his burial.

units.la: DE INCHOATIONE MUNE-ris Regii.
units.tr: On the Beginning of the Kingly Office.

units.la: TRIUMPHUS Christi resurgentis deinceps vsque ad finem libri describitur, capite scilicet xx, & xxi. quibus narratur quomodo Christus post resurrectionem suam ex mortuis, sese vivum ostenderit discipulis suis.
units.tr: The triumph of the risen Christ is described from here to the end of the book, namely in chapters 20 and 21, which tell how Christ, after his resurrection from the dead, showed himself alive to his disciples.

units.la: Capite xx Historia resurrectionis Christi continetur, cum tribus distinctis apparitioni bus, quibus veritatem resurrectionis suæ com-probauit Dominus. Partes principales sunt quatuor. In prima narratur, cui omnium primo innotuerit Domini resurrectio & quomodo: nempe Ioanni & Petro, qui moti indicio Mariæ Magdalenæ de sublato corpore Iesu, sepulcrum inspexerunt, ac linteis solis repertis, Dominum resurrexisse crediderunt, usque ad v. 11. In secunda parte narratur, quomodo eadem Maria viderit in sepulcro duos angelos, & mox extra sepulcrum Iesum ipsum: quem tamen initio non agnouit, donec nominatim ab eo compellaretur: item quomodo mandata Domini ad discipulos detulerit, usque ad v. 19. In tertia parte narratur, quomodo se Iesus patefecerit discipulis in domo clausa congregatis, & quibus mandatis, quaque facultate simul & potestate ad ministerium verbi eos instruxerit, usque ad v. 24. In quarta parte narratur de Thoma, quomodo is narrationem condiscipulorum, testantium Dominum resurrexisse, fidem detraxerit; & quomodo post octi-duum Dominus se ei patefecerit, eiusque incredu-litatem reprehenderit: ipse vero fidem suam plenis-sime confessus sit, usque ad v. 30. in quo est apodio-xis narrationis plurium miraculorum Christi.v.vltimo causa finalis duplex exponitur, cur ea quæ hoc libro continentur, conscripserit.
units.tr: Chapter 20 contains the history of Christ's resurrection, the history of Christ's resurrection is contained, with three distinct appearances by which the Lord confirmed the truth of his resurrection. There are four principal parts. In the first, it is told to whom the Lord's resurrection was first made known and how. John and Peter, moved by the report of Mary Magdalene that Jesus' body had been taken away, went to inspect the tomb; finding only the linen cloths, they believed that the Lord had risen. This runs to verse 11. In the second part, it is told how the same Mary saw two angels in the tomb and then, outside the tomb, Jesus himself, whom at first she did not recognise until he addressed her by name; also how she carried the Lord's commands to the disciples. This runs to verse 19. In the third part, it is told how Jesus revealed himself to the disciples gathered in a closed room, and with what commands and what authority and power he instructed them for the ministry of the Word. This runs to verse 24. In the fourth part, it is told of Thomas, how he refused to believe his fellow disciples who testified that the Lord had risen; how after eight days the Lord revealed himself to him and rebuked his unbelief, while he himself fully confessed his faith. This runs to verse 30, where there is a conclusion to the narrative of the many miracles of Christ. In verse 31, finally, a twofold final cause is set out, explaining why he wrote the things contained in this book.

units.la: Caput xxi. cohæret cum præcedente: continet enim adhuc unam patefactionem Iesu post resurrectionem. Sunt autem duæ partes. In prima parte narratur, quomodo se patefecerit Iesus discipulis ad mare Tiberiadis, usque ad v. 15. In altera parte narratur colloquium Domini cum Petro: ubi Dominus ei commendat pascendas oves [illegible, ~2 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~8 letters] [illegible, ~5 letters] [illegible, ~7 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~8 letters] suas: prædicit ei mortem violentam siue martyrium & respondet de Ioanne, nempe hoc ipso Evangelista, qui hunc librum scripsit.
units.tr: Chapter 21 is connected with the preceding one, for it still contains one further manifestation of Jesus after the resurrection. There are two parts. In the first part it is narrated how Jesus revealed himself to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias, up to v. 15. In the second part is narrated the conversation of the Lord with Peter, in which the Lord commends to him the feeding of his sheep: he foretells to him a violent death, that is martyrdom, and answers concerning John, namely this very Evangelist who wrote this book.

units.la: SVMMÆ CAPITVM EX versibus. D. R. G.
units.tr: SUMMARY OF THE CHAPTERS BY VERSES. D. R. G.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAP. I.

units.la: AEterni narrat naturam & semina Verbi, Quod simul & verum prædicat esse Deum, Andream & Petrum fortem, magnumque Philippum, Cumque illis iustum Nathaniela vocat.
units.tr: The Eternal One tells of the nature and seeds of the Word, who also declares that he is at once true God; he calls Andrew and brave Peter, and great Philip, and with them Nathanael, the just man.

units.la: 2 CHRISTVS mutat aquas in dulcis pocula vini, Eque sacra pellit turpia lucra domo. Destruite hoc templum, lux illud tertia reddet. Hinc multos ad se per sua signa trahit.
units.tr: 2 Christ changes water into cups of sweet wine, and drives the shameful profits from the holy house. "Destroy this temple"; the third light will restore it. Hence he draws many to himself by his signs.

units.la: 3 Salvifici discit Nicodemus munera Verbi, Utque sit æterna percipienda salus. Quis finis CHRISTI, quod & hic sit causa salutis, Baptista haud vana cum ratione docet.
units.tr: 3 Nicodemus learns the saving gifts of the Word, and how eternal salvation is to be received. What the end of Christ is, and that this too is the cause of salvation, the Baptist teaches with no empty reasoning.

units.la: 4 Fœmina Samariæ vigilanti pectore discit, Quum CHRISTVS sancto prædicat ore fidem. Multi illi credunt: Galilæa in regna reversus Restituit vitæ, qui prope fata videt.
units.tr: 4 The woman of Samaria learns with a watchful breast, when Christ preaches faith with holy mouth. Many believe in him. Returned to the kingdom of Galilee, he restores to life the one who sees death near.

units.la: 5 Convalui CHRISTI verbo, qui corpore languens Traxerat in morbo tempora longa graui. Accusant Scribæ, CHRISTVS se rite iuvetur[?], Auxilioque patris se facere illa probat.
units.tr: 5 By Christ's word he healed the one who, wasting in body, had spent long times in a grievous illness. The scribes accuse him; Christ proves that he is rightly helped, and that he does these things by the Father's aid.

units.la: 6 Millia multa cibat, detrectat regia sceptra, Et fluidas sancto corpore calcat aquas. Seque cibum esse docet credentis corde receptum, Deficiunt multi, discipulique manent.
units.tr: 6 He feeds many thousands, refuses the royal sceptre, and treads the watery waves with his holy body. He teaches that he is the food received in the heart of the believer; many fall away, and the disciples remain.

units.la: 7 Reppetit in festo Solymorum mœnia CHRISTVS, Et populum in templo dogmata sancta docet. Accusant alii, mox vincula dura parantur, Non habet eventum res tamen ista suum.
units.tr: 7 Christ returns at the feast to the walls of Jerusalem and teaches the holy doctrines to the people in the temple. Others accuse him; soon hard chains are prepared, yet that matter has no outcome of its own.

units.la: 8 Turpis adulterii fontem de morte redemit, Et Christus mundi est luxque salusque simul. Semen Abræ non sunt, æterno numine vinis CHRISTVS, & euadit cum lapidare volunt.
units.tr: 8 He redeemed from death the adulteress of shameful fame, and Christ is at once the light and salvation of the world. They are not the seed of Abraham; Christ conquers by eternal power, and he escapes when they want to stone him.

units.la: Lumina restituit claro cum luminis usu Illi, qui cæco lumine natus erat.
units.tr: He restored sight, with clear use of the light, to him who had been born blind.

units.la: Pontifices illum culpant, expellitur insons, CHRISTVS at hunc vera credere mente docet[?].
units.tr: The high priests blame him, the innocent one is cast out, and Christ teaches this man to believe with a true mind.

units.la: Est verus pastor CHRISTVS, est ianua vitæ, Cuius omnes norunt dulcia verba sequi.
units.tr: Christ is the true shepherd, he is the door of life; all know how to follow his sweet words.

units.la: Quisque fit exponit: lapides rapit impia turba. Hic tamen illasus[?] cæpta nefanda fugit.
units.tr: Whoever explains it, the impious crowd snatches up stones. Yet he, unharmed, flees the wicked undertaking.

units.la: Lazarus e tumulo CHRISTI virtute resurgit, Obturbant stultos talia signa sophos.
units.tr: Lazarus rises from the tomb by Christ's power; such signs disturb the foolish wise men.

units.la: Utiliusque putant, unum quam perdier[?] omnes. Hunc ergo immerita tollere morte student.
units.tr: They think it more useful that one man should perish than all. Therefore they strive to remove him by an undeserved death.

units.la: Unguento redolent vescentis[?] crura pedesque, Proditor iniustus murmura dira monet.
units.tr: The legs and feet of the one reclining smell of ointment; the treacherous traitor utters dire murmurs.

units.la: Lazaro & insidias ponunt: invectius asella. Quæritur a Græcia vita salusque viris.
units.tr: They also lay snares for Lazarus. The life and salvation of men are sought from Greece.

units.la: Vox delapsa venit cælo, cui credere pergunt. Non veni iudex, sed bene fausta salus.
units.tr: A voice fell from heaven, and they go on believing it: "I came not to judge, but to bring blessed salvation."

units.la: Abluit unda pedes CHRISTO sic usa ministro, Elati ponant corda superba viri.
units.tr: Water washes the feet, Christ using his servant thus; let proud men of lofty hearts lay aside their pride.

units.la: Unus & e vobis prodet me, mutuo amate. Hei ter me miserum Petre negabis iners.
units.tr: "One of you will betray me; love one another." Alas, thrice wretched me; Peter, you will deny me in your sloth.

units.la: Hortatur fortis ut patienter pectore pergant, Cumque fide flagrans ut quoque crescat amor.
units.tr: He urges the brave to persevere patiently in heart, and that love may grow as faith burns.

units.la: Non inopes linquam, dabitur nam spiritus almus, Omnia qui cupidos edocuisse potest.
units.tr: "I will not leave you destitute, for the kindly Spirit will be given, who can teach all things to those who desire them."

units.la: Qui palmes CHRISTI fuerit, det tempore fructus: Sitque comes fidei pectoris almus amor.
units.tr: Whoever is a branch of Christ's vine, let him bear fruit in season; and let kindly love be the companion of the believing heart.

units.la: Cuncta pater vobis largitur, spernite mundi Consilia, en similis me quoque mente petit.
units.tr: The Father grants all things to you; despise the counsels of the world. Behold, he seeks me similarly in mind as well.

units.la: Solatur misere perdendos morte cruenta, Pneumatis officium denotat inde sacri.
units.tr: He comforts those who are to be wretchedly lost by bloody death, and hence he points out the office of the holy Spirit.

units.la: Ferte precor magnos patienti corde dolores. Quæ nostro petitis nomine, quippe dabit.
units.tr: Bear, I pray, great sorrows with a patient heart. Whatever you ask in my name, he will indeed give.

units.la: Glorifica natum nunc, o pater optime, sanctos Nunc, vogo[?], clementi perge iuvare manu.
units.tr: Glorify the Son now, O best Father, and the saints; now, continue to help with a merciful hand.

units.la: Ipse quidem iuvi, docui pia verba salutis. Nunc tibi commissos tu tueare[?], pater. 18 Perfide Iuda venis, prosternitur impia turba. Quique prius pugnas, nunc male firme negas. Pontifices quærunt, alapa cum cæditur insons. Prætori Ausonio traditur inde tamen. An rex sit quærit, CHRISTVS sua regna recenset. Iniustosævum Barrabam ore petunt. 19 Multatus virgis spinosam fronte coronam Gestat, quem prætor eripuisse cupit. Sed frustra: quoniam suspensus luditur, inde Distribuunt vestes scriptaque verba notant. Commendat matrem: transfigit lancea corpus Mortuum, & in duro marmore membra locant, 20 Magdalidi apparet viuens a funere CHRISTVS, Discipulis etiam cernitur inde suis: Pneumaque dat sacrum: sed tunc fors absuit illis Thomas, qui tacto credit & ipse Deo. 21 Denuo comparet, vescuntur piscibus assis, Quos nimio attraxit pondere retecavum. Hinc commendat oues Petro, mortemque recenset, Seque iubet toto pectore rite sequi.
units.tr: I indeed have helped; I taught the pious words of salvation. Now, Father, you keep safe those committed to you. 18: Treacherous Judas comes, and the impious crowd is thrown down. He who before fought now firmly denies his wrong. The priests seek him, and though innocent he is struck with a slap. Then he is handed over to the Ausonian praetor. He asks whether he is king, and Christ recounts his kingdoms. They demand the cruel Barabbas with unjust mouths. 19: Scourged with rods, he bears a thorny crown on his brow, which the praetor wishes to snatch away. But in vain, since hung up he is mocked; then they divide the garments and note the written words. He commends his mother; a lance pierces the dead body, and they lay the limbs in hard marble. 20: Christ appears living to Mary Magdalene from the funeral; then he is seen by his disciples, and gives the holy Spirit. But then Thomas was absent from them by chance, who believes too once he touches God. 21: He appears again; they eat roasted fish, which he drew in with the great weight of the net. Hence he commends the sheep to Peter, recounts his death, and bids him rightly follow with his whole heart.

units.la: VERSVS EX G. F.
units.tr: VERSES BY G. F.

units.la: CAP. I.
units.tr: CHAP. I.

units.la: AEternus caro fit testatur præco rogatur. Monstrat, se iungit par tibi Christe duplex.
units.tr: The Eternal becomes flesh; the herald is called to witness. He shows himself joined to you, Christ, a double equal.

units.la: 2 Baccho mutat aquam, fugit emptor soluite templum Interiora hominum pectora Christe vides.
units.tr: 2 He changes water into wine; the buyer flees. Loose the temple: you see the inward hearts of men, Christ.

units.la: 3 Cur nescis princeps? Lucem vir perditus odit. Inque dies minui sanctæ prophetæ cupis
units.tr: 3 Why do you not know, ruler? The ruined man hates the light. And you desire that the holy prophet be diminished day by day.

units.la: 4 De Samaritana legis, & de frugibus albis. Nemo propheta domi. Regulæ febris abit.
units.tr: 4 Of the Samaritan woman, of the law, and of the white harvest. No prophet in his own home. The official's fever departs.

units.la: 5 En piscina patri par natus corpora surgent. Non quæro testem, scripta vetusta probant.
units.tr: 5 Behold the pool: the son, equal to the Father, the bodies rise. I seek no witness; ancient writings prove it.

units.la: 6 Fracta replent cophinos rex esse recusat Iesus. Manna dedit carnem nunc dabit ipse suam.
units.tr: 6 The broken pieces fill the baskets; Jesus refuses to be king. Manna gave flesh; now he himself will give his own.

units.la: 7 Grande instat festum. murmur doctrina fluentes Undæ dissidium tu Nicodeme sapis.
units.tr: 7 A great feast is at hand. Murmuring at the teaching, flowing waves, division: you, Nicodemus, understand.

units.la: 8 I mulier, de te testaris, quo fugies nos? Quid tactatis eum, quo prior ipse fui?
units.tr: 8 Go, woman, you bear witness of yourself: where will you flee from us? Why do you handle him before whom I myself was first?

units.la: 9 Lux datur à partu cæco, violata queruntur Sabbatha Iudæi, hisque subortæ calet.
units.tr: 9 Light is given to the man blind from birth; the Jews complain that the Sabbath is violated, and heat arises from these things.

units.la: 10 Mortem pastor adit. num sis edicito Christus? Peccone,si patrem dico me habere Deum?
units.tr: 10 Death the shepherd approaches. Tell us, Christ, whether you are... Do I sin if I say that I have God as my Father?

units.la: 11 Nuper functus eras fato: nunc Lazare viuis. Vni pro toto mors subeunda grege est.
units.tr: 11 Lately you had died by fate; now, Lazarus, you live. Death must be undergone by one for the whole flock.

units.la: 12 Offendit Nardus, caue Lazare: vox ruit alto. Non credunt signis, mundus honorque placent.
units.tr: 12 The spikenard offends; beware, Lazarus: a voice rushes from on high. They do not believe the signs; the world and honour please them.

units.la: 13 Plantas Christe lauas, male sano porrigis offam. Das insigne tuis, tristificasque Petrum.
units.tr: 13 Christ, you wash the feet; you offer a morsel to the ill-disposed. You give a sign to your own, and you grieve Peter.

units.la: 14 Quis timor iste? locum paro. sum via. crede Philippe, Spiritus adveniet. mox rediturus eo.
units.tr: 14 What is this fear? I prepare a place. I am the way. Believe, Philip; the Spirit will come. Soon I shall return to where I am going.

units.la: 15 Reiectus palmes, dilectio nostris amici Omnia, quos mecum non bene mundus amat.
units.tr: 15 The branch is cast off; love for our friends. All those whom the world, not rightly, loves along with me.

units.la: 16 Spiritus afflictis aderit, mundumque notabit. Pro lachrymis rediens gaudia plena dabo.
units.tr: 16 The Spirit will be present to the afflicted, and will convict the world. Returning, I will give full joy for tears.

units.la: 17 Tempus adest vt glorificer. nunc cuncta peregi. Da bona discipulis quae peto sancte pater.
units.tr: 17 The time is come that I be glorified; now I have finished all things. Give good things to the disciples, which I ask, holy Father.

units.la: 18 Vis armata ruit, cædis bone Petre, negasque. Pontifices arguunt, multa Pilate rogas.
units.tr: 18 Armed force rushes in; good Peter, you strike and then deny. The chief priests accuse; you question much, Pilate.

units.la: 19 Abs re cur damnem? reticem? inscriptio sortes. Astans virgo sitis, fractio crurum aloe.
units.tr: 19 Why should I condemn him without cause? Should I be silent? An inscription, lots. Standing by, the virgin; thirst; the breaking of the legs; aloes.

units.la: 20 Eini concurrunt. Mariase monstrat Iesus. Bis pax inquit eis. Thoma videto manus.
units.tr: 20 Two run together. Jesus shows himself to Mary. Twice he says to them, Peace. Thomas, see the hands.

units.la: 21 Conspiciunt septem Dominum Petre curris in undis. Cura pastor oues, meque sequare ducem.
units.tr: 21 Seven see the Lord; Peter, you run into the waves. Care for the sheep, shepherd, and follow me as your leader.

units.la: VOCABULA MEMORIALIA, SINGULA EX SINGULIS CAPITIBUS, quina vero uno versu hexametro comprehensa.
units.tr: MNEMONIC WORDS, ONE FROM EACH CHAPTER, but five together comprehended in one hexameter verse.

units.la: 1 2 3 4 Verbum, Mutat aquas, Nicodemus, & Hydria, 5 Motus, 6 7 8 9 10 Sum Panis, Mysta, stat Adultera, Coecus, Ouile, 11 12 13 14 15 Faenus, Libra, Pedes, Christus, Via, Palmites, estis
units.tr: 1 2 3 4 Word, Changes water, Nicodemus, and Waterpot, 5 Movement, 6 7 8 9 10 I am the Bread, Initiates, stands the Adulteress, Blind man, Sheepfold, 11 12 13 14 15 Usury, Scales, Feet, Christ, Way, Branches, are you

units.la: Pneuma, Ardens, Lux, Illusus, Currit, Mani-festat.
units.tr: Spirit, Burning, Light, Mocked, Runs, Manifests.

units.la: Declaratio.
units.tr: Explanation.

units.la: Verbum caro factum est. v.14. Mutat aquas Chri-stus in vinum generosissimum. v.7. Nicodemus, dispu-tat cum Christo de resurrectione. v.4. & Hydria reli-cta à Samaritana. v.28. Motus aquæ in Bethesda. v.3.
units.tr: Word became flesh. v.14. Changes water Christ into the finest wine. v.7. Nicodemus, disputes with Christ about the resurrection. v.4. & Waterpot left by the Samaritan woman. v.28. Movement of the water at Bethesda. v.3.

units.la: Sum panis, inquit Christus. v.35. Mystæ.i. sacerdo-tes Christum capere conantur. v.32. Stat adultera sola coram Domino. v.3. Cæcus abluit lutum in piscina Si-loam. v.7. Ouile in quod fur per tectum ascendit. v.1.
units.tr: I am the bread, says Christ. v.35. Initiates, that is, the priests, try to seize Christ. v.32. Stands the adulteress alone before the Lord. v.3. Blind man washes the clay in the pool of Siloam. v.7. Sheepfold into which the thief climbs over the wall. v.1.

units.la: Facens Lazarus quatriduanus in sepulcro, v.39. Libra unguenti pretiosi. v.3. Pedes discipulorum lavat Christus. v.5. Christus Via, v.6. Palmites estis, vos discipuli. v.2.
units.tr: Stinking Lazarus, four days in the tomb. v.39. Scales of precious ointment. v.3. Feet of the disciples washed by Christ. v.5. Christ the Way, v.6. You are the branches, you disciples. v.2.

units.la: Pneuma Veritatis promittitur. v.13. Ardens Christi precatio. Lux fertur à ministro Pharisaei. v.3. Illusus Christus varie. v.3. Currit Iohannes & Petrus. v.4. Manifestat se Christus frangendo panem. v.13.
units.tr: Spirit of truth is promised. v.13. Burning prayer of Christ. Light is brought by the servant of the Pharisees. v.3. Mocked Christ in various ways. v.3. Runs John and Peter. v.4. Manifests himself, Christ, by breaking bread. v.13.

units.la: ANALYSIS ACTORVM Apostolicorum.
units.tr: Analysis of the Acts of the Apostles.

units.la: HACTENVS fuerunt Libri historici, qui de Saluatore nostro Iesu Christo agunt. Nam Euangelistæ omnes quatuor, ad hunc scopum collineant, ut res à Christo immediatè in terris gestas explicent: sequitur nunc liber
units.tr: Up to this point the historical books have been those dealing with our Saviour Jesus Christ. For all four Evangelists aim at this purpose, namely to set out the things done on earth by Christ himself; now follows the book of the Acts of the Apostles.

units.la: DE ACTIS APOSTOLORVM,
units.tr: ON THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES,

units.la: Hoc est:
units.tr: That is:

units.la: QVID APOSTOLI tum vniuersi, tum in specie Petrus, Iohannes, Iacobus & Paulus; ac præter illos alij quidam sancti viri, ut nominatim Stephanus Diaconus, Philippus Euange-lista & Barnabas comes Pauli, quid(inquam) illi nomine Christi iam ad dextram æterni Patris exaltati, Spiritus sancti ductu & instinctu esse-cerint, & perpessi sint.
units.tr: WHAT THE APOSTLES did, both all of them together and in particular Peter, John, James and Paul; and besides these, certain other holy men, namely Stephen the deacon, Philip the evangelist and Barnabas, Paul's companion: what they did and suffered (I say) in the name of Christ, now exalted to the right hand of the eternal Father, under the guidance and impulse of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: AVTOR huius libri est S. Lucas Euangelista, de quo supra est expositum. Is harum rerum quæ hic scripsit αὐτόπτης[?] i. testis oculatus fuit: utpote Apostoli Pauli in omnibus ipsius peregrinationibus comes indiuiduus, ut ex multis huius historiæ locis colligi potest. Nemo igitur felicius hanc & aptius contexere historiam potuit ipso Luca. Et testatur Nicephorus lib.2. cap. 43. & 45: Lucam rogatu Pauli id præstitisse: cui sententiæ etiam Hieronymus & alij ad-stipulantur. Quod si verum est, discipulus tanto Præceptori, officium tam utile posteritati & necessarium denegare non potuit. Hæc igitur fuit S. Lucæ huius libri scribendi occasio: cui accedit & illud, quod in primis ad causam impel-lentem & finalem pertinet: Voluit Spiritus sanctus singulari consilio, primæ Ecclesiæ histo-riam certam & indubitatam extare: ideoque ad hanc scribendam elegit aptissimum orga-num. Debuit enim posteritas certissima esse, promissiones Christi ad amussim impletas esse, non solum de ascensionis articulo: sed de communicato Spiritu sancto, de testimonio per Apostolos propagato, de periculis quæ testes Christi excepissent, ut constaret, verè missos, ut agnos inter lupos. Voluit etiam Spiritus sanctus distinguere regnum Christi à Politicis imperiis, ne somniemus, quod etiam Apostolis interdum accidit, Christum in his terris regna administrare: sed totum hoc pertinere ad salutem animarum, ad redemptionem a peccato & morte, ac vires humanas nihil prorsus valere in regno illo Christi.
units.tr: The author of this book is St Luke the evangelist, of whom we have spoken above. He was an eyewitness [αὐτόπτης] of the things he writes here, as the inseparable companion of the Apostle Paul in all his travels, as can be gathered from many passages of this history. No one could therefore have woven this history together more happily and fittingly than Luke himself. Nicephorus, book 2, chapters 43 and 45, testifies that Luke did this at Paul's request, and Jerome and others agree with this view. If this is true, the disciple could not refuse so great a teacher, nor deny posterity so useful and necessary a service. This, then, was the occasion for St Luke to write this book. To this is added what pertains chiefly to the impelling and final cause: the Holy Spirit, by a singular counsel, willed that a certain and undoubted history of the first Church should exist, and so he chose the most suitable instrument for writing it. For posterity had to be fully certain that the promises of Christ had been fulfilled exactly, not only concerning the article of the ascension, but concerning the gift of the Holy Spirit, the testimony spread through the Apostles, and the dangers which the witnesses of Christ underwent, so that it might be plain that they were truly sent as lambs among wolves. The Holy Spirit also willed to distinguish the kingdom of Christ from political empires, lest we imagine, as the Apostles sometimes did, that Christ administers kingdoms on this earth; rather, all of this pertains to the salvation of souls, to redemption from sin and death, and human powers are of no value whatever in that kingdom of Christ.

units.la: Argumentum. Quomodo doctrina Christi post eius in coelum ascensionem per Apostolos sit propagata & quibus confirmata miraculis: quae pericula ob testimonium hoc sint experti, & quam vbique Domini praesentem habuerint liberationem. Summa, quae fuerit primae Ecclesiae facies, quae incunabula, quae incrementa, quae doctrina Apostolorum, & quae verbi praedicati vis, quod discrimen inter veram & falsam doctrinam, quales veri & falsi doctores, &c. Orditur autem ab assumptione Domini: hinc quomodo Apostoli diuinitus instructi fuerint ad hoc munus. Accipiunt enim Spiritum sanctum, & virtutibus ad docendum necessariis instruuntur. Hinc quid seorsim Petrus in hac causa egerit, quid Stephanus, quid Philippus, inprimis vero quid Paulus passim & docuerit & fecerit. Mortem quoque nonnullorum depingit, ut Stephani, Iacobi.Paulum comitatur Romam usque, ubi in vinculis eum relinquit.
units.tr: Argument. How the doctrine of Christ was propagated through the Apostles after his ascension into heaven, and by what miracles it was confirmed; what dangers they underwent for this testimony, and how everywhere they experienced the Lord's presence as their deliverer. In sum: what the face of the first Church was, its beginnings, its growth, the doctrine of the Apostles, and the power of the preached word; what the difference is between true and false doctrine, and what true and false teachers are like, etc. It begins with the Lord's ascension, and then shows how the Apostles were divinely equipped for this office. For they receive the Holy Spirit and are furnished with the gifts necessary for teaching. Then it recounts what Peter did separately in this cause, what Stephen did, what Philip did, and above all what Paul both taught and did throughout his ministry. It also portrays the deaths of some, such as Stephen and James. It accompanies Paul all the way to Rome, where it leaves him in chains.

units.la: Propositio. Quicquid Christus vel de se, vel de Apostolis praedixerat adamussim adimpletum esse: inprimis vero testimonium illud per Apostolos de Christo in toto terrarum orbe, ut iusserat, bona fide, & summa diligentia exhibitum esse. Haec summa est scripti praesentis. Quod ut intelligamus, expendendum est quid Chri[?] stius de se mox futurum, item de Apostolis quid prae-dixerit. De se prædixit: Expedire ut abeat: nisi enim abeat, consolatorem non venturum, Ioh. 16. Item, vado paraturus vobis locum, Ioh. 14: &c. De Apostolis autem prædixit, acceptu-ros eos alium consolatorem, Ioh. 14. 15. & 16. Prædixit illorum persecutiones, Ioh 16. Matth. 10. prædixit fore ipsos testes suæ doctrinæ, & resurrectionis. Luc. 24. iussit docere in toto orbe terrarum Matth. 28. Prædixit factutos[?] miracula, Marc. 16. Hæc & similia omnia, quomodo præcisè sint impleta, hoc libro docetur.
units.tr: Proposition. That whatever Christ had foretold, either about himself or about the Apostles, was fulfilled exactly; and above all that the testimony concerning Christ was given through the Apostles throughout the whole world, as he had commanded, in good faith and with the greatest diligence. This is the sum of the present writing. To understand this, we must consider what Christ foretold would happen soon concerning himself, and likewise what he predicted about the Apostles. He predicted about himself: "It is expedient for you that I go away; for unless I go away, the Comforter will not come," John 16. Likewise: "I go to prepare a place for you," John 14, etc. About the Apostles, he predicted that they would receive another Comforter, John 14, 15 and 16. He predicted their persecutions, John 16, Matt. 10. He predicted that they would be witnesses of his doctrine and resurrection, Luke 24. He commanded them to teach throughout the whole world, Matt. 28. He predicted that they would work miracles, Mark 16. How all these things were precisely fulfilled is taught in this book.

units.la: Usus. Præter narrationes historicas de veritate & complemento promissionum Dei testantes, hic liber immensum habet in se coelestis doctrinæ thesaurum reconditum: ut est. 1. doctrina de præcipuis fidei Christianæ articulis, videlicet de veritate indubitata resurrectionis, ascensionis in coelum & exaltationis Christi ad dextram æterni patris: de impletione & abolitione caeremoniarum Leviticarum, umbræ legis, discriminis populorum & ciborum per promulgationem Euangelij: inprimis vero de summo religionis Christianæ capite, de omnium hominum sive Iudaeorum, sive Gentium iustitia & salute, non ex operibus legis, sed ex sola Domini nostri Iesu Christi misericordia & gratia proveniente, uti expresse id testatur Petrus cap. 15. v. 11. &c: ut[?] Promissionum etiam Veteris Testamenti complementum, de vocatione Gentium & eorum in populum Dei adoptione per Euangelium: de effusione Spiritus sancti ultimis temporibus[?] super omnem carnem: de Ecclesia contra omnes Diaboli tyrannorum & Sophistarum furores, potenter & mirando modo defendenda, & ad finem usque mundi conservanda. III Vivam verae Ecclesiae faciem, eiusque reformandae rationem nobis hic liber delineat, ad quam omnes Ecclesiae se conformare debeant. IV De efficacia ministerij Verbi, impios convertentis, corda penetrat, &c: V In exemplis fidelium Ecclesiae ministrorum, quid nostri, qui ad idem munus vocamur, sit officij in allegandis & explicandis S. scripturis, & in totius functione muneris. De hoc libro vere dici potest esse hanc historiam magistram vitae &c.
units.tr: Use. Besides the historical narratives bearing witness to the truth and fulfilment of God's promises, this book contains within it a vast treasure of heavenly doctrine, laid up as it were in store. It contains: (1) doctrine on the principal articles of the Christian faith, namely the indubitable truth of the resurrection, of the ascension into heaven, and of the exaltation of Christ to the right hand of the eternal Father; on the fulfilment and abolition of the Levitical ceremonies, the shadow of the law, and the distinction of peoples and foods through the proclamation of the Gospel; and above all on the chief head of the Christian religion, namely that the righteousness and salvation of all men, whether Jews or Gentiles, comes not from the works of the law but from the sole mercy and grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, as Peter expressly testifies in chapter 15, verse 11, etc.; (2) the fulfilment also of the promises of the Old Testament, concerning the calling of the Gentiles and their adoption into the people of God through the Gospel, and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon all flesh in the last times; and concerning the Church, which is to be defended powerfully and wonderfully against all the fury of the Devil, of tyrants and of sophists, and to be preserved until the end of the world; (3) this book sketches for us the living face of the true Church and the manner of its reform, to which all churches ought to conform themselves; (4) on the efficacy of the ministry of the Word, which converts the impious and penetrates hearts, etc.; (5) from the examples of the faithful ministers of the Church, what the duty is of us who are called to the same office, in citing and explaining the Holy Scriptures and in the whole discharge of our calling. Of this book it can truly be said that this history is the teacher of life, etc.

units.la: DISTRIBUTIO SEU SYNOPSIS
units.tr: DISTRIBUTION, OR SYNOPSIS

units.la: προκεφαλαίωσις[?] Acta Apostolorum describuntur Omnium in genere, doctrina, facta, eve-ta[?]. De ipso rū Ministerio in plā-tanda Ecclesia Duorū adscititiorū Pauli & Barnabæ: hīc de iis quæ Inter Iudaeos nominatim Ierosolymis: de Apostolorum præparatione Actiua, in eligendo Mathia. cap.1. Passiua, in accipiendo Spiritus.cap.2. Actione: Vide pag: 147. Inter Gentes etiam:cap.8.9.10.11.12. Ab utroque Paulo & Barnabae simul gesta sunt.cap.13.14.15. ubi prima Pauli peregrinatio. A Paulo tantum: ipsius Peregrinatio Secunda c. 15 16. 17. & 18. Tertia. c.9 16. Quarta: c. 37. 28.
units.tr: Summary [προκεφαλαίωσις]. The Acts of the Apostles are described in general as to teaching, deeds and events. Concerning the ministry itself in spreading the Church, two men are added, Paul and Barnabas. Here is what was done among the Jews, especially at Jerusalem, and the apostles' preparation: active, in choosing Matthias, ch. 1; passive, in receiving the Spirit, ch. 2. The action: see p. 147. Among the Gentiles also, ch. 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. What was done by Paul and Barnabas together, ch. 13, 14, 15, where Paul's first journey is recorded. By Paul alone: his second journey, ch. 15, 16, 17 and 18; third, ch. 9, 16; fourth, ch. 27, 28.

units.la: Cap. i. Post transitionem generalem (v. 1.) repetuntur breviter ultimi duo loci Evangelicæ historiæ, quid scilicet Christus post resurrectionem discipulos suos docuerit per dies illos 40. & quibus testibus Ascensio illius ad cœlos fuerit peracta: usque ad v. 12. Inde subiungit quæ ad initium pertinent huius operis de cœtu Apostolico, quomodo concordes simul perdurarint in precibus & expectarint promissum Patris, usque ad v. 15. Postremo narratur cooptatio Matthiæ in numerum Apostolorum, ubi gravissima Petri describitur oratio.
units.tr: Ch. 1. After the general introduction (v. 1), the last two episodes of the Gospel history are briefly repeated: what Christ taught his disciples during those forty days, and by which witnesses his ascension into heaven was accomplished, to v. 12. He then adds what belongs to the beginning of this work concerning the apostolic company: how they persevered together in harmony in prayer and waited for the Father's promise, to v. 15. Lastly, the co-option of Matthias into the number of the apostles is related, where Peter's very weighty speech is described.

units.la: Cap. ii. Propositio: Apostoli secundum pro-missionem Christi, Spiritum S. acceperunt il-lustri miraculo, qui mox etiam sese magno cum fructu in doctrina illorum exercuit. Quatuor hic narrantur. Primum missio Spiritus sancti in Apostolos, usque ad v. 14. Deinde concio Petri in die Pentecostes habita ad Iudæos Hierosolymis congregatos, usque ad v. 37. Tertiò, effectum con-cionis illius, usque ad v. 42. Postremò, conversa-tio & status novæ illius Apostolicæ Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: Ch. 2. The proposition: the apostles received the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's promise, by a notable miracle, and soon he also showed himself in their teaching with great fruit. Four things are narrated here. First, the sending of the Holy Spirit upon the apostles, to v. 14. Second, Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost, delivered to the Jews gathered at Jerusalem, to v. 37. Third, the effect of that sermon, to v. 42. Last, the manner of life and state of that new apostolic church.

units.la: Hactenus fuit Apostolorum ad ministerium propagandi Evangelij præparatio, & primum Spiritus divini in ipsis loquentis experimentum: se-quitur
units.tr: So far, the preparation of the apostles for the ministry of propagating the Gospel, and the first experience of the divine Spirit speaking in them. What follows:

units.la: DE MINISTRIO APOSTOLORUM & Diaconorum apud Iudaeos tantum.
units.tr: ON THE MINISTRY OF THE APOSTLES AND DEACONS AMONG THE JEWS ONLY

units.la: Est hic A Elio circa Apostolatum quorundam Petri cap.3. Petri & Iohannis: cap.4. Omnium: cap.5. Diaconatum quomodo Instituitur cap.6. Administratur Stephano c.6. & 7. Philippo, deinceps etiam Gentibus praedicante: usque ad cap.10.
units.tr: This section concerns the apostleship of certain men: of Peter and John, ch. 3 and 4; of all, ch. 5. How the diaconate was instituted, ch. 6; administered by Stephen, ch. 6 and 7; and by Philip, who thereafter also preached to the Gentiles, to ch. 10.

units.la: Cap. iii. Lucas descripturus nouam accessionem Ecclesiae, quae facta est ex Petri concione noua, praemittit insigne illius miraculum, quo tanquam tubâ publicâ & voce praeconis conuocantur auditores, vt frequentes & attenti audiant docentem Petrum. Πρόλογος est: Christum verè Dei Filium esse, in cuius nomine salus, & peccatorum remissio omnibus piis speranda, & expectanda. Partes duae sunt: Prior complectitur ipsum miraculum, quo claudum ab annis 40. sanauit, magna cum totius populi admiratione: vsque ad v. 12. Posterior orationem S. Petri continet, in qua editi miraculi reddit rationem, & auditores ad fidem in Christum prouocat, differendo de morte, resurrectione, exaltatione, & meritis ipsius ex Scripturis.
units.tr: Ch. 3. Luke, about to describe the new accession to the Church made by Peter's new sermon, prefaces it with that notable miracle, by which the hearers are summoned as if by a public trumpet and a herald's voice, so that they come in crowds and listen attentively to Peter as he teaches. The prologue is that Christ is truly the Son of God, in whose name salvation and remission of sins are to be hoped for and expected by all the pious. There are two parts. The first comprises the miracle itself, by which he healed a lame man of forty years, to the great amazement of the whole people, to v. 12. The second contains St Peter's speech, in which he accounts for the miracle performed and calls the hearers to faith in Christ, discoursing from the Scriptures on his death, resurrection, exaltation and merits.

units.la: Post doctrinam sequuntur pericula. Petrus enim & Iohannes comprehenduntur, coniiciuntur in vincula, sistuntur in concilio, se defendunt, post longam deliberationem dimittuntur, & à suis magno gaudio excipiuntur.
units.tr: After the teaching come the dangers. Peter and John are seized, thrown into chains, brought before the council, defend themselves, are released after long deliberation, and are received by their own people with great joy.

units.la: Capite igitur iv. primum narrantur euenta concionis Petri superiore capite recitatæ, ac inter illa inprimis actio iudicialis contra Petrum & Iohannem à primoribus populi instituta, vsque ad v. 23. Deinde recitatur precatio credentium pro Apostolis, à v. 23. vsque ad v. 32. Postremo commemoratur credentium conuersatio & status.
units.tr: Therefore in ch. 4, first, the events of Peter's sermon recited in the previous chapter are narrated, and among them especially the judicial action against Peter and John instituted by the leaders of the people, to v. 23. Then the prayer of the believers for the apostles is recited, from v. 23 to v. 32. Lastly, the manner of life and state of the believers is recalled.

units.la: Hactenus omnia in primitiua & tenera illa Ecclesia fuerunt admodum laudabilia: nunc verò agitur de Zizaniis quibusdam in agro Domini repertis, hoc est de hypocritis qui synceris Christianis se adiungere volebant, sed infelici successu.
units.tr: Up to this point, everything in that primitive and tender church was highly praiseworthy. But now certain tares found in the Lord's field are treated of, that is, hypocrites who wished to join themselves to sincere Christians, but with an unhappy outcome.

units.la: Capitis v. Propositio est: quamuis diuersis miraculis Dominus suam Ecclesiam defendat, & regat: attamen & ab hypocritis domesticis, & ab externis persecutoribus subinde lacessitur. Tria narrantur. Primum quomodo Deus puniuerit hypocrisin Ananiæ & Sapphiræ, vsque ad v. 12. Deinde statum Ecclesiæ gloriosus & felix describitur, vsque ad v. 17. Postremo, quomodo primores populi seu magistratus Hierosolymitani nouam persecutionem susceperint aduersus Apostolos, qui ex carcere ab Angelo liberati, rursum ad iudicium producuntur, & ex Gamalielis consilio, prius cœsi, dimittuntur. Post contumeliam Christi nomine illatam, omni die in templo & circa domos docere infracto animo perrexerunt.
units.tr: Ch. 5. The proposition is: although the Lord defends and rules his Church by various miracles, it is nevertheless from time to time assailed both by hypocrites within and by external persecutors. Three things are narrated. First, how God punished the hypocrisy of Ananias and Sapphira, to v. 12. Then the glorious and happy state of the Church is described, to v. 17. Lastly, how the leaders of the people, that is, the magistrates of Jerusalem, undertook a new persecution against the apostles, who, freed from prison by an angel, are again brought to judgment and, by Gamaliel's counsel, are released after being beaten. After the insult inflicted in Christ's name, they went on, with unbroken spirit, to teach every day in the temple and in houses.

units.la: Persequitur Lucas alia domestica mala, quibus Satan conatus est primitiuam Ecclesiam pessundare. Nam à multis querela mouentur quasi inaequaliter bona publica dispensarentur ab Apostolis. Hinc murmur & querela, quae vt sint ad Ecclesiae utilitatem vtilitatem compositæ, iam docebitur. Eliguntur enim septem diaconi hac occasione, qui illa deinceps curent: Et quia inter hos est etiam Stephanus, illius historiam deinceps persequitur copiosius, quantus fuerit in asserenda Christi doctrina, quantus in disputationibus contra Libertinos, quæ res ad captiuitatem illius spectauit. Nam hostium insidiis & fraude capitur, & ad causam dicendam rapitur ad concilium, de cuius euentu capite septimo agitur.
units.tr: Luke pursues other domestic evils by which Satan tried to overthrow the primitive Church. For many were stirred to complaint, as if the public goods were distributed unequally by the apostles. Hence murmuring and complaint, which will now be taught how to be settled for the benefit of the Church. For seven deacons are chosen on this occasion, who would thereafter attend to those matters. And because Stephen is among these, Luke then follows his history more fully: how great he was in asserting Christ's doctrine, how great in disputations against the Libertines, which matter bore on his captivity. For he is taken by the snares and deceit of enemies, and is dragged before the council to answer the charge, the outcome of which is treated in ch. 7.

units.la: Capita v 1. duo narrantur. Primùm, quomodo Ecclesia Hierosolymitana constituerit Diaconos, id est dispensatores pecuniæ publicæ; usque ad v. 8.
units.tr: Two things are narrated in ch. 6. First, how the Jerusalem Church appointed deacons, that is, stewards of public money, to v. 8.

units.la: Alterum , de Stephani in asserenda veritate Zelo & acrimonia, & , quæ hanc excepit, persecutione, quam sustinuit à nonnullis Iudæorum doctoribus.
units.tr: Second, Stephen's zeal and vehemence in asserting the truth, and the persecution which followed, which he endured from some Jewish teachers.

units.la: Cap. v 11. recitatur oratio Stephani ad concilium Hierosolymitanum, vnà cum reliqua eius persecutione, videlicet lapidatione. Partes sunt duæ. Prior. Oratio Stephani, cuius πρόλογος[?] est: Stephanum non esse blasphemum in Deum, Legem, aut templum: sed de eo conqueri, quòd legem inspiritu & veritate non seruent, templo verò abutantur ad suam hypocrisin: usque ad v. 54. Posterior habet euenta orationis Stephani. Hostes, quem iustis rationibus, & Scripturæ testimoniis non poterant confutare, lapidibus vincunt & obruunt.
units.tr: Ch. 7 recites Stephen's speech to the Jerusalem council, together with his further persecution, namely stoning. There are two parts. The first is Stephen's speech, whose prologue is that Stephen was not blasphemous against God, the Law or the temple, but complained that they did not keep the Law in spirit and truth and abused the temple for their hypocrisy, to v. 54. The second contains the outcome of Stephen's speech. His enemies, whom they could not refute by sound reasons and testimonies of Scripture, they overcome and crush with stones.

units.la: HACTENUS Hierosolymis solum plantata est Ecclesia Christi, & confirmata variis miraculis. Nunc scripturus est Lucas.
units.tr: Thus far the Church of Christ had been planted only at Jerusalem, and confirmed by various miracles. Now Luke is about to write of

units.la: DE PROPAGATA EVANGELII doctrina ad vicinos populos.
units.tr: On the spread of the doctrine of the Gospel to neighbouring peoples.

units.la: Descripturus S. Lucas, quomodo ad vicinos populos sensim deriuata sit Evangelij cognitio, ostendit qui primi sint per Samariam doctores, qua occasione illuc eiecti, quo fructu docuerint, quo animo excepta doctrina, & quomodo Ecclesiæ sint confirmatæ & auctæ. Continet hæc pars historiam trium insignium doctorum, Philippi, Pauli & Petri. Producitur autem usque ad cap. 13. Initium narrationis huius sumitur à Saulis truculentia, & Stephani sepultura, ut constet qua occasione fideles per Samariam fuerint dispersi, nimirum propter persecutionem excitatam à Saule. Agitur hic de Mini-sterio Philippi Diaconi, eius studium in plantanda Ecclesia Samaritana, & conuertendo Reginæ Candaces Eunucho. cap. 8. Petri (præmissa narratione de cōuersione Saulis, cap. 9. usque ad v. 31.) eius Miracula duo, sanatio AE-neæ & suscitatio Tabithæ, cap. 9. Doctrina Proposita Genti-bus; Cornelio & familiæ eius. c.10. Defensa, contra iniquum Iudæo-rum iudiciū. c.11. Fortuna: Incarceratio & li-beratio ex carcere. cap. 12[?]
units.tr: St. Luke, describing how knowledge of the Gospel gradually spread to neighbouring peoples, shows who the first teachers in Samaria were, on what occasion they were driven there, with what fruit they taught, with what disposition the doctrine was received, and how the churches were strengthened and increased. This part contains the history of three outstanding teachers: Philip, Paul and Peter. It extends as far as chapter 13. The beginning of this narrative is taken from Saul's savagery and the burial of Stephen, so that it is clear on what occasion the faithful were scattered through Samaria, namely because of the persecution stirred up by Saul. Here the ministry of Philip the deacon is treated: his zeal in planting the Samaritan church, and his conversion of the eunuch of Queen Candace. Chapter 8. Peter: after the narrative of Saul's conversion (chapter 9, to verse 31) is premised, his two miracles, the healing of Aeneas and the raising of Tabitha, chapter 9. The doctrine proposed to the Gentiles: Cornelius and his household, chapter 10. Defended against the unjust judgement of the Jews, chapter 11. The misfortune: the imprisonment and the release from prison, chapter 12[?].

units.la: OCTAVO capite docet persecutionem illam priuatam, qua Stephanus occubuit, sen-sim vires acquisiuisse, adeò ut fideles Hierosolymis passim protraherentur ad examen. Hinc multi ex urbe tam hostili cesserunt; inter quos etiam Philippus Diaconus concessit ad Samaritanos, ubi magno eum fructu docuit & baptizauit. Partes sunt tres: 1. De occasione propagatæ doctrinæ, vsque ad v. 3.[?] 11 De Ecclesia Samariæ per Philippum instituta, per Iohannem vero & Petrum confirmata impositione manuum & dono Spiritus S. vbi etiam de Simone Mago represso: vsque ad v. 26. 111 De Æthiope Eunucho, ad fidem Christi per Philippum adducto.
units.tr: In chapter 8 he teaches that the private persecution in which Stephen perished gradually gained strength, so that the faithful were dragged before the court everywhere in Jerusalem. Hence many withdrew from that hostile city; among them Philip the deacon also withdrew to the Samaritans, where he taught and baptized with great fruit. There are three parts: (1) concerning the occasion of the spread of the doctrine, to verse 3[?]; (2) concerning the church in Samaria founded by Philip and confirmed by John and Peter through the laying on of hands and the gift of the Holy Spirit, where also Simon Magus is restrained, to verse 26; (3) concerning the Ethiopian eunuch, brought to faith in Christ by Philip.

units.la: Capite nono narrantur quatuor. 1. Conuersio Saulis & vocatio ad apostolatum: Propositio & summa: Saulus Damascum proficiscens (animo persequendi Christianos) in via convertitur, Ananiæ beneficio visum recipit, & ab eodem baptizatur, ac Iudæorum insidias per murum demissus euadit: vsque ad v. 31. 11 Ecclesiarum in Iudæa, Galilæa & Samaria statu. v. 31. 111. Sanatio Æneæ paralytici per Petrum in oppido Lydda, vsque ad v. 36. 1 v. Excitatio Tabithæ per Petrum in vrbe Ioppe.
units.tr: Four things are related in chapter 9. (1) The conversion of Saul and his call to the apostleship. The proposition and summary: Saul, setting out for Damascus (intending to persecute Christians), is converted on the road, receives his sight through the kindness of Ananias, is baptized by him, and escapes the ambush of the Jews by being lowered through the wall; to verse 31. (2) The state of the churches in Judea, Galilee and Samaria, verse 31. (3) The healing of Aeneas the paralytic by Peter in the town of Lydda, to verse 36. (4) The raising of Tabitha by Peter in the city of Joppa.

units.la: HACTENVS doctrina Euangelij propagata est in Samaria per Apostolos: in Æthiopia per Eunuchum reginæ Candaces. Iam Italicis quoque incipit innotescere. Nam Cornelius Romanus Centurio per Apostolum Petrum de Christo plenè edocetur, & cum suis domesticis, acceptis Spiritus S. donis baptizatur. Hinc iam Apostoli quoque discunt discrimina sublata esse circumcisorum & præputiatorum, puri & impuri: solamque in Christum fidem ad salutem esse necessariam.
units.tr: Hitherto the doctrine of the Gospel has been spread in Samaria by the Apostles, and in Ethiopia by the eunuch of Queen Candace. Now it begins to become known among the Italians also. For Cornelius, a Roman centurion, is fully instructed about Christ by the apostle Peter, and together with his household, having received the gifts of the Holy Spirit, is baptized. From this the Apostles too now learn that the distinction between the circumcised and the uncircumcised, the clean and the unclean, has been abolished, and that faith in Christ alone is necessary for salvation.

units.la: Capitis igitur decimi summa est: quomodo centurio quidā in vrbe Cæsarea, nomine Cornelius, vnà cum familia sua, ad fidem Iesu Christi per Petrum adductus sit: membra huius narrationis principalia duo sunt: primum enim exponuntur causa efficiente[?] sermonis Petri, per quem Cornelius ad fidem Iesu adductus fuit, vsque ad v. 34. Deinde ipse sermo Petri recitatur.
units.tr: The sum of chapter 10 is therefore this: how a certain centurion in the city of Caesarea, named Cornelius, together with his family, was brought to faith in Jesus Christ through Peter. The principal parts of this narrative are two. For first the efficient cause of Peter's sermon is set out, through which Cornelius was brought to faith in Jesus, to verse 34. Then Peter's own sermon is recited.

units.la: Capitis vndecimi Propositio est: Petrum rectè fecisse admittendo Gentes in Euangelij communionem sine circumcisione: quod non solum conuersione Cornelij probatur: sed etiam Antiochena Ecclesia quam Dominus constituit, quasi extra ordinem, & necessario dono prophetico ad futura mala publica præparauit. Membra duo sunt. Primum est, Apologia Petri apud fratres Hierosolymitanos de suo ingressu ad Cornelium, vsque ad v. 19. Secundum, de plantatione Ecclesiarum in Phoenicia & Cypro, & maxime Antiochiæ.
units.tr: The proposition of chapter 11 is that Peter acted rightly in admitting the Gentiles to fellowship in the Gospel without circumcision. This is proved not only by the conversion of Cornelius, but also by the church at Antioch, which the Lord established, as it were outside the ordinary course, and prepared by a necessary prophetic gift for the public evils to come. There are two parts. The first is Peter's apology before the brethren at Jerusalem concerning his entry to Cornelius, to verse 19. The second is concerning the planting of churches in Phoenicia and Cyprus, and especially at Antioch.

units.la: Hactenus audiuimus iucunda percepimus, quomodo vi-delicet Euangelium Christi longè lateque inter Iudæos & Gentes fuerit propagatum: nunc tri-stia sequuntur, quomodo Herodes persecutionem contra Christianos, & quidem aduersus Apostolos Christi mouerit: quæ tamen & ipsa in glo-riam Dei,& incrementum Ecclesiæ cessit.
units.tr: Hitherto we have heard pleasant things, namely how the Gospel of Christ has been spread far and wide among the Jews and the Gentiles. Now sad things follow, how Herod stirred up persecution against Christians, and indeed against the apostles of Christ; yet this too turned to the glory of God and the increase of the Church.
