units.tr: Then the bowls. They pour out the wrath of God, ch. 16. Harlot, whose damnation is shown to John: v. 1. Luxury of Babylon, v. 3. Stagnant ones: those who worship the beast are cast into the lake of fire, v. 20. Into Orcus: the dragon is cast, v. 3.

units.la: Sponsa pudica Dei. i. Ecclesia ostenditur. v. 9. Iura colenda nome ciuitatis, v. 3.
units.tr: Chaste bride of God: the Church is shown, v. 9. Laws to be observed: the name of the city, v. 3.

units.la: CHRONICA
units.tr: CHRONICLE

units.la: CHRONICA SYNOPSIS APOCALYPSEOS, VEL SECVNDUM argumentorum tempora.
units.tr: A SYNOPSIS CHRONICLE OF THE APOCALYPSE, OR ACCORDING TO THE TIMES OF ITS SUBJECTS.

units.la: Anno Christi.
units.tr: In the year of Christ.

units.la: Cap. 12. | Ecclesiam Iudæorum parturientem ob servat Draco. | 1
units.tr: Chap. 12. The dragon watches over the Church of the Jews as she is in labour. | 1

units.la: Eadem parit, fugit, latet, agente in terris Christo.
units.tr: She gives birth, flees and hides, while Christ is at work on earth.

units.la: Christum ascendentem in cælum Draco persequitur, pugnat, deiicitur. | 34
units.tr: The dragon pursues Christ ascending into heaven, fights, and is cast down. | 34

units.la: Ecclesiam Iudæorum persequitur deiectus Draco.
units.tr: The dragon, cast down, pursues the Church of the Jews.

units.la: Ecclesia Iudæorum in solitudinem recipitur annos tres & dimidium. | 67
units.tr: The Church of the Jews is received into the wilderness for three and a half years. | 67

units.la: Ea subversa, catholicam invadit Draco. | 70
units.tr: When that Church is overthrown, the dragon attacks the catholic Church. | 70

units.la: Cap. 20. Draco vincitur ad annos 1000.
units.tr: Chap. 20. The dragon is bound for 1000 years.

units.la: Cap. 13. Draco bestiam septicipitem & bicipitem excitat, quæ Ecclesiam catholicam & Prophetas eius infestant annos 1260. à passione Christi.
units.tr: Chap. 13. The dragon stirs up the seven-headed and two-headed beast, which harass the catholic Church and its prophets for 1260 years from the passion of Christ.

units.la: Cap. 11. Cap. 2. & 3. Ecclesia instituuntur sub finem Domitiani de rebus præsentibus: præmonentur de persecutione per Traianum futura decennium. | 79
units.tr: Chap. 11; Chap. 2 and 3. The churches are instituted under the end of Domitian, concerning present matters; they are forewarned of the persecution to come under Trajan within a decade. | 79

units.la: Cap. 6. & 7. Deus verbo & signis provocat mundum, obstignat bonos.
units.tr: Chap. 6 and 7. God challenges the world by word and signs, and seals the good.

units.la: Cap. 8. In creaturas omneis, homine excepto, statuit iræ suæ documenta.
units.tr: Chap. 8. He sets forth the evidences of his wrath upon all creatures, man excepted.

units.la: Cap. 10. Draco solvitur post annos 1000. furente contra Henricum III. Cæsarem Gregorio VII. Pontifice. | 1073
units.tr: Chap. 10. The dragon is loosed after 1000 years, raging against Henry III, Emperor, under Pope Gregory VII. | 1073

units.la: Cap. 9. | Draco malis vexat mundum annos 150. usque ad Gregorium IX. qui Decretales conscripsit, & atrocissimè infestauit Fridericum II. Cæsarem. | 1217
units.tr: Chap. 9. The dragon vexes the world with evils for 150 years, until Gregory IX, who compiled the Decretals and most savagely harassed Frederick II, Emperor. | 1217

units.la: Draco per utramque bestiam persequitur Ecclesiam, & morte afficit pios.
units.tr: The dragon, through both beasts, persecutes the Church and puts the godly to death.

units.la: Cap. II. & 13. | Draco prophetas extinguit post annum 1260. Bonifacio VIII. Pontifice, auctore Sexti Decretalium, qui excommunicavit Philippum Pulcrum Franc. regem. | 1295
units.tr: Chap. 11 and 13. The dragon extinguishes the prophets after the year 1260, under Pope Boniface VIII, author of the Sixth Book of Decretals, who excommunicated Philip the Fair, King of the French. | 1295

units.la: Cap. 12. | Primum Iubilaeum celebrat Bonifacius gratulatorium. | 1300
units.tr: Chap. 12. Boniface celebrates the first Jubilee with rejoicing. | 1300

units.la: Cap. 12. | Terræmotus maximus, quo plurima urbis ædificia diruta. | 1301
units.tr: Chap. 12. A very great earthquake, by which many buildings of the city were thrown down. | 1301

units.la: Cap. 12. | Prophetia aboletur triennium cum dimidio donec Bonifacio VIII. Benedictus II. successisset | 1305
units.tr: Chap. 12. Prophecy is abolished for three and a half years, until Benedict II succeeded Boniface VIII. | 1305

units.la: Cap. 12. | Prophetia reviviscit.
units.tr: Chap. 12. Prophecy revives.

units.la: Cap. 13. | Prophetiam draco & bestiae oppugnant.
units.tr: Chap. 13. The dragon and the beasts assail prophecy.

units.la: Cap. 14. | Christus Ecclesiam propugnat: verbo, opere.
units.tr: Chap. 14. Christ defends the Church by word and by work.

units.la: Cap. 15. | Minis armatis.
units.tr: Chap. 15. With armed threats.

units.la: Cap. 16. | Iudiciis singularibus.
units.tr: Chap. 16. By singular judgments.

units.la: Cap. 17. & 18. | Victoriam Christus Ecclesiae tribuit de meretrice.
units.tr: Chap. 17 and 18. Christ grants the Church victory over the harlot.

units.la: Cap. 19. | de bestiis duabus, septicipite & bicipite:
units.tr: Chap. 19. Concerning the two beasts, the seven-headed and the two-headed:

units.la: Cap. 20. | de dracone & morte.
units.tr: Chap. 20. Concerning the dragon and death.

units.la: Cap. 21. & 22. | Ecclesia plene glorificatur in coelis aeterna gloria in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Chap. 21 and 22. The Church is fully glorified in heaven, in eternal glory in Christ Jesus.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: THE END.
